Service credits are to be applied automatically as a deduction from the next invoice, but the MSA requires payment in full without any set-off or deduction except as agreed by Provider in writing. 04_sla cl.4.1 and 10_pricing cl.4.1 vs 01_msa cl.4.5

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW's independent credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of all liability limits. 04_sla cl.4.3 vs 02_sow cl.7.4; 03_dpa cl.11.1

Credits are calculated on the 'monthly Fee' (SOW/SLA) and on the 'recurring monthly charge' (Pricing), which are different amounts; the Glossary further redefines 'Fee' to include all T&M charges and expenses, changing the credit and liability-cap base again. 02_sow cl.7.4; 04_sla cl.4.2; 10_pricing cl.4.2; 15_glossary §2 ('Fee') vs 01_msa cl.1.4

Service-level commencement conflict: SOW says service levels start at the beginning of Phase 3 (about month 19), the Order Form says they apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form cl.3.3
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form cl.3.1 vs 04_sla cl.2.2

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees (approx. £148,800 at the MSA rate) and states this prevails over any Schedule; the SOW sets a £250,000 Provider cap; the DPA disapplies all limits for breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa cl.13.1/13.3 vs 02_sow cl.9.2 vs 03_dpa cl.11.1
Insurance conflict: professional indemnity cover of not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) versus not less than £2,000,000 (SOW) for the same engagement. 01_msa cl.16.1 vs 02_sow cl.9.4

Audit rights conflict: MSA 10.2 gives only a SOC 2 report and expressly removes any further right to audit, inspect or attend, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems, and the InfoSec Policy lets Customer nominate a penetration-test target. 01_msa cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa cl.9.1–9.2; 06_infosec cl.7.3

MSA 12.2 requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 denies any inspection right — internally self-cancelling. 01_msa cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict three ways: express written acceptance always required (MSA 6.1); deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days' silence (SOW 6.3); signed certificate required with silence expressly not acceptance and a 15 Business Day review window (Exhibit A 5.2–5.3). 01_msa cl.6.1; 02_sow cl.6.3; 13_exhibit_a cl.5.2–5.3
Broken cross-reference: MSA 6.2 refers to acceptance criteria in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SOW has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa cl.6.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflict: Exhibit A claims to be the sole source, the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead, and the MSA points to a non-existent SOW section. 13_exhibit_a cl.1.2 vs 02_sow cl.6.1 vs 01_msa cl.6.2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) versus 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). 01_msa cl.8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a cl.7.1

'Deliverable' defined inconsistently: only items identified as deliverables in a SOW (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary), which expands the IP assignment and acceptance obligations unpredictably. 01_msa cl.1.3 vs 15_glossary §2

'Services' defined inconsistently: services described in a SOW (MSA) versus SOW services plus SLA support services (Glossary), which changes the scope of the fee, the caps and the SLA regime. 01_msa cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary §2

'Agreement' defined inconsistently: MSA plus Schedules and Addenda (MSA 1.1, with 'Schedule' requiring express designation) versus MSA plus Order Form plus every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum (Glossary). On the MSA definition the Order Form is not part of the Agreement, yet it claims top precedence. 01_msa cl.1.1/1.6 vs 15_glossary §2; 05_order_form cl.2.2

Data-location conflict: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations, but the SOW places the whole delivery team (with system access) in Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa cl.4.1/Annex 2 vs 02_sow cl.3.4

InfoSec Policy permits Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region as unilaterally determined by Provider's CISO, with notice only 30 days after a new region enters service — contradicting the DPA's UK/EEA restriction and requirement for prior written authorisation. 06_infosec cl.2.1/2.3 vs 03_dpa cl.4.1–4.2

Approved subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, outside the UK/EEA and outside DPA Annex 2's approved locations, without any recorded transfer authorisation. 12_subprocessors §2 vs 03_dpa cl.4.1–4.3

Disaster recovery site conflict: BCDR uses Frankfurt, Germany, while DPA Annex 2 designates Dublin as the disaster recovery location and the subprocessor list shows backup/archival in Dublin. Frankfurt is not an approved processing location. 07_bcdr cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa Annex 2; 12_subprocessors §2

Two different documents purport to be 'Annex 2' to the DPA: the DPA's own Annex 2 (approved processing locations) and Schedule 9 (approved subprocessor list), which also gives Schedule 9 two different precedence ranks. 12_subprocessors preamble vs 03_dpa cl.4.3/Annex 2
Broken cross-reference: SLA 7.4 refers to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2, so the security escalation contacts do not exist. 04_sla cl.7.4

Broken cross-reference: Change Control 4.1 submits Change Requests to a 'Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. 08_change_control cl.4.1
Broken cross-reference: Exit Plan 5.3 refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit cl.5.3

Misdirected cross-reference: Change Control 7.2 charges impact-assessment preparation 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan'; the Exit Plan only sets a transition-assistance rate (£1,250/day) and no impact-assessment rate, and that rate conflicts with the rate card and Exhibit B rates. 08_change_control cl.7.2 vs 09_exit cl.3.2; 10_pricing cl.2.1; 14_exhibit_b §3

Subprocessor consent regimes are incompatible: DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; Schedule 9 permits addition/replacement on 30 days' notice with only an objection right, and immediate replacement with notice afterwards; the MSA allows subcontracting with no consent at all. 03_dpa cl.5.1 vs 12_subprocessors cl.3.1/3.4 vs 01_msa cl.9.3

Data retention/deletion obligations cannot all be satisfied: MSA requires 7-year retention of all records, data and materials after termination; DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan requires 90-day retention then deletion; InfoSec requires security logs to be deleted at 18 months; SLA and Change Control require retention only 'for the duration of the Agreement'. 01_msa cl.12.4; 03_dpa cl.8.2; 09_exit cl.2.3/5.2; 06_infosec cl.5.2; 04_sla cl.6.3; 08_change_control cl.9.3

The DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination, yet the Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services and complete parallel running and handover for up to six months after termination — the Services cannot be provided without the data. 03_dpa cl.8.2 vs 09_exit cl.2.1–2.2/4.1

Internal inconsistency in the Exit Plan: data is retained for only 90 calendar days after termination, but Annex 1 milestone 4 (parallel running complete) falls at T+90 Business Days (about 126 calendar days) and handover certification at the end of the six-month transition period. 09_exit cl.2.3 vs Annex 1 milestones 4–5
Data return format conflict: Exit Plan requires return in 'the format used by Provider's systems'; the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa cl.8.1

Governing law conflict and internal contradiction: MSA is governed by England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction; DPA 13.1 defers to the Agreement's law 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 imposes the law of the Republic of Ireland. 03_dpa cl.13.1–13.2 vs 01_msa cl.15.1–15.2

Change control conflicts with the MSA: the MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, whereas the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 08_change_control cl.4.2/4.3/6.1 vs 01_msa cl.2.4

Escalation paths conflict: SOW uses delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor; Change Control uses Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer (roles not defined and party unspecified). 02_sow cl.8.3 vs 08_change_control cl.8.1

Change Control 8.3 states escalation does not suspend 'the timetable in clause 3' (the impact assessment timetable), which is not the timetable at risk during an approval dispute — the deemed-approval clock in 4.2 continues to run, so escalation can result in a change being deemed approved while still disputed. 08_change_control cl.8.3 with cl.4.2

Recovery objectives are incompatible with the service levels: RTO is 8 hours from Invocation and clause 5.2 contemplates a further 12 hours' planned unavailability, whereas the SLA requires Priority 1 Resolution within 4 hours and 99.9% monthly availability (about 43 minutes' downtime). 07_bcdr cl.2.1/5.2 vs 04_sla cl.5.1/3.1

Exclusion conflict: BCDR excludes continuity-event and failback unavailability from the availability calculation, but the SLA's exclusive exclusions list (clause 9) and calculation method (clause 3.2/3.3) do not include them; under MSA precedence the SLA would control. 07_bcdr cl.5.3 vs 04_sla cl.3.2–3.3/9.1–9.3

BCDR clause 5.1 suspends all Service Level Schedule obligations for the duration of a Continuity Event with no cap, effectively disapplying the service levels and credits at Provider's discretion (Invocation is declared solely by Provider's Head of Operations). 07_bcdr cl.5.1 with cl.4.1

Response/Resolution targets are self-referential: SLA times are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the response target can never be missed and Provider controls the clock start. 04_sla cl.5.4 with cl.5.1–5.3

Root cause / incident reporting deadlines conflict for the same event: root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution (SLA) versus written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident (InfoSec). 04_sla cl.8.1 vs 06_infosec cl.6.2

Internal inconsistency in the InfoSec Policy: critical security patches must be applied within 14 days of release, but critical penetration-test findings may be remediated within 30 days. 06_infosec cl.9.1 vs cl.7.4

Key personnel location conflict: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow cl.3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b §1

Substitution conflict: the SOW forbids substituting named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement; Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in stated circumstances. 02_sow cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b cl.2.1/2.4

Rate conflicts for the same work: standard rate £1,450/day (Pricing), role rates in Exhibit B (some below and some equal), and transition/knowledge-transfer assistance at £1,250/day (Exit Plan), with no rule stating which prevails. 10_pricing cl.2.1/2.4; 14_exhibit_b §3; 09_exit cl.3.2/6.3

Exhibit B holds rates 'for the initial term' and Pricing fixes charges 'for the initial term', but the initial term is 12 months (Order Form) or 24 months (MSA) — the fixing period is indeterminate. 14_exhibit_b cl.3.2; 10_pricing cl.1.3 vs 01_msa cl.3.1; 05_order_form cl.1.2

Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, yet the InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data held on Provider systems and a payment tokenisation subprocessor is engaged; the DPA's data categories omit payment card data entirely. 11_acceptable_use cl.3.2 vs 06_infosec cl.1.2; 12_subprocessors §2; 03_dpa cl.3.3

Provider may unilaterally amend the Acceptable Use Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice with acceptance deemed by continued use, contradicting the MSA requirement that changes be agreed in writing and the Change Control Procedure. 11_acceptable_use cl.8.1–8.2 vs 01_msa cl.2.4; 08_change_control §1

Provider may disclose Customer content to law enforcement or regulators at its own discretion with no obligation to notify Customer at any time, conflicting with the processor's duty to process only on Customer's documented instructions and with the confidentiality obligations. 11_acceptable_use cl.6.1–6.2 vs 03_dpa cl.2.2; 01_msa cl.11.2

Confidentiality survives only 3 years after termination, which is inconsistent with the 7-year records retention obligation and with all Customer Personal Data being treated as Confidential Information for as long as it exists. 01_msa cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa cl.1.4

Suspension under the Acceptable Use Policy is immediate and without notice while charges continue to accrue, with no carve-out from the availability calculation or service credits in the SLA — Provider's own suspension would breach its availability commitment. 11_acceptable_use cl.5.1/5.4 vs 04_sla cl.3.1/§9

Double-charging ambiguity: it is unclear whether the SOW monthly Fee and the Pricing Schedule's recurring monthly platform charge are the same charge or cumulative, and whether the Order Form ACV covers both. 02_sow cl.5.1; 10_pricing cl.1.1; 05_order_form cl.1.4

Expense approval thresholds conflict: the SOW requires prior written approval for any expense outside the Fee, while Pricing requires approval only where monthly expenses exceed £500 (and states travel is recoverable at cost, whereas the SOW says the Fee covers travel). 02_sow cl.5.2/5.4 vs 10_pricing cl.3.1–3.2

'Subprocessor' defined inconsistently (third party processing Customer Personal Data vs any Personal Data), and 'Personal Data' is defined only by reference to UK GDPR while the DPA relies on a broader multi-territory 'Data Protection Law'. 03_dpa cl.1.5/1.2 vs 15_glossary §2

'Statement of Work' is used throughout as an operative concept but is never defined in any document; the Order Form and Exhibits are likewise not defined document types under the MSA. 01_msa §1; 15_glossary §2

The SOW records assumptions (accurate documentation, no more than three legacy interfaces requiring bespoke adapters) but provides no consequence, relief or link to the Change Control Procedure if they prove wrong. 02_sow cl.10.2–10.3

Mutual indemnity against regulatory fines is combined with a total disapplication of liability limits, creating an uncapped and probably unenforceable exposure inconsistent with the MSA liability architecture. 03_dpa cl.11.1–11.2 vs 01_msa cl.13.1

Change Control requires only Provider to acknowledge a Change Request, so Change Requests raised by Provider have no acknowledgement trigger and the clause 3.1 impact-assessment clock never starts. 08_change_control cl.2.1/2.3/3.1

Transition assistance is expressed as a Provider obligation but is conditioned on Customer approving Provider's effort estimate before assistance begins, allowing exit assistance to stall; no fallback applies where the estimate is disputed. 09_exit cl.3.1 vs cl.3.4

Exhibit B requires Key Personnel to be exclusively dedicated to the programme, while the Exit Plan requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect to run knowledge-transfer for an incoming supplier for up to six months after termination — no provision reconciles these or resources the post-termination period after the SOW ends. 14_exhibit_b cl.1.2 vs 09_exit cl.6.1

BCDR contemplates up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on failback but is silent on the SLA's requirement of 5 Business Days' notice for maintenance windows, so the failback outage is neither an agreed maintenance window nor an SLA exclusion. 07_bcdr cl.5.2 vs 04_sla cl.3.3/3.4/9.3

Glossary maintenance is vested unilaterally in Provider's Commercial Director while Glossary definitions are stated to override all other documents, allowing Provider to alter the contract's operative terms. 15_glossary cl.1.2/4.1

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule, but SOW 1 (Schedule 1) clause 1.2 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. The two cannot both operate. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Further circular/conflicting precedence: Order Form cl. 2.1-2.2 puts the Order Form above everything, while the Glossary (Schedule 10) cl. 1.2 says its definitions prevail over any other document, and the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules. Three documents each claim supremacy. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1-2.2; 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2; 01_msa.md cl. 14.2

"Business Day" defined three incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA); Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA); Monday-Friday including public holidays (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl. 1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 1.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

"Confidential Information" defined inconsistently: MSA requires written marking at disclosure; DPA cl. 1.4 and the Glossary extend it to unmarked and oral information. 01_msa.md cl. 11.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4 and 15_glossary.md s.2

"Deliverable" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. 01_msa.md cl. 1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

"Fee" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to amounts payable under clause 4; Glossary extends it to all amounts including T&M and expenses. This changes the base for service credits and the liability cap. 01_msa.md cl. 1.4 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

"Security Incident" defined three incompatible ways: DPA (unauthorised access/loss of personal data), SLA cl. 7.1 (confirmed unauthorised access causing loss or corruption of data only), and Glossary (any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of any Customer data or the platform). 03_dpa.md cl. 1.6 vs 04_sla.md cl. 7.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2
Monthly charge stated three different ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing Schedule). All are irreconcilable. 01_msa.md cl. 4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.1 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.1

Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals £12,800/month, matching the SOW figure but contradicting both the MSA (£12,400 = £148,800) and the Pricing Schedule (£13,100 = £157,200). 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4

Payment terms stated three different ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.6

Billing timing conflict: MSA cl. 4.3, SOW cl. 5.3 and Order Form cl. 1.5 require invoicing monthly in arrears, but Pricing cl. 1.2 requires the recurring charge to be invoiced monthly in advance. 10_pricing.md cl. 1.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3 / 02_sow.md cl. 5.3 / 05_order_form.md cl. 1.5

Fee indexation conflict: MSA cl. 4.4 allows a CPI-linked increase once every 12 months, but Pricing cl. 1.3 fixes the recurring charge with no indexation during the initial term. 01_msa.md cl. 4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3
Availability target conflict: SOW requires not less than 99.5% monthly availability; the SLA requires not less than 99.9%. 02_sow.md cl. 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1

Service credit cap stated three different ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SOW), maximum 10% of monthly Fee (SLA), maximum 5% of recurring monthly charge (Pricing). 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 4.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 4.2

Service credit trigger date conflict: SOW cl. 7.1 applies service levels only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme), whereas Order Form cl. 3.3 applies service levels from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl. 7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 3.3

Support coverage conflict: SLA cl. 2.2 limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00-18:00 on Business Days, but Order Form cl. 3.1 promises 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md cl. 2.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 3.1

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: MSA cl. 6.1 and Exhibit A cl. 5.3 require express written acceptance and state silence is not acceptance, but SOW cl. 6.3 deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days of silence. 01_msa.md cl. 6.1 / 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 6.3
Acceptance assessment period conflict: SOW cl. 6.3 gives Customer 5 Business Days; Exhibit A cl. 5.2 gives 15 Business Days. 02_sow.md cl. 6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflict: MSA cl. 6.2 points to "Schedule 1, Section 12" (the SOW has only 10 sections, so this reference does not exist), SOW cl. 6.1 says Deliverables are in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, and Exhibit A cl. 1.2 claims to be the sole source of acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl. 6.2; 02_sow.md cl. 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 1.2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: MSA cl. 8.2 gives 90 days from acceptance; Exhibit A cl. 7.1 gives 180 days from acceptance. 01_msa.md cl. 8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 7.1

Liability cap conflict: MSA cl. 13.1/13.3 impose a 12-months-Fees cap that applies notwithstanding any Schedule, but SOW cl. 9.2 sets a £250,000 cap. The two caps differ and both claim to govern. 01_msa.md cl. 13.1 and 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.2

DPA cl. 11.1 disapplies all limitations of liability for breach of the Addendum, contradicting MSA cl. 13.3 which states the cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of any Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.3
Professional indemnity insurance conflict: MSA requires not less than £5,000,000; SOW requires not less than £2,000,000. 01_msa.md cl. 16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.4

Governing law conflict: MSA cl. 15.1 selects England and Wales; DPA cl. 13.2 selects the Republic of Ireland for the Addendum, and DPA cl. 13.1 is internally self-contradictory (adopts the Agreement's law "save as provided in clause 13.2", which negates it entirely). 03_dpa.md cl. 13.1-13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 15.1

Audit rights conflict: MSA cl. 10.2 removes any right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises, but DPA cl. 9.1-9.2 grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. 01_msa.md cl. 10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 9.1-9.2

MSA cl. 12.2 makes Provider's record availability subject to cl. 10.2, which is a provision denying audit rights rather than granting access — the cross-reference is self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2

Subcontracting conflict: MSA cl. 9.3 allows subcontracting without Customer consent, but DPA cl. 5.1 requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, and Subprocessor List cl. 3.1 allows addition on 30 days' notice with no consent. Three incompatible regimes. 01_msa.md cl. 9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 5.1 vs 12_subprocessors.md cl. 3.1

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: 24 hours (DPA cl. 6.1), 72 hours (SLA cl. 7.3), 48 hours (InfoSec cl. 6.1). Provider cannot comply with a single standard. 03_dpa.md cl. 6.1 vs 04_sla.md cl. 7.3 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 6.1

Data location conflict: DPA cl. 4.1 restricts processing to the UK/EEA and Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, but InfoSec cl. 2.1 permits storage in any Provider region as unilaterally determined by Provider's CISO. 03_dpa.md cl. 4.1 and Annex 2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 2.1

Subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, and the BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt, Germany — neither is an approved processing location under DPA Annex 2, and Singapore is outside the UK/EEA restriction in DPA cl. 4.1. 12_subprocessors.md s.2 and 07_bcdr.md cl. 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.1 and Annex 2

Conflicting identification of DPA Annex 2: the DPA sets out its own Annex 2 as "Approved Processing Locations", but Schedule 9 states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA (a subprocessor list). Two different documents claim to be the same annex. 12_subprocessors.md preamble vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Delivery team location conflict: SOW cl. 3.4 states the whole delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, but Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London; the Bengaluru location also conflicts with the UK/EEA-only processing restriction if the team accesses Customer Personal Data. 02_sow.md cl. 3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1 and 03_dpa.md cl. 4.1

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW cl. 3.5 forbids substitution without Customer's prior written agreement, but Exhibit B cl. 2.1 allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and cl. 2.4 allows immediate substitution. 02_sow.md cl. 3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 2.1 and 2.4

Team size arithmetic error: cl. 3.1 requires not fewer than eleven FTE but the composition in cl. 3.2 (1 delivery lead + 2 architects + 6 engineers + 1 test lead + 1 business analyst) totals eleven only if all are counted — however the SOW elsewhere describes the roles inconsistently with Exhibit B, which lists a Test Lead and two architects as Key Personnel but no business analyst or engineers. 02_sow.md cl. 3.1-3.2 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1

Programme duration arithmetic error: cl. 2.1 states a 36-month programme, but the four phase durations in cl. 4.1-4.4 (3 + 15 + 12 + 6) total 36 months only without overlap while cl. 4.5 permits overlap; more importantly the 36-month programme cannot fit within the 24-month initial term of the MSA or the 12-month initial term in the Order Form. 02_sow.md cl. 2.1, 4.1-4.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.1 and 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2
Initial term conflict: MSA cl. 3.1 sets a 24-month initial term; Order Form cl. 1.2 sets a 12-month initial term. 01_msa.md cl. 3.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2

Commencement date conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but SOW cl. 2.2 states the programme commences on 1 March 2027 — before the Agreement exists and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 02_sow.md cl. 2.2 vs 01_msa.md preamble and 05_order_form.md cl. 1.3/7.3

Termination notice period conflict: MSA cl. 3.3 requires not less than 90 days' notice for convenience; SOW cl. 2.3 allows 30 days; Order Form cl. 6.2 requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal. 01_msa.md cl. 3.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 6.2

Data retention/deletion obligations are mutually impossible: MSA cl. 12.4 requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination; DPA cl. 8.2 requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan cl. 2.3 requires retention for 90 days then deletion; InfoSec cl. 5.2 requires security logs to be deleted at 18 months. 01_msa.md cl. 12.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 2.3/5.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 5.2

Deletion within 30 days of termination is incompatible with the Exit Plan's transition period running for 6 months after termination during which Provider must continue providing the Services and deliver all Customer data. 03_dpa.md cl. 8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 2.1-2.2 and 4.1(a)

Confidentiality survival period (3 years post-termination) is shorter than the 7-year record retention obligation and inconsistent with the DPA's treatment of personal data as Confidential Information indefinitely. 01_msa.md cl. 11.3 vs cl. 12.4 and 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4

Reference to a non-existent provision: Change Control cl. 4.1 refers to a "Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17". The MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.1
Reference to a non-existent provision: Exit Plan cl. 5.3 refers to the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14. The DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl. 5.3
Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA cl. 7.4 refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum. The DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl. 7.4

Reference to a non-existent exhibit: Pricing cl. 2.4 refers to role-specific rates "set out in Exhibit B", but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule; no Exhibit B to Schedule 7 exists. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.4

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist in the referenced document: Change Control cl. 7.2 says impact assessments are charged "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", but the Exit Plan cl. 3.2 sets only a transition assistance rate (£1,250/day) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl. 7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 3.2

Day rate conflict: standard rate card sets £1,450 per person per day and Exhibit B sets £1,450 for Delivery Lead/Architect, but the Exit Plan charges transition assistance (including further knowledge transfer sessions) at £1,250 per person per day with no stated basis for the discount. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.1 / 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.3 vs 09_exit.md cl. 3.2

Change approval conflict: MSA cl. 2.4 requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but Change Control cl. 4.2 deems changes approved by Customer silence, cl. 4.3 lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 unilaterally, and cl. 6.1 permits emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md cl. 2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Change Control cl. 4.3 permits unilateral Provider approval of changes up to £35,000, which exceeds any threshold reconcilable with the £12,400-£13,100 monthly fee and bypasses Customer's approval of charges entirely; it also conflicts with cl. 4.1's requirement for submission to a Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.3 vs cl. 4.1

Change Control cl. 5.3 exempts change-related charges from notice requirements for charge increases, conflicting with Pricing cl. 1.3 which fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no increase permitted. 08_change_control.md cl. 5.3 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3

Change Control cl. 8.3 says escalation does not suspend the timetable in clause 3, but clause 3 is the impact assessment timetable which precedes any disagreement; the intended reference is presumably to the approval deadlines in clause 4, and as drafted the deemed-approval clock in cl. 4.2 continues to run during escalation, so a disputed change can be deemed approved while under escalation. 08_change_control.md cl. 8.3 and 4.2

Service credits described as an automatic deduction with no claim required (SLA cl. 4.1, Pricing cl. 4.1) yet MSA cl. 4.5 requires payment in full without any set-off or deduction except as agreed by Provider in writing. 04_sla.md cl. 4.1 / 10_pricing.md cl. 4.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.5

SLA cl. 4.3 makes service credits Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, conflicting with SOW cl. 7.4's entitlement and with the general liability and termination remedies in the MSA; it also conflicts with DPA cl. 11.1's disapplication of limitations. 04_sla.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 and 01_msa.md cl. 13

SLA response/resolution measurement starts when Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the response target in cl. 5.1-5.3 circular and unenforceable (response time measured from Provider's own response). 04_sla.md cl. 5.4

Maintenance window notice (5 Business Days) is inconsistent with the SLA's own Business Day definition being Monday-Saturday US-holiday-based, and with the DPA/BCDR notice regimes; more materially cl. 3.3 excludes maintenance windows unilaterally set by Provider, with no cap on their duration or frequency, gutting the 99.9% commitment. 04_sla.md cl. 3.3-3.4

BCDR objectives are internally incompatible with the SLA: an 8-hour RTO plus up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on return to primary (cl. 5.2) far exceeds the maximum downtime consistent with 99.9% monthly availability (~43 minutes), and cl. 5.1/5.3 suspend and exclude these periods, rendering the availability commitment illusory. 07_bcdr.md cl. 2.1, 5.1-5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1

BCDR RPO of 24 hours (tolerated data loss) is incompatible with Exhibit A acceptance criteria requiring zero record loss and 0.01% reconciliation variance, and with treating data loss as a Priority 1 Security Incident. 07_bcdr.md cl. 2.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 3.4-3.5

Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident with a 4-hour Resolution target, which is inconsistent with the 24/48/72-hour notification windows elsewhere and with BCDR's 8-hour RTO. 04_sla.md cl. 7.2 and 5.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 6.1, 06_infosec.md cl. 6.1, 07_bcdr.md cl. 2.1

Payment card data conflict: InfoSec cl. 1.2 classifies payment card data as Restricted Data to be protected on the platform, and a Subprocessor (Ashcombe Payments Ltd) provides payment tokenisation, yet Acceptable Use cl. 3.2 prohibits Customer storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform. 06_infosec.md cl. 1.2 / 12_subprocessors.md s.2 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 3.2

Encryption at rest conflict: DPA cl. 7.2 requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, but InfoSec cl. 3.1 requires encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, leaving Internal Data (which includes personal data such as contact details and loyalty identifiers) unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl. 7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 3.1

Acceptable Use cl. 3.1 prohibits storing personal data of anyone under 16, yet the DPA identifies retail/loyalty customers as data subjects with no age screening mechanism and no corresponding Customer warranty or Provider filtering obligation. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 3.2

Unilateral amendment right conflicts with the change control regime and the MSA: Provider may amend the Acceptable Use Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice, and amend the InfoSec Policy, whereas MSA cl. 2.4 and the Change Control Procedure require bilateral agreement to changes, and Glossary cl. 3.3 incorporates documents as amended from time to time. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 8.1 / 06_infosec.md cl. 10.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 2.4 and 08_change_control.md

Suspension right conflicts with continuity of service obligations: Acceptable Use cl. 5.1 permits immediate suspension without notice with charges continuing, which is irreconcilable with the 99.9% availability commitment, the service credit regime, and the Exit Plan requirement to continue providing Services throughout transition. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 5.1 and 5.4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1 and 09_exit.md cl. 2.2

Lawful disclosure without notice (Acceptable Use cl. 6.1-6.2) conflicts with DPA cl. 2.2 (process only on Customer's documented instructions), cl. 6.3 (no public statement without approval) and the processor's duty to notify the controller of legally compelled disclosures. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 6.1-6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 2.2

Exit Annex 1 milestone timing is internally inconsistent with the transition period: milestone 4 (parallel running complete) at T+90 Business Days is approximately 4.5 calendar months, and milestones are measured in Business Days while the transition period is 6 calendar months from termination, yet cl. 2.1 starts the transition period at the date notice is given (not T), so the milestone baseline and the period baseline differ. 09_exit.md cl. 2.1 and Annex 1

Exit Plan cl. 4.1(a) requires data to be returned "in the format used by Provider's systems", contradicting DPA cl. 8.1 which requires return in a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl. 4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl. 8.1

Exit Plan cl. 3.4 requires Customer to approve the effort estimate before assistance begins, which allows Customer inaction to block the mandatory transition assistance and conflicts with cl. 1.2 (plan applies however the Agreement ends) and the fixed Annex 1 milestone dates. 09_exit.md cl. 3.4 vs cl. 1.2 and Annex 1

Exit Plan cl. 6.1 requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect for knowledge transfer during the transition period, but Exhibit B cl. 1.2 requires Key Personnel to be dedicated exclusively to the programme, and the SOW/Order Form terms may have ended — no mechanism reconciles post-termination availability of Key Personnel. 09_exit.md cl. 6.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 1.2

Exit Plan cl. 4.1(b) requires delivery of all Deliverables including source code, but MSA cl. 7.2 only assigns IP on payment in full and cl. 7.3 reserves Provider's pre-existing tools; no licence is granted to enable Customer to use delivered source code that embeds Provider tools. 09_exit.md cl. 4.1(b) vs 01_msa.md cl. 7.2-7.3

Remedy/cure period inconsistency: MSA cl. 3.4 gives 15 days to remedy a material breach, while Acceptable Use cl. 9.1 deems policy breach a material breach and cl. 5.1 permits immediate suspension without any cure period. 01_msa.md cl. 3.4 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 5.1 and 9.1

Renewal conflict: MSA cl. 3.2 renews the Agreement automatically for successive 12-month periods terminable only under cl. 3.3 (90 days), while Order Form cl. 6.1-6.2 has its own 12-month auto-renewal with 30 days' non-renewal notice; the two renewal clocks are not aligned given the different initial terms (24 vs 12 months). 01_msa.md cl. 3.1-3.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 6.1-6.2

Indemnity in DPA cl. 11.2 is drafted backwards/circularly: each party indemnifies the other against fines imposed on it as a result of the other's breach, which read literally makes the innocent party the indemnifier. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.2

DPA cl. 12.1 is headed "Precedence" but states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, giving no precedence rule — leaving DPA-versus-MSA conflicts (audit, subprocessing, liability, governing law, deletion) unresolved. 03_dpa.md cl. 12

InfoSec cl. 2.3 permits notification of a new processing region up to 30 days after it enters service, i.e. retrospective notification of a transfer, contradicting DPA cl. 4.2 which requires prior written authorisation before any transfer. 06_infosec.md cl. 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.2

InfoSec cl. 5.2 mandates deletion of security logs at 18 months, which conflicts with the 7-year record retention obligation in MSA cl. 12.4 and with DPA cl. 7.2's logging obligation for evidential purposes. 06_infosec.md cl. 5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

Patching and remediation timelines are inconsistent: InfoSec cl. 9.1 requires critical patches within 14 days but cl. 7.4 allows 30 days to remediate a critical penetration-test finding, for what may be the same vulnerability. 06_infosec.md cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

Vetting obligation conflict: InfoSec cl. 8.1 requires criminal-record checks on all personnel with access to Customer data, which is not achievable uniformly for the Bengaluru-based team and is not reflected in the SOW or Exhibit B commitments; Exhibit B cl. 5.1 simply cross-refers back to the Policy, creating no substantive standard. 06_infosec.md cl. 8.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 3.4 and 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 5.1

Governance/reporting forum mismatch: InfoSec cl. 6.3 refers to a "quarterly security review" that is not established anywhere; SOW cl. 8 provides only a monthly service review and a quarterly steering committee. 06_infosec.md cl. 6.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 8

Volume band pricing (£0.004 per transaction above 250,000/month) contradicts SOW cl. 5.2, which states the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and provides for no volume-based overage. 10_pricing.md cl. 5.1-5.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.2

Expense approval thresholds conflict: SOW cl. 5.4 requires prior written approval for any expense outside the Fee, whereas Pricing cl. 3.2 requires approval only where expenses exceed £500 in a month. 02_sow.md cl. 5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 3.2

Pricing cl. 6.1 requires invoices on the first Business Day of each month, but SLA cl. 6.1 allows the service report (which determines service credits to be itemised on the invoice under Pricing cl. 6.2) up to 10 Business Days after month end — credits cannot be applied to an invoice issued before they are known. 10_pricing.md cl. 6.1-6.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 6.1

Invoice query window of 10 Business Days conflicts with the payment terms allowing 30/45/60 days and with the concept of an "undisputed invoice" in MSA cl. 4.3, effectively cutting off dispute rights before payment is due. 10_pricing.md cl. 6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3

Purchase order requirement in Order Form cl. 5.3 (invoices returnable unpaid without a valid PO) conflicts with MSA cl. 4.3's obligation to pay undisputed invoices within 30 days and creates a payment condition not reflected in any other document. 05_order_form.md cl. 5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3

Signature/authority defect: the Order Form is dated 12 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027, yet it is stated to be made "under" the MSA; it is also signed by a Chief Procurement Officer while cl. 4.1 names the Head of Procurement as commercial contact, with no evidence of authority alignment. 05_order_form.md cl. 7.3 vs 01_msa.md preamble

Glossary defines "Agreement" to include the Order Form and Exhibits, whereas MSA cl. 1.1 defines it as the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only (omitting the Order Form and Exhibits), so documents such as the Order Form and Exhibits A and B may fall outside the MSA's own definition. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.1

MSA cl. 1.6 defines "Schedule" as a document executed by both parties and expressly stated to be a Schedule; several Schedules (InfoSec Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Subprocessor List, Glossary) are unilaterally maintained or amendable by Provider and contain no execution provision, so they may not qualify as Schedules at all. 01_msa.md cl. 1.6 vs 06_infosec.md, 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 8.1, 12_subprocessors.md cl. 1.2, 15_glossary.md cl. 4.1

Glossary defines "Services" to include the support services in the SLA, whereas MSA cl. 1.5 limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work; SOW 1 does not describe the SLA support services, creating a gap as to what Provider is actually obliged to perform and what the Fee covers. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.5

Glossary defines "Subprocessor" by reference to "Personal Data" generally while the DPA defines it by reference to Customer Personal Data processed on Customer's behalf — a materially wider category under the prevailing Glossary definition. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 1.5

Glossary cl. 4.2 makes any addition to the Glossary a change under the Change Control Procedure, but cl. 4.1 vests maintenance in Provider's Commercial Director and cl. 1.2 gives Glossary definitions overriding force — combined with Change Control cl. 4.2's deemed approval, Provider can unilaterally rewrite every defined term in the contract set. 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2, 4.1-4.2 with 08_change_control.md cl. 4.2

"Restricted Data" in the Glossary is defined by cross-reference to the InfoSec Policy, and the Glossary claims its definitions prevail over other documents — producing a circular definition that resolves to nothing while purportedly overriding the source. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 1.2

"Transition Period" is defined by reference to the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan cl. 2.1 uses the lower-case "transition period" and never defines a capitalised Transition Period, and its start date (notice date) and end date (6 months post-termination) produce a period of indeterminate length. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 2.1

"Personal Data" is defined by reference to the UK GDPR, whereas the DPA defines "Data Protection Law" as the law of all territories where Services are provided (including India and Singapore) — the two are inconsistent in scope. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 1.2

Provider both raises Change Requests and produces the impact assessment, and may charge for the impact assessment of a rejected request, creating a conflict of interest with no cap or Customer approval of that charge. 08_change_control.md cl. 2.1, 3.1, 7.2

Change Control cl. 4.4 states an approved change takes effect immediately on approval, which is inconsistent with cl. 5.1 (revised charges apply only from the next invoice) and with MSA cl. 2.4 requiring written agreement before implementation. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.4 vs cl. 5.1 and 01_msa.md cl. 2.4

SOW cl. 6.4 requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, but Exhibit A cl. 5.4 provides simply for remedy and resubmission with a fresh 15-day assessment and no resubmission deadline — two inconsistent resubmission regimes. 02_sow.md cl. 6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.4

MSA cl. 6.3 requires Provider to correct and resubmit rejected Deliverables at no additional charge, which conflicts with Change Control cl. 1.1 and the Pricing rate card permitting charges where acceptance criteria are changed, and with Exhibit A cl. 4.3 permitting acceptance with Minor Defects and a later remediation date. 01_msa.md cl. 6.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 1.1 and 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 4.3

Exhibit A cl. 3.2 makes acceptance of D2 dependent on "every requirement in the requirements register", but no requirements register is defined or incorporated anywhere in the contract set; similarly cl. 3.3 refers to an undefined "agreed functional test pack" and cl. 3.1 to undefined "in-scope systems". 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 3.1-3.3

Exhibit A Deliverables are assigned to phases but D4 and D5 sit in Phase 3 (migration), which under SOW cl. 7.1 is also when service levels begin — the platform is subject to 99.5%/99.9% availability while migration and parallel running are still in progress, an obligation Provider cannot realistically satisfy and which the documents do not reconcile. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md s.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.1

Exhibit A cl. 6.1 escalates acceptance disputes under "the governance provisions of the Statement of Work" (SOW cl. 8.3: delivery lead, account director, executive sponsor), which differs from the Change Control escalation path (Delivery Lead, Programme Director, Chief Information Officer) — inconsistent escalation ladders with undefined roles. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 8.3 and 08_change_control.md cl. 8.1

Exhibit B cl. 3.2 holds rates for "the initial term", which is ambiguous given the MSA's 24-month and the Order Form's 12-month initial terms and the SOW's 36-month programme. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 3.2

Exhibit B cl. 6.2 gives Provider 20 Business Days to replace an unsatisfactory individual, which is inconsistent with cl. 1.2's dedication requirement and cl. 2.3's two-week funded handover overlap, and leaves the SOW cl. 3.1 minimum team size unmet in the interim. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 6.2 vs cl. 1.2, 2.3 and 02_sow.md cl. 3.1

Subprocessor List cl. 3.4 allows immediate replacement of a Subprocessor with notice afterwards, contradicting DPA cl. 5.1 (prior specific written consent) and cl. 3.2's objection right, which becomes meaningless. 12_subprocessors.md cl. 3.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 5.1

Subprocessor List cl. 3.3 gives Customer only a right to terminate "the affected Services" on 30 days' notice where its data protection objection is overridden, which conflicts with the MSA's 90-day termination regime and provides no mechanism for partial termination of the Fee or the SOW. 12_subprocessors.md cl. 3.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.3

Subprocessor list is stated to be maintained and published by Provider on its trust portal (cl. 1.2) while simultaneously being a bilaterally executed Schedule and DPA Annex, so the contractual list and the published list can diverge with no rule as to which governs. 12_subprocessors.md cl. 1.2 vs preamble and 01_msa.md cl. 1.6

No document allocates responsibility for the DPA's Annex 1 processing duration ("the term of the Agreement") against the differing terms in the MSA (24 months), Order Form (12 months) and SOW (36 months), so the lawful processing period is indeterminate. 03_dpa.md Annex 1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.1, 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2, 02_sow.md cl. 2.1

BCDR cl. 5.1 suspends all SLA obligations for the duration of a Continuity Event, which Provider alone declares (cl. 4.1) and which has no defined maximum duration — Provider can unilaterally and indefinitely disapply the service levels and credits. 07_bcdr.md cl. 4.1 and 5.1

BCDR recovery environment in Frankfurt is described as warm-standby with scheduled replication consistent with a 24-hour RPO, which is inconsistent with the DPA Annex 2 designation of Dublin as the disaster recovery location. 07_bcdr.md cl. 3.1-3.3 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

BCDR cl. 6.2 requires 20 Business Days' notice of a test while cl. 7.2 obliges Customer to participate on reasonable request; no provision addresses the service level or availability consequences of a test, nor whether test downtime counts as an agreed maintenance window. 07_bcdr.md cl. 6.2, 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.3

Exit Plan cl. 9.2 requires a desk-based exit rehearsal "at least once in the term" without specifying which term or by when, and cl. 9.1 requires annual review of a plan that may only be triggered once — internally vague and unenforceable. 09_exit.md cl. 9.1-9.2

MSA cl. 2.3 obliges Provider to comply with Customer's reasonable instructions as to manner of performance, which conflicts with InfoSec cl. 2.1 (Provider's CISO determines data location) and Acceptable Use/InfoSec unilateral amendment rights vesting control in Provider. 01_msa.md cl. 2.3 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 2.1

SLA cl. 6.3 requires retention of service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, and Change Control cl. 9.3 and Exit cl. 4.1(e) similarly, all conflicting with the 7-year post-termination retention obligation in MSA cl. 12.4. 04_sla.md cl. 6.3 / 08_change_control.md cl. 9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

MSA cl. 13.1 caps liability by reference to Fees paid in the preceding 12 months, but with three conflicting monthly fee figures and a Glossary definition of Fee that includes expenses and T&M, the cap amount is indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl. 13.1 with 15_glossary.md s.2

SOW cl. 9.3 excludes indirect and consequential loss for both parties, but the DPA cl. 11.1 disapplies all limitations and exclusions for breaches of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, and MSA cl. 13.3 asserts the MSA cap overrides Schedules — three inconsistent exclusion regimes with no resolution. 02_sow.md cl. 9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.3

SOW cl. 10.3 assumes no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters but no document states the consequence if that assumption fails (no change control trigger, no relief event, no charge adjustment mechanism). 02_sow.md cl. 10.3

SOW cl. 10.1 requires Customer SMEs within 5 Business Days of request but no document provides Provider any relief from timetable, service levels or acceptance deadlines if Customer fails to comply. 02_sow.md cl. 10.1

No dispute resolution or escalation procedure exists at MSA level; the MSA goes straight to exclusive court jurisdiction while the SOW, Change Control and Exhibit A each specify different internal escalation ladders with no linkage to cl. 15.2. 01_msa.md cl. 15.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 8.3, 08_change_control.md cl. 8.1, 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 6.1

Acceptable Use Policy imposes obligations solely on Customer yet is a Schedule to an agreement whose precedence clauses subordinate Schedules to the MSA; MSA cl. 3.4's 15-day cure right and cl. 13 liability cap are inconsistent with cl. 9.2's unlimited cost recovery from Customer for policy breach. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 9.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.1

Order Form describes the Services as including "ongoing platform operation" as described in Statement of Work 1, but SOW 1 describes only a four-phase replatforming programme and does not describe ongoing platform operation. 05_order_form.md cl. 1.1 vs 02_sow.md s.4

Order Form cl. 3.2 names Provider's service desk as the named support contact, but Subprocessor List shows out-of-hours service desk is provided by Larkfield Support Partners (a third party), which is inconsistent with a 24x7 Provider-operated contact and with SLA cl. 2.1. 05_order_form.md cl. 3.2 vs 12_subprocessors.md s.2

MSA cl. 10.2 makes the annual SOC 2 Type II report the only assurance mechanism, yet InfoSec cl. 7.1-7.3 grants penetration test rights and nomination of a target system, and DPA cl. 9 grants audit rights — three inconsistent assurance regimes. 01_msa.md cl. 10.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 7.1-7.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 9
unmatched: "Deliverable" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. 01_msa.md cl. 1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2
Acceptance assessment period conflict: SOW cl. 6.3 gives Customer 5 Business Days; Exhibit A cl. 5.2 gives 15 Business Days. 02_sow.md cl. 6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.2

MSA cl. 12.2 makes Provider's record availability subject to cl. 10.2, which is a provision denying audit rights rather than granting access — the cross-reference is self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2

Confidentiality survival period (3 years post-termination) is shorter than the 7-year record retention obligation and inconsistent with the DPA's treatment of personal data as Confidential Information indefinitely. 01_msa.md cl. 11.3 vs cl. 12.4 and 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4

SLA response/resolution measurement starts when Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the response target in cl. 5.1-5.3 circular and unenforceable (response time measured from Provider's own response). 04_sla.md cl. 5.4

Unilateral amendment right conflicts with the change control regime and the MSA: Provider may amend the Acceptable Use Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice, and amend the InfoSec Policy, whereas MSA cl. 2.4 and the Change Control Procedure require bilateral agreement to changes, and Glossary cl. 3.3 incorporates documents as amended from time to time. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 8.1 / 06_infosec.md cl. 10.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 2.4 and 08_change_control.md

Lawful disclosure without notice (Acceptable Use cl. 6.1-6.2) conflicts with DPA cl. 2.2 (process only on Customer's documented instructions), cl. 6.3 (no public statement without approval) and the processor's duty to notify the controller of legally compelled disclosures. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 6.1-6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 2.2

Exit Plan cl. 3.4 requires Customer to approve the effort estimate before assistance begins, which allows Customer inaction to block the mandatory transition assistance and conflicts with cl. 1.2 (plan applies however the Agreement ends) and the fixed Annex 1 milestone dates. 09_exit.md cl. 3.4 vs cl. 1.2 and Annex 1

Exit Plan cl. 6.1 requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect for knowledge transfer during the transition period, but Exhibit B cl. 1.2 requires Key Personnel to be dedicated exclusively to the programme, and the SOW/Order Form terms may have ended — no mechanism reconciles post-termination availability of Key Personnel. 09_exit.md cl. 6.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 1.2

Indemnity in DPA cl. 11.2 is drafted backwards/circularly: each party indemnifies the other against fines imposed on it as a result of the other's breach, which read literally makes the innocent party the indemnifier. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.2

InfoSec cl. 2.3 permits notification of a new processing region up to 30 days after it enters service, i.e. retrospective notification of a transfer, contradicting DPA cl. 4.2 which requires prior written authorisation before any transfer. 06_infosec.md cl. 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.2

findings: Circular precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 (which is Schedule 1) says it prevails over the MSA. Neither conflict can be resolved. MSA cl. 14.2 vs SOW 1 cl. 1.2

Further circularity: the Order Form declares itself top of the precedence ladder and ranks Schedules third, but the Glossary (Schedule 10) states its definitions prevail over any definition in any other document, including the Order Form and MSA. Order Form cl. 2.1–2.2 vs Glossary cl. 1.2 vs MSA cl. 14.2

The precedence ladder gives no ranking as between Schedules, yet Schedules directly conflict with each other (e.g. SOW 1 vs SLA availability and credit caps; SLA vs BCDR; Pricing vs SOW). Schedule-versus-Schedule conflicts are unresolvable. Order Form cl. 2.1(c); MSA cl. 14

The Order Form claims highest precedence but is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined in the MSA (MSA 1.1 covers only the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda, and MSA 14 does not mention the Order Form). Exhibits A and B are likewise omitted from both the MSA definition and the precedence ladder. MSA cl. 1.1 and 14.1 vs Order Form cl. 2.1; Exhibits A and B

Three different monthly charges for the same services: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW 1 and the Order Form's £153,600 ACV) and £13,100 (Pricing Schedule). MSA cl. 4.1 vs SOW 1 cl. 5.1 vs Order Form cl. 1.4 vs Pricing cl. 1.1
Three different payment terms: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). MSA cl. 4.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 5.3 vs Order Form cl. 1.6

Billing basis conflict: the MSA, SOW and Order Form all require invoicing monthly in arrears, but the Pricing Schedule invoices the recurring charge monthly in advance (and on the first Business Day of the month). MSA cl. 4.3 / SOW 1 cl. 5.3 / Order Form cl. 1.5 vs Pricing cl. 1.2 and 6.1

Indexation conflict: the MSA permits an annual CPI-linked Fee increase on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or increase. MSA cl. 4.4 vs Pricing cl. 1.3

'Initial term' is ambiguous for the purposes of the price freeze and rate hold: the MSA initial term is 24 months, the Order Form initial term is 12 months. MSA cl. 3.1 vs Order Form cl. 1.2; Pricing cl. 1.3; Exhibit B cl. 3.2

Term conflict: MSA initial term 24 months, Order Form initial term 12 months, SOW programme 36 months. The 36-month programme cannot be completed within either contractual term. MSA cl. 3.1 vs Order Form cl. 1.2 vs SOW 1 cl. 2.1

Start-date conflict: the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — a month before the Agreement exists, and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027). MSA Effective Date; Order Form cl. 1.3 and 7.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 2.2

Inconsistent termination/non-renewal notice periods: MSA 90 days for convenience, SOW 30 days for convenience, Order Form 30 days' non-renewal notice. A 30-day SOW termination guts the 90-day MSA regime. MSA cl. 3.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 2.3 vs Order Form cl. 6.2

Three inconsistent definitions of 'Business Day': Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA); Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA); Monday–Friday *including* public holidays (Glossary). Every Business-Day-based deadline is indeterminate. MSA cl. 1.2 vs SLA cl. 1.1 vs Glossary, 'Business Day'
The SLA's Business Day definition (US federal holidays, Saturdays included) is internally incoherent for an England-and-Wales-governed contract with a UK customer and UK/India delivery. SLA cl. 1.1
Availability target conflict: 99.5% in the SOW versus 99.9% in the SLA for the same platform. SOW 1 cl. 7.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1
Service credit cap stated three different ways: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SOW), not more than 10% (SLA), not more than 5% (Pricing). SOW 1 cl. 7.4 vs SLA cl. 4.2 vs Pricing cl. 4.2
No formula or scale for calculating service credits appears anywhere — only caps — so the credit entitlement is unquantifiable. SOW 1 cl. 7.4; SLA cl. 4.1–4.2; Pricing cl. 4

Service levels start on two different dates: from the start of Phase 3 (approx. month 19) under the SOW, but from the Service Commencement Date under the Order Form. SOW 1 cl. 7.1 vs Order Form cl. 3.3
Because the Order Form initial term is 12 months, the SOW's service levels (Phase 3, month 19 onward) would never take effect within the term. Order Form cl. 1.2 vs SOW 1 cl. 4.1–4.3 and 7.1
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 for all priority levels; the SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl. 3.1 vs SLA cl. 2.2

Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) versus 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A); the MSA warrants conformity to acceptance criteria while Exhibit A warrants only against Material Defects. MSA cl. 8.2 vs Exhibit A cl. 7.1

'Deliverable' is defined inconsistently: an item identified as a deliverable in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary), which materially widens the IP assignment and warranty scope. MSA cl. 1.3 vs Glossary, 'Deliverable'

'Confidential Information' conflict: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at the time of disclosure; the Glossary protects all information whether marked or not, including oral disclosures. MSA cl. 11.1 vs Glossary, 'Confidential Information'

'Fee' conflict: the MSA limits Fee to amounts payable under clause 4, while the Glossary extends it to all amounts including time-and-materials charges and expenses — which changes both the liability cap and every 'percentage of the monthly Fee' credit calculation. MSA cl. 1.4 vs Glossary, 'Fee'

'Services' conflict: MSA limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work; the Glossary adds the support services in the SLA, changing the scope of warranties, service levels and the AUP. MSA cl. 1.5 vs Glossary, 'Services'
'Agreement' is defined differently: MSA (this MSA plus Schedules and Addenda) versus Glossary (MSA, Order Form and every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum). MSA cl. 1.1 vs Glossary, 'Agreement'

Data retention/deletion obligations cannot all be satisfied: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention for 90 days then deletion; the SLA and Change Control Procedure require retention only 'for the duration of the Agreement'; the InfoSec Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. MSA cl. 12.4 vs DPA cl. 8.2 vs Exit Plan cl. 2.3 and 5.2 vs SLA cl. 6.3 vs Change Control cl. 9.3 vs InfoSec cl. 5.2

Internal impossibility in the Exit Plan: Customer data must be retained only 90 days after termination and then deleted, yet the full data handover is due 'on or before the end of the transition period', which ends six months after termination (Annex 1 milestone 5). Exit Plan cl. 2.3, 4.1 and Annex 1 milestone 5

The Exit Plan requires delivery of 'the outstanding change log maintained under the Change Control Procedure' at the end of the transition period, but the change log need only be retained for the duration of the Agreement, which has already ended. Exit Plan cl. 4.1(e) vs Change Control cl. 9.3
Data return format conflict: 'in the format used by Provider's systems' (Exit Plan) versus 'a structured, commonly used format' (DPA). Exit Plan cl. 4.1(a) vs DPA cl. 8.1

The Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which is irreconcilable with the DPA's 30-day post-termination deletion obligation and with the Agreement having ended (no term, fee or governing service level is specified for that period beyond 'terms then in force'). Exit Plan cl. 2.1–2.2 vs DPA cl. 8.2 vs MSA cl. 3

Exit assistance is made conditional on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, with no deadlock mechanism — Provider's exit obligation can be stalled indefinitely, contradicting the statement that the Plan applies however the Agreement ends. Exit Plan cl. 3.4 vs cl. 1.2 and 3.1
RTO of 8 hours from Invocation is inconsistent with the SLA's Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours for the same total outage. BCDR cl. 2.1 vs SLA cl. 5.1

BCDR permits up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on return to primary and excludes Continuity Event downtime from availability, but the SLA's exclusions list (cl. 9) and availability calculation exclude only agreed maintenance windows, and 12 hours' downtime is irreconcilable with a 99.9% monthly target (≈43 minutes). BCDR cl. 5.1–5.3 vs SLA cl. 3.1–3.3 and 9
BCDR's planned return-to-primary unavailability cannot satisfy the SLA requirement of 5 Business Days' notice for any maintenance window. BCDR cl. 5.2 vs SLA cl. 3.4

Change control conflicts with the MSA: the MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, whereas the Procedure allows deemed approval on Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. MSA cl. 2.4 vs Change Control cl. 4.2, 4.3 and 6.1

Internal timing conflict: a Change Request is deemed approved after 10 Business Days of Customer silence, yet the escalation ladder allows three levels of 5 Business Days each (15 Business Days) and expressly does not suspend the timetable — a disputed change is approved while the dispute is still running. Change Control cl. 4.2, 8.1–8.3

Change-related charges are declared exempt from ordinary charge-increase notice requirements, conflicting with the Pricing Schedule's fixed, non-increasable recurring charge for the initial term. Change Control cl. 5.3 vs Pricing cl. 1.3

Personnel substitution conflict: the SOW forbids substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement; Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediately on resignation, dismissal or medical absence. SOW 1 cl. 3.5 vs Exhibit B cl. 2.1 and 2.4

Key Personnel are identified only by reference to a 'programme initiation document' that is not part of the contract set, so the individuals protected by the substitution controls are unidentifiable. Exhibit B cl. 1.1 vs SOW 1 cl. 3.5

Exhibit B's Key Personnel table lists only four roles and locates the second solution architect and test lead in Bengaluru, while requiring dedication; it also does not cover the engineers and business analyst committed in the SOW, and the removal/replacement period (20 Business Days) sits oddly with the 2-week handover overlap requirement. Exhibit B cl. 1, 2.3 and 6.2 vs SOW 1 cl. 3.1–3.2

Encryption conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, but the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, leaving 'Internal Data' (which includes personal data) unencrypted. DPA cl. 7.2 vs InfoSec cl. 1.3–1.4 and 3.1

The InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data and a payment tokenisation Subprocessor is listed, yet the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits Customer from storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform. InfoSec cl. 1.2 and Subprocessor List cl. 2 vs AUP cl. 3.2

The AUP prohibits storing personal data of anyone under 16, but the DPA scope covers 'Customer retail customers' and loyalty scheme identifiers with no age screening mechanism or reconciliation. AUP cl. 3.1 vs DPA cl. 3.2–3.3

The AUP states Provider does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility for it, which is inconsistent with its continuous monitoring, logging and processor duties elsewhere. AUP cl. 4.1 vs InfoSec cl. 5.1 and 5.3, DPA cl. 7

The AUP permits Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement with no obligation to notify Customer before or after, conflicting with the processor's duty to process only on documented instructions and to notify incidents/disclosures. AUP cl. 6.1–6.2 vs DPA cl. 2.2 and 6.1

Immediate suspension without notice for a policy breach conflicts with the MSA's requirement of a 15-day remedy period for material breach, given that the AUP deems its own breach a material breach of the Agreement. AUP cl. 5.1 and 9.1 vs MSA cl. 3.4

Provider may unilaterally amend the AUP on 30 days' notice, and the Glossary and Subprocessor List are maintained/published by Provider alone, contradicting the MSA definition of a Schedule as a document executed by both parties and the requirement for bilateral written change. AUP cl. 8.1, Glossary cl. 4.1, Subprocessor List cl. 1.2 vs MSA cl. 1.6 and 2.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination, but Provider is required to hold Customer records and data for 7 years — leaving 4 years of unprotected retained data. MSA cl. 11.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Sole-remedy conflict: the SLA makes service credits Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which is inconsistent with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of all limitations for data protection breaches affecting availability. SLA cl. 4.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 7.4 and DPA cl. 11.1

The Order Form scopes 'ongoing platform operation' but no Statement of Work describes an operational/hosting service — SOW 1 covers only the replatforming programme, so the operational service is unscoped. Order Form cl. 1.1 vs SOW 1

The Order Form permits invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, which cuts across the unconditional obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated period. Order Form cl. 5.3 vs MSA cl. 4.3
Provider must report transaction volumes 'in the monthly service report', but the prescribed contents of that report do not include volumes. Pricing cl. 5.3 vs SLA cl. 6.2

Invoice queries must be raised within 10 Business Days, yet payment obligations refer only to 'undisputed' invoices with no defined dispute procedure or effect of a dispute on the due date. Pricing cl. 6.3 vs MSA cl. 4.3

Resubmission timetable conflict: the SOW requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, while Exhibit A imposes no remedy deadline and adds a further 15 Business Day assessment period, so the review cycles do not align. SOW 1 cl. 6.4 vs Exhibit A cl. 5.4

Exhibit A acceptance criteria depend on undefined external artefacts (the 'requirements register', 'agreed functional test pack', 'architecture review') with no definition, owner or agreement mechanism. Exhibit A cl. 3.2–3.3
Only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, with no deputy or alternate, creating a single point of failure in the continuity plan. BCDR cl. 4.1

The SOW's assumptions (e.g. no more than three legacy interfaces requiring bespoke adapters; accurate Customer documentation) carry no stated consequence or relief mechanism if they prove untrue. SOW 1 cl. 10.2–10.3

The InfoSec Policy requires the incident register to be available at a 'quarterly security review', a forum not established by the governance provisions (which provide only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee). InfoSec cl. 6.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 8
Inconsistent remediation deadlines for critical security issues: 30 days for a critical penetration test finding versus 14 days for a critical security patch. InfoSec cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

'Data Protection Law' is defined by reference to the territories in which the Services are provided (which include India and Singapore per other documents), while the Glossary defines Personal Data solely by reference to the UK GDPR — leaving the applicable regime indeterminate. DPA cl. 1.2 vs Glossary, 'Personal Data'

The Glossary states any addition to it is a change under the Change Control Procedure, but that Procedure governs only changes to scope, timetable, charges or acceptance criteria and so cannot process a definitional change. Glossary cl. 4.2 vs Change Control cl. 1.1

'Subprocessor' is defined inconsistently: a third party engaged to process Customer Personal Data (DPA) versus a third party engaged to process Personal Data generally (Glossary). DPA cl. 1.5 vs Glossary, 'Subprocessor'

The mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is unworkable/circular against a controller-processor allocation and against the DPA's disapplication of all liability caps, with no cap, conduct-of-claims or apportionment provision. DPA cl. 11.2 with cl. 11.1

The Change Control Procedure lets Provider's own Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 'without reference to Customer', which contradicts the Change Control Board approval route in the same clause set and gives Provider unilateral power over Customer's charges. Change Control cl. 4.1 vs 4.3

The contract set is described as four documents but comprises fifteen, and several documents are cross-numbered inconsistently (e.g. Schedule 1 is the SOW while Exhibits A and B sit under it without being listed anywhere), so the composition of the Agreement is uncertain. Contract set as a whole; MSA cl. 1.1, 2.1; Order Form cl. 2.1
unmatched: No formula or scale for calculating service credits appears anywhere — only caps — so the credit entitlement is unquantifiable. SOW 1 cl. 7.4; SLA cl. 4.1–4.2; Pricing cl. 4

Credits are applied automatically to the 'next invoice' issued on the first Business Day of the month, but achieved availability is not reported until 10 Business Days after month end — the credit cannot be calculated before the invoice is issued. SLA cl. 4.1 and 6.1 vs Pricing cl. 6.1

Response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider itself 'acknowledges the Incident in its service management tool', making the response target self-referential and effectively impossible to breach. SLA cl. 5.4
MSA 12.2 requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights — the obligation is self-cancelling. MSA cl. 12.2 and 10.2
The DPA clause headed 'PRECEDENCE' contains no precedence rule at all, merely stating that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement. DPA cl. 12.1

The Pricing Schedule defers role-specific rates to 'Exhibit B', which is an Exhibit to the SOW rather than to the Pricing Schedule and is not incorporated into the precedence ladder. Pricing cl. 2.4 vs Exhibit B

'Services' conflict: MSA limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work; the Glossary adds the support services in the SLA, changing the scope of warranties, service levels and the AUP. MSA cl. 1.5 vs Glossary, 'Services'

The Exit Plan requires delivery of 'the outstanding change log maintained under the Change Control Procedure' at the end of the transition period, but the change log need only be retained for the duration of the Agreement, which has already ended. Exit Plan cl. 4.1(e) vs Change Control cl. 9.3
