findings: Circular / mutually inconsistent order of precedence: the MSA says it prevails over every Schedule and Addendum, the SOW (Schedule 1) says it prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says it prevails over everything, and the Glossary (Schedule 10) says its definitions prevail over any other document. No conflict can be resolved. MSA cl.14.2; SOW cl.1.2; Order Form cl.2.1–2.2; Glossary cl.1.2

The Order Form claims top precedence but is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined in the MSA (MSA 1.1 covers only Schedules and Addenda; the Order Form is neither, and is not 'expressly stated to be a Schedule' per MSA 1.6). The Glossary, by contrast, includes the Order Form in the Agreement. MSA cl.1.1, 1.6, 14; Order Form cl.2; Glossary, 'Agreement'

Order Form precedence list omits Exhibits (Exhibit A and Exhibit B), which the Glossary treats as part of the Agreement — no ranking exists for those documents. Order Form cl.2.1; Glossary, 'Agreement'

Monthly Fee stated four inconsistent ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing), and £12,800 implied by the Order Form's £153,600 ACV (MSA figure would give £148,800; Pricing figure £157,200). MSA cl.4.1; SOW cl.5.1; Pricing cl.1.1; Order Form cl.1.4
Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date. MSA cl.4.3; SOW cl.5.3; Order Form cl.1.6

Billing timing conflict: MSA, SOW and Order Form require invoicing monthly in arrears; the Pricing Schedule invoices the recurring charge monthly in advance on the first Business Day of the month. MSA cl.4.3; SOW cl.5.3; Order Form cl.1.5 vs Pricing cl.1.2, 6.1

Initial term conflict: 24 months (MSA) vs 12 months from Service Commencement Date (Order Form) vs a 36-month programme (SOW) that cannot be completed within either term. MSA cl.3.1; Order Form cl.1.2; SOW cl.2.1, cl.4

Start-date conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — i.e. before the Agreement exists and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027). MSA preamble; Order Form cl.1.3, 7.3; SOW cl.2.2

Termination/non-renewal notice conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice for convenience and for preventing renewal; SOW allows 30 days' notice; Order Form allows 30 days' non-renewal notice; Subprocessor Schedule allows 30 days' termination of affected Services. MSA cl.3.2–3.3; SOW cl.2.3; Order Form cl.6.2; Subprocessor List cl.3.3

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Mon–Fri excluding England & Wales public holidays; Mon–Sat excluding US federal holidays; Mon–Fri including public holidays. Every deadline expressed in Business Days is indeterminate. MSA cl.1.2; SLA cl.1.1; Glossary, 'Business Day'
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly (SOW) vs 99.9% monthly (SLA). SOW cl.7.2; SLA cl.3.1
Service credit cap conflict three ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SOW), maximum 10% (SLA), maximum 5% (Pricing). SOW cl.7.4; SLA cl.4.2; Pricing cl.4.2
Service credits are applied as a deduction from the next invoice, but the MSA prohibits any deduction, set-off or withholding from amounts due. MSA cl.4.5 vs SLA cl.4.1; Pricing cl.4.1
Service level start date conflict: SOW says service levels begin at the start of Phase 3 (month 19); Order Form says they apply from the Service Commencement Date. SOW cl.7.1 vs Order Form cl.3.3
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; SLA restricts P2/P3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl.3.1 vs SLA cl.2.2

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: MSA requires express written acceptance and says nothing is accepted without it; SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence; Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and allows 15 Business Days. MSA cl.6.1; SOW cl.6.3; Exhibit A cl.5.2–5.3
Reference to a non-existent provision: MSA points to acceptance criteria in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SOW has only 10 sections. MSA cl.6.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflicts three ways: MSA (Schedule 1 §12), SOW (phase plan maintained by the delivery lead), Exhibit A (which declares itself the sole source). MSA cl.6.2; SOW cl.6.1; Exhibit A cl.1.2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) vs 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). MSA cl.8.2 vs Exhibit A cl.7.1

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees (~£148,800–£157,200) and states the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule; the SOW sets a £250,000 cap; the DPA states no limitation in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. MSA cl.13.1, 13.3; SOW cl.9.2; DPA cl.11.1

Audit rights irreconcilable: MSA gives Customer no right whatsoever to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises/systems beyond the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. MSA cl.10.2 vs DPA cl.9.1–9.2

Self-defeating cross-reference: MSA requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights, so the obligation has no content. MSA cl.12.2 read with cl.10.2
Professional indemnity insurance limit conflict: not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) vs not less than £2,000,000 (SOW). MSA cl.16.1 vs SOW cl.9.4

Subcontracting/subprocessing conflict: MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent; DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without specific prior written consent; Subprocessor Schedule permits addition on 30 days' notice and immediate replacement with notice afterwards. MSA cl.9.3; DPA cl.5.1; Subprocessor List cl.3.1, 3.4

Data location obligations cannot all be met: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA, yet the delivery team (with system access) operates from Bengaluru, India, a listed subprocessor is in Singapore, and the InfoSec Policy lets Provider's CISO unilaterally choose any Provider region. DPA cl.4.1–4.2; SOW cl.3.4; Exhibit B cl.1 table; Subprocessor List cl.2; InfoSec cl.2.1

InfoSec allows notification of a new processing region up to 30 days after it enters service, directly contradicting the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation plus a transfer mechanism. InfoSec cl.2.3 vs DPA cl.4.2
Approved processing locations conflict: DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, but the BCDR Plan places the recovery environment in Frankfurt, Germany. DPA Annex 2 vs BCDR cl.3.1

Duplicate/incompatible 'Annex 2': the DPA contains its own Annex 2 (approved processing locations) while the Subprocessor Schedule declares itself to be Annex 2 to the DPA (a subprocessor list). Both cannot be Annex 2, and DPA cl.4.3 relies on Annex 2 being a locations list. DPA cl.4.3 and Annex 2 vs Subprocessor List header
Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. SLA cl.7.4

Reference to a non-existent clause: Change Control Procedure refers to the Change Control Board 'described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. Change Control cl.4.1
Reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. Exit Plan cl.5.3

'Security Incident' defined three incompatible ways: broad (any unauthorised access/loss/alteration of personal data) in the DPA; narrow (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption) in the SLA; broadest (any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform) in the Glossary. DPA cl.1.6; SLA cl.7.1; Glossary, 'Security Incident'
Security incident notification deadline conflicts three ways: 24 hours (DPA), 48 hours (InfoSec), 72 hours (SLA). DPA cl.6.1; InfoSec cl.6.1; SLA cl.7.3

Change control conflicts with the MSA: the MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure deems a change approved on Customer silence and lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 without reference to Customer. MSA cl.2.4 vs Change Control cl.4.2–4.3

Charge-increase provisions incompatible: MSA permits an annual CPI-linked increase on 60 days' notice; Pricing fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation; Change Control says change-related charges escape the ordinary notice requirements. MSA cl.4.4; Pricing cl.1.3; Change Control cl.5.3

Mis-directed cross-reference: Change Control charges for impact assessments 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan'; the Exit Plan contains only a transition-assistance rate (£1,250/day) and no impact-assessment rate. Change Control cl.7.2; Exit Plan cl.3.2

Day-rate conflicts: standard rate £1,450/day (Pricing) and role rates in Exhibit B (e.g. Test Lead/Engineer £1,100) versus a flat £1,250/day for transition assistance and further knowledge-transfer sessions. Pricing cl.2.1, 2.4; Exhibit B cl.3; Exit Plan cl.3.2, 6.3

Data retention/deletion obligations mutually impossible: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days and delivery of all data by the end of a 6-month transition period. MSA cl.12.4; DPA cl.8.2; Exit Plan cl.2.1, 2.3, 4.1(a), 5.2

Deletion within 30 days of termination is incompatible with the Exit Plan requirement that Provider continue to provide the Services for six months after the effective date of termination (Services cannot be run without the data). DPA cl.8.2 vs Exit Plan cl.2.1–2.2

Exit milestones exceed the data retention window: parallel running completes at T+90 Business Days (~4.5 months) and handover is certified at the end of the 6-month transition period, but Customer data is only retained for 90 calendar days after termination. Exit Plan Annex 1 (milestones 4–5) vs Exit Plan cl.2.3

Log/report retention conflicts with the MSA's 7-year retention obligation: security logs deleted after 18 months; service reports retained only for the duration of the Agreement; change log retained only for the duration of the Agreement. InfoSec cl.5.2; SLA cl.6.3; Change Control cl.9.3 vs MSA cl.12.4

Governing law contradiction inside one document and against the MSA: DPA cl.13.1 applies the law of the Agreement 'save as provided in 13.2', and 13.2 applies the law of the Republic of Ireland, while the MSA specifies England and Wales law with exclusive English jurisdiction. DPA cl.13.1–13.2 vs MSA cl.15.1–15.2

Clause headed 'Precedence' contains no precedence rule — it only states that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, leaving DPA/MSA conflicts (audit, liability, subprocessing, law) unresolved. DPA cl.12.1

'Confidential Information' defined three incompatible ways: only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure (MSA); all personal data whether or not marked (DPA); any information disclosed, marked or not, oral or written (Glossary). MSA cl.11.1; DPA cl.1.4; Glossary, 'Confidential Information'
Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination while data and records must be held for 7 years (MSA) — protected material outlives the duty of protection. MSA cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4

'Deliverable' defined inconsistently: only items identified as deliverables in a SOW (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary); and the deliverable set is fixed in Exhibit A but 'maintained by the delivery lead' in the SOW. MSA cl.1.3; Glossary, 'Deliverable'; Exhibit A cl.2; SOW cl.6.1

'Fee' defined inconsistently: amounts payable under MSA cl.4 versus all amounts including time-and-materials and expenses (Glossary). Because service credits are capped as a percentage of 'the monthly Fee', the cap is indeterminate. MSA cl.1.4; Glossary, 'Fee'; SOW cl.7.4; SLA cl.4.2; Pricing cl.4.2

'Services' defined inconsistently: services described in a SOW (MSA) versus SOW services plus SLA support services (Glossary), which changes the scope of the SLA, credits and exit obligations. MSA cl.1.5 vs Glossary, 'Services'

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW forbids substitution without Customer's prior written agreement; Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in stated circumstances. SOW cl.3.5 vs Exhibit B cl.2.1, 2.4
Team location conflict: SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. SOW cl.3.4 vs Exhibit B cl.1 table

SOW requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's (UK) working hours yet places the team in Bengaluru with no adjustment; combined with 24x7 P1 support this obligation set is unworkable as drafted. SOW cl.3.3–3.4; Order Form cl.3.1; SLA cl.2.1

Response-time measurement is circular/self-defeating: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute 'response' target measures nothing and Provider controls the clock start. SLA cl.5.4 read with cl.5.1–5.3

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, conflicting with the SOW credit regime and with the DPA's disapplication of limitations, and with the MSA's general liability regime. SLA cl.4.3 vs SOW cl.7.4; DPA cl.11.1; MSA cl.13

BCDR objectives are incompatible with the availability commitment: an 8-hour RTO plus up to 12 hours' planned unavailability on failback far exceeds the ~43 minutes of monthly downtime permitted by 99.9%; the BCDR Plan purports to exclude these periods but the SLA's exclusions list does not include Continuity Events. BCDR cl.2.1, 5.2–5.3 vs SLA cl.3.1, cl.9

Suspension for Acceptable Use breach creates unavailability that is not excluded from the availability calculation, so Provider would incur service credits for its own permitted suspension while charges continue to accrue. AUP cl.5.1, 5.4 vs SLA cl.3.1, cl.9

Provider may disclose Customer content (including personal data) to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer, contradicting the DPA duty to process only on Customer's documented instructions and to notify Customer of incidents/disclosures. AUP cl.6.1–6.2 vs DPA cl.2.2, cl.6

Unilateral amendment rights conflict with the requirement that changes be bilaterally agreed and processed through change control: Provider may amend the AUP on 30 days' notice, amend the InfoSec Policy, add regions, and change the subprocessor list. AUP cl.8.1; InfoSec cl.10.2, 2.3; Subprocessor List cl.3.1 vs MSA cl.2.4; Change Control cl.1.1

The Glossary's definitions override all other documents yet are maintained unilaterally by Provider's Commercial Director and changed via a change process that deems approval on Customer silence — Provider can rewrite the controlling definitions. Glossary cl.1.2, 4.1–4.2 read with Change Control cl.4.2

Payment card data is treated as a data category to be protected (Restricted Data) while the AUP prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform, and the DPA's data categories omit payment card data although a payment tokenisation subprocessor is engaged. InfoSec cl.1.2; AUP cl.3.2; DPA cl.3.3; Subprocessor List cl.2 (Ashcombe Payments)

AUP bars storing personal data of anyone under 16, while the DPA/Annex 1 contemplate processing loyalty and transaction data for all 'retail customers' with no age screening mechanism. AUP cl.3.1 vs DPA cl.3.2, Annex 1

Subprocessor transfer trigger is narrower than the DPA restriction: the Subprocessor Schedule only requires a transfer mechanism for subprocessors 'outside the United Kingdom', whereas the DPA restricts processing to the UK and EEA and requires prior authorisation for any transfer outside both. Subprocessor List cl.5.1 vs DPA cl.4.1–4.2

Governance meetings referenced but not established: InfoSec relies on a 'quarterly security review' that no document creates (the SOW establishes only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee). InfoSec cl.6.3 vs SOW cl.8

Escalation cross-reference appears wrong/ineffective: 'Escalation does not suspend the timetable in clause 3' (impact assessment) although escalation arises after assessment, at approval stage under clause 4 — leaving the deemed-approval clock running during escalation. Change Control cl.8.3 read with cl.4.2

Escalation paths are inconsistent: the SOW route is delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor, while the Change Control route is Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer; roles such as Programme Director and CIO are defined nowhere. SOW cl.8.3 vs Change Control cl.8.1

Deemed approval of a change 'takes effect immediately on approval' while revised charges only apply from the next invoice, and change-related charges are exempt from notice requirements — allowing implemented, unpriced changes. Change Control cl.4.4, 5.1, 5.3

Acceptance criteria internally inconsistent for the migration workstream: D4 requires zero record loss while D5 tolerates a 0.01% reconciliation variance, and the 24-hour RPO permits loss inconsistent with both. Exhibit A cl.3.4–3.5; BCDR cl.2.2

Phase 3 duration (12 months of migration and parallel running) is inconsistent with the Exit Plan's 90-Business-Day parallel-running milestone and with the 12-month Order Form term; the 36-month phase total also cannot fit the MSA's 24-month initial term without relying on automatic renewal that either party can defeat on 30–90 days' notice. SOW cl.4.1–4.4; Exit Plan Annex 1; Order Form cl.1.2; MSA cl.3.1–3.3

Transition assistance is conditioned on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider's pricing to block the exit obligations that the Plan says apply however the Agreement ends. Exit Plan cl.1.2, 3.1, 3.4

Data return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires data 'in the format used by Provider's systems' while the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format on request. Exit Plan cl.4.1(a) vs DPA cl.8.1
SOW assumption of no more than three legacy interfaces requiring bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or remedy if incorrect, and no link to the Change Control Procedure. SOW cl.10.3

Rate card review at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date conflicts with the statement that the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term (and with the ambiguity over whether the initial term is 12 or 24 months for the purpose of held rates). Pricing cl.1.3, 7.1; Exhibit B cl.3.2

Invoice query window of 10 Business Days sits awkwardly with the right to withhold payment only on 'undisputed' invoices and with the no-set-off clause, leaving no mechanism for disputed amounts after the window closes. Pricing cl.6.3; MSA cl.4.3, 4.5

MSA cl.2.3 vs InfoSec cl.2.1, 4.2

AUP cl.8.1; InfoSec cl.10.2, 2.3; Subprocessor List cl.3.1 vs MSA cl.2.4; Change Control cl.1.1

Glossary cl.1.2, 4.1–4.2 read with Change Control cl.4.2

The measurement base also differs ("Fee" vs "recurring monthly charge"). SOW cl.7.4; SLA cl.4.2; Pricing cl.4.2

Service levels start dates conflict: the Order Form applies service levels from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) while the SOW applies them only from the start of Phase 3 (i.e. after Phases 1 and 2, some 18 months later). Order Form cl.3.3; SOW cl.7.1

Support coverage conflict: the Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, while the SLA provides 24x7 only for Priority 1 and restricts P2/P3 to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl.3.1; SLA cl.2.1–2.2

Response and Resolution times are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the 15-minute "response" target circular/self-satisfying and leaves the clock start entirely within Provider's control. SLA cl.5.4 with cl.5.1

Liability cap conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees (approx. £148,800–£157,200) and states in 13.3 that this applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap for the same work. MSA cl.13.1 and 13.3; SOW cl.9.2

The DPA disapplies every limitation and exclusion of liability for any breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law, which directly contradicts the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. DPA cl.11.1 vs MSA cl.13.3
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: £5,000,000 (MSA) versus £2,000,000 (SOW). MSA cl.16.1; SOW cl.9.4

Governing law is self-contradictory and conflicts with the MSA: the DPA says it is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement (England and Wales) "save as provided in clause 13.2", and clause 13.2 then chooses the laws of the Republic of Ireland; the MSA also confers exclusive jurisdiction on the English courts. DPA cl.13.1–13.2 vs MSA cl.15.1–15.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA states that after delivery of the SOC 2 report the Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems, the InfoSec Policy lets Customer nominate a penetration-test target, and the Subprocessor Schedule requires quarterly review confirmations. MSA cl.10.2 vs DPA cl.9.1–9.2; InfoSec cl.7.3; Subprocessor Schedule §6

Self-defeating cross-reference: the record-access obligation is expressed as being "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 extinguishes the Customer's inspection rights, so clause 12.2 confers nothing. MSA cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Reference to a non-existent provision: acceptance criteria are said to be in "Schedule 1, Section 12", but the Statement of Work (Schedule 1) has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. MSA cl.6.2

Reference to a non-existent provision: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17" — the MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. Change Control cl.4.1
Reference to a non-existent provision: the Exit Plan points to "the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14" for personal data obligations; the DPA ends at clause 13. Exit Plan cl.5.3
Reference to a non-existent annex: security escalation contacts are said to be listed in "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum", but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. SLA cl.7.4

Annex conflict/duplication: the Subprocessor Schedule declares itself to be "Annex 2 to the Data Processing Addendum", but the DPA already contains an Annex 2 listing approved processing locations, and the DPA contains no annex for subprocessors. Subprocessor Schedule preamble vs DPA cl.4.3 and Annex 2

Reference to a rate that does not exist in the cited document: charges for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request are said to be "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", which contains only a transition-assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate; that rate also conflicts with the £1,450 standard rate card. Change Control cl.7.2 vs Exit Plan cl.3.2 and Pricing cl.2.1

Acceptance mechanism is irreconcilable across three documents: the MSA requires express written acceptance and no deemed acceptance; the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence; Exhibit A requires a signed acceptance certificate within 15 Business Days and states that silence is not acceptance. MSA cl.6.1; SOW cl.6.3; Exhibit A cl.5.2–5.3
Assessment periods conflict: 5 Business Days (SOW) versus 15 Business Days (Exhibit A) for the same review of the same Deliverable. SOW cl.6.3; Exhibit A cl.5.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflicts: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by Provider's delivery lead; Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria; the MSA points to a non-existent Schedule 1 Section 12. SOW cl.6.1; Exhibit A cl.1.2 and §2; MSA cl.6.2
Deliverable warranty periods conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) versus 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). MSA cl.8.2; Exhibit A cl.7.1

Change approval conflict: the MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. MSA cl.2.4 vs Change Control cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Escalation paths conflict: SOW governance escalates delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor, while the Change Control Procedure escalates Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer (roles not defined anywhere else). SOW cl.8.3; Change Control cl.8.1

Key personnel substitution conflict: the SOW forbids substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in stated circumstances. SOW cl.3.5; Exhibit B cl.2.1 and 2.4

Personnel location conflict: the SOW states the whole delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. SOW cl.3.4; Exhibit B §1

Data-location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with approved locations of London and Dublin only, yet the delivery team (with system access) is in Bengaluru, the InfoSec Policy allows storage/processing in any Provider region determined unilaterally by Provider's CISO, the BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt (not an approved location), and an approved Subprocessor is in Singapore. DPA cl.4.1–4.3 and Annex 2 vs SOW cl.3.4; InfoSec cl.2.1; BCDR cl.3.1; Subprocessor Schedule §2

The InfoSec Policy allows a new processing region to be notified up to 30 days after it enters service, which is incompatible with the DPA's requirement for prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism before any transfer. InfoSec cl.2.3 vs DPA cl.4.2

Subprocessor governance conflict: the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Subprocessor Schedule permits additions on 30 days' notice with only an objection right, and immediate replacement with notice afterwards. DPA cl.5.1 vs Subprocessor Schedule cl.3.1, 3.3, 3.4

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, which contradicts the DPA's specific-consent requirement for subprocessors handling personal data. MSA cl.9.3 vs DPA cl.5.1

Transfer clause covers only Subprocessors located outside the United Kingdom, ignoring the DPA's UK-and-EEA perimeter and the requirement for prior Customer authorisation, and provides no mechanism for the Singapore Subprocessor's authorisation. Subprocessor Schedule cl.5.1 vs DPA cl.4.1–4.2

Irreconcilable data retention/deletion obligations for the same data: 7 years' retention of all records, data and materials (MSA); deletion of all personal data within 30 days of termination (DPA); retention of all Customer data for 90 days after termination then deletion (Exit Plan); security logs deleted after 18 months (InfoSec); service reports retained only for the duration of the Agreement (SLA). MSA cl.12.4; DPA cl.8.2; Exit Plan cl.2.3 and 5.2; InfoSec cl.5.2; SLA cl.6.3

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination although records and data (including personal data deemed confidential) must be retained for 7 years, leaving retained data unprotected. MSA cl.11.3 vs MSA cl.12.4 and DPA cl.1.4

Data return format conflict: the DPA requires return in a structured, commonly used format, while the Exit Plan requires return only "in the format used by Provider's systems". DPA cl.8.1; Exit Plan cl.4.1(a)

The Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for up to six months after the effective date of termination and to retain data for 90 days, which cannot be reconciled with the DPA's obligation to delete all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination. Exit Plan cl.2.1–2.3 vs DPA cl.8.2

Encryption-at-rest conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy mandates encryption at rest only for Restricted Data (Internal Data, which would include most contact and transaction data, is excluded). DPA cl.7.2 vs InfoSec cl.3.1 and 1.3

Availability-exclusion conflict: the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows (plus clause 9 exclusions) from the availability calculation, while the BCDR Plan purports to exclude Continuity Event downtime and up to 12 hours' failback downtime and to suspend all SLA obligations during a Continuity Event. SLA cl.3.2–3.3 and §9 vs BCDR cl.5.1–5.3

BCDR objectives are internally inconsistent with the recovery approach: an 8-hour RTO from a warm-standby site sits alongside a 24-hour RPO (up to a day of data loss) and a permitted 12-hour planned outage to fail back — a period that alone exceeds the entire annual downtime allowance under a 99.9% availability target. BCDR cl.2.1–2.2 and 5.2 vs SLA cl.3.1

Single point of failure with no alternate: only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, with no deputy or escalation if that person is unavailable, and the same person owns the Plan. BCDR cl.4.1 and 9.1

Expenses conflict: the SOW states the Fee covers all travel and that any expense outside the Fee needs prior written approval, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel, subsistence and mileage recoverable at cost and requires approval only where the monthly total exceeds £500. SOW cl.5.2 and 5.4 vs Pricing cl.3.1–3.3

Rate inconsistency: transition assistance is charged at £1,250 per person per day while the standard rate card is £1,450 per person per day and Exhibit B role rates range £950–£1,450, with no statement of which prevails for exit work. Exit Plan cl.3.2 vs Pricing cl.2.1 and Exhibit B §3

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend a contract Schedule unilaterally on 30 days' notice with acceptance deemed by continued use, contradicting the MSA's requirement for bilateral written change and the Change Control Procedure. AUP cl.8.1–8.2 vs MSA cl.2.4; Change Control §1 and §4

The AUP permits Provider to disclose Customer content to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer before or after, which conflicts with the processor's duty to process only on documented instructions and to notify the controller of incidents/disclosures affecting personal data. AUP cl.6.1–6.2 vs DPA cl.2.2, 2.3, 6.1

Payment card data inconsistency: the AUP prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform, yet the InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as a category of Restricted Data held by Provider and an approved Subprocessor provides payment tokenisation. AUP cl.3.2 vs InfoSec cl.1.2; Subprocessor Schedule §2

Suspension under the AUP causes unavailability and continuing charges, but suspension is not among the SLA's availability exclusions, so Provider would breach the availability target through its own permitted suspension. AUP cl.5.1 and 5.4 vs SLA cl.3.1 and §9

A clause headed "Precedence" contains no precedence rule at all, leaving the DPA's rank in the hierarchy unstated while other documents (MSA 14.2, Order Form 2.1(d)) subordinate it and DPA 11.1 purports to override the MSA. DPA cl.12.1

The Order Form's precedence list omits Exhibits (A and B) and the Order Form itself, though ranked first, is not part of the "Agreement" as defined in the MSA, so documents such as Exhibit A's acceptance criteria have no defined rank. Order Form cl.2.1 vs MSA cl.1.1; Exhibits A and B

The Glossary is stated to be maintained unilaterally by Provider's Commercial Director while also providing that any addition is a change requiring the Change Control Procedure — and its definitions are said to override all other documents, allowing one party to rewrite the contract's operative terms. Glossary cl.1.2, 4.1–4.2

"Subprocessor" is defined by reference to processing of "Customer Personal Data" in the DPA but to any "Personal Data" in the Glossary, creating differing scopes for the consent and flow-down obligations. DPA cl.1.5; Glossary §2

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failure, which conflicts with the SOW's separate 25% credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of all liability limitations, and is inconsistent with treating an availability failure as a material breach. SLA cl.4.3 vs SOW cl.7.4; DPA cl.11.1

Reporting content mismatch: the Pricing Schedule requires transaction volumes to be reported in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents do not include volumes. Pricing cl.5.3 vs SLA cl.6.2

Exit milestone timings are expressed in Business Days (T+15 to T+90) while the transition period is expressed in calendar months, and milestone 4 (parallel running complete at T+90 Business Days, c. 4.5 calendar months) leaves handover certification and deletion timing ambiguous against the 6-month period and the 90-day retention window. Exit Plan Annex 1 vs Exit Plan cl.2.1 and 2.3

Exit assistance is made conditional on Customer approving Provider's effort estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider to stall mandatory exit obligations by pricing, and applies even where termination is for Provider's breach. Exit Plan cl.3.4 with cl.1.2 and 3.1

Phase durations (3 + 15 + 12 + 6 = 36 months) run to March 2030 from a 1 March 2027 start, extending well beyond the MSA's 24-month initial term and the Order Form's 12-month initial term, with no linkage of renewal to programme completion. SOW §4 vs MSA cl.3.1; Order Form cl.1.2
Stated assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or change mechanism if exceeded, leaving scope and price open. SOW cl.10.3

Exhibit A permits acceptance with Minor Defects outstanding subject only to a Provider-committed remediation date, which conflicts with the MSA warranty that Deliverables will conform to the applicable acceptance criteria and with MSA 6.3's correction-before-acceptance model. Exhibit A cl.4.3 vs MSA cl.6.3 and 8.2

Purchase-order gate conflicts with payment obligations: invoices without a valid PO number may be returned unpaid, but the payment clauses require payment of undisputed invoices within a fixed period from receipt and the Pricing Schedule's invoice-content list does not require a PO number. Order Form cl.5.1–5.3 vs MSA cl.4.3; Pricing cl.6.2

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is likely unenforceable/inoperable as drafted (fines are imposed on the party at fault) and sits inconsistently with the unlimited-liability rule in the same clause and the MSA cap. DPA cl.11.2 with cl.11.1 and MSA cl.13.1

findings: Circular / mutually exclusive precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, but SOW 1 (Schedule 1) says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says it prevails over every other document, and the Glossary (Schedule 10) says its definitions prevail over any other document. No conflict can be resolved. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2; 15_glossary.md cl.1.2

Order Form ranks '(b) the Master Services Agreement' above '(c) any Schedule', which directly contradicts SOW 1.2 and Glossary 1.2; the Order Form's own 2.2 also duplicates/overrides its 2.1 ranking table. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2

The Order Form claims to be the highest-ranking contract document, yet the MSA definition of 'Agreement' (this MSA plus each Schedule and Addendum) does not include an Order Form, so on the MSA's own terms the Order Form is not part of the Agreement. 01_msa.md cl.1.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.2.1

Exhibits A and B are stated to be Exhibits to the Statement of Work, but the MSA's 'Agreement' definition and precedence clause cover only Schedules and Addenda, leaving the Exhibits outside the contractual hierarchy. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 14.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md heading; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md heading

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Mon–Fri excluding England & Wales public holidays; Mon–Saturday excluding US federal holidays; Mon–Fri *including* public holidays. Every deadline expressed in Business Days is indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

'Confidential Information' defined two ways: only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure (MSA) versus any information whether or not marked and whether oral or written (Glossary); the DPA adds a third rule deeming all Customer Personal Data confidential regardless of marking. 01_msa.md cl.11.1; 15_glossary.md §2; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

'Deliverable' defined two ways: only items identified as deliverables in a SOW (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary), which changes the scope of the IP assignment, acceptance and warranty regimes. 01_msa.md cl.1.3; 15_glossary.md §2

'Fee' defined two ways: amounts payable under MSA clause 4 versus all amounts payable including T&M charges and expenses (Glossary). Service-credit caps and the liability cap are expressed as percentages/multiples of 'Fees', so the exposure figures are indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl.1.4; 15_glossary.md §2; 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2; 01_msa.md cl.13.1

'Security Incident' defined three incompatible ways: broad unauthorised access/alteration/loss of personal data (DPA); narrow 'confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption' (SLA); and any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform (Glossary). 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1; 15_glossary.md §2
'Services' defined two ways: the services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus SOW services plus the support services in the SLA Schedule (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl.1.5; 15_glossary.md §2
'Subprocessor' scoped to processors of Customer Personal Data in the DPA but to processors of any Personal Data in the Glossary. 03_dpa.md cl.1.5; 15_glossary.md §2
'Agreement' defined two ways: MSA plus Schedules and Addenda (MSA) versus MSA, Order Form and every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl.1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Four different monthly charges for the same Services: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing Schedule), and an Annual Contract Value of £153,600 (= £12,800 × 12) in the Order Form. £13,100 × 12 = £157,200 and £12,400 × 12 = £148,800, so no figure reconciles. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 10_pricing.md cl.1.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Three different payment terms: 30 days from receipt of invoice (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Billing direction conflict: MSA, SOW and Order Form all require invoicing monthly in arrears; the Pricing Schedule states the recurring charge is invoiced monthly in advance and issued on the first Business Day of each month. 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.5 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.2, 6.1

Price-increase conflict: MSA permits a CPI-linked increase once every 12 months on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing Schedule states the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or any other increase; the Pricing Schedule also requires an annual rate-card review at each anniversary, which cannot occur within a 24-month fixed period. 01_msa.md cl.4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.3, 7.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.3.2

Three different initial terms/durations: 24-month MSA initial term, 36-month SOW programme, and a 12-month Order Form initial term. The 36-month programme cannot be completed within either the 24-month or the 12-month term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start-date conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme is stated to commence on 1 March 2027 — a month before the Agreement exists. 02_sow.md cl.2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3

The Order Form is dated 12 March 2027, after the SOW's stated programme commencement of 1 March 2027, so performance is contracted to have begun before signature. 05_order_form.md cl.7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.2

Termination-notice conflict: 90 days' notice for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form; the MSA renewal clause permits termination only 'in accordance with clause 3.3' (90 days), so the Order Form's 30-day non-renewal right is inoperable. 01_msa.md cl.3.2–3.3; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.1–6.2
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly availability in the SOW versus 99.9% in the SLA Schedule for the same platform. 02_sow.md cl.7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1

Three different service-credit caps for the same failure: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SOW), maximum 10% of the monthly Fee (SLA), and maximum 5% of the recurring monthly charge (Pricing). 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2; 10_pricing.md cl.4.2

Service-level start date conflict: SOW says service levels begin at the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme), Order Form says they apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support-hours conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, while the SLA provides 24x7 only for Priority 1 and restricts Priority 2/3 to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.1–2.2

Set-off prohibition conflicts with the automatic service-credit mechanism: the MSA bars any deduction or set-off from amounts due, while the SLA and Pricing Schedules require credits to be applied automatically as a deduction from the next invoice. 01_msa.md cl.4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 10_pricing.md cl.4.1

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and states the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap on Provider's liability under the SOW. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.2

The DPA disapplies every limitation and exclusion of liability in the Agreement for any breach of the Addendum or of Data Protection Law, contradicting the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum and the SOW's exclusion of indirect loss. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.3

The SLA states service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW's separate credit regime and with the general damages/liability provisions (and with the DPA's unlimited-liability rule where the outage involves personal data). 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13.1; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limit conflict: not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) versus not less than £2,000,000 (SOW). 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Audit rights conflict: MSA states that provision of the SOC 2 report leaves Customer with 'no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems', while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2

Internal circularity: MSA clause 12.2 requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 confers no access rights and expressly removes them, so clause 12.2 has no operative content. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Acceptance regimes are mutually exclusive: MSA requires express written acceptance and prohibits deemed acceptance; the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence; Exhibit A requires a signed acceptance certificate within a 15 Business Day window and states silence is not acceptance. 01_msa.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.2–5.3

Dangling cross-reference: MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria 'set out in Schedule 1, Section 12', but Statement of Work 1 has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl.6.2 vs 02_sow.md

Source of Deliverables/acceptance criteria conflicts: SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by Provider's delivery lead, while Exhibit A contains a fixed Deliverable table and claims to be 'the sole source of the acceptance criteria'. 02_sow.md cl.6.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.1.2, §2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) versus 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). 01_msa.md cl.8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.7.1

Resubmission timetable conflict: SOW requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, Exhibit A imposes no resubmission deadline but adds a fresh 15 Business Day assessment period; the two review windows (5 vs 15 Business Days) cannot both run. 02_sow.md cl.6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.4

Internal inconsistency in acceptance criteria: D4 requires 'zero record loss' on a sample while D5 tolerates a 0.01% reconciliation variance on the full dataset, producing inconsistent migration quality standards. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.3.4–3.5

DPA governing law is internally contradictory: clause 13.1 adopts the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 then applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland; this also conflicts with the MSA's exclusive English law and jurisdiction clause. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2

Processing-location conflict: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations, but the delivery team (with system access) operates from Bengaluru, India, a subprocessor is in Singapore, key personnel are based in Bengaluru, and the DR site is Frankfurt (not an approved location in DPA Annex 2). 03_dpa.md cl.4.1, Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4; 12_subprocessors.md §2; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1; 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1

The Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region as determined by Provider's CISO, with notice only 30 days after a new region enters service — directly contrary to the DPA's UK/EEA-only rule and requirement for prior written authorisation of transfers. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.2

Two conflicting documents purport to be 'Annex 2 to the Data Processing Addendum': the DPA's own Annex 2 (approved processing locations: London, Dublin) and Schedule 9, the subprocessor list (which includes Singapore and Manchester locations). 03_dpa.md Annex 2 vs 12_subprocessors.md heading

Subprocessor approval conflict: DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; Schedule 9 permits addition or replacement on 30 days' notice with only an objection right, and immediate replacement with notice afterwards; the MSA separately permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent. 03_dpa.md cl.5.1 vs 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.1, 3.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.9.3

Schedule 9 clause 5.1 requires a transfer mechanism for subprocessors located outside the UK, implicitly permitting non-EEA locations (Singapore) that DPA clause 4.1 prohibits outright. 12_subprocessors.md cl.5.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1

Security incident notification deadlines conflict three ways: within 24 hours of awareness (DPA), within 48 hours of confirmation (InfoSec Policy), and within 72 hours of confirming it (SLA). The triggers (awareness vs confirmation) also differ. 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3
Dangling cross-reference: the SLA refers to escalation contacts 'listed in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum', but the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4 vs 03_dpa.md Annexes
Dangling cross-reference: the Exit Plan states Provider's personal data obligations are in 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14', but the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3 vs 03_dpa.md

Dangling cross-reference: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17', but the MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md

Dangling cross-reference: the Change Control Procedure charges for impact assessments 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', but the Exit Plan sets only a transition-assistance day rate and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2

The Pricing Schedule refers to role-specific rates 'set out in Exhibit B' without identifying that Exhibit B is an Exhibit to Statement of Work 1 (a document ranked differently in the precedence order), leaving the reference ambiguous. 10_pricing.md cl.2.4

Data deletion/retention obligations cannot all be satisfied: DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention for 90 days and delivery of all Customer data by the end of a 6-month transition period; the MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination. 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.2.1, 2.3, 4.1, Annex 1 milestone 5 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Records retention conflicts with the 7-year MSA retention obligation: security logs are to be retained 18 months 'and then deleted', service reports and the change log only 'for the duration of the Agreement'. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Encryption-at-rest conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data' (which excludes ordinary Customer personal data classified as Internal Data). 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.1.2–1.3, 3.1

Recovery objective conflicts with the incident target: RTO is 8 hours from Invocation, but a Priority 1 Incident (platform wholly unavailable) must be resolved within 4 hours. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.5.1

The BCDR Plan suspends all Service Level Schedule obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes failback unavailability (up to 12 hours) from availability, whereas the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows and the listed clause 9 exclusions; the two exclusion regimes are inconsistent. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.3, §9

The Acceptable Use Policy permits suspension of the Services with charges continuing to accrue, but suspension-related unavailability is not among the SLA's availability exclusions, so a permitted suspension would breach the availability service level and trigger credits. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.5.1, 5.4 vs 04_sla.md §9

Change control conflicts with the MSA requirement that any change to the Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation: the Procedure deems changes approved on Customer silence, allows Provider's Delivery Lead to approve changes up to £35,000 unilaterally, and allows unilateral emergency changes. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Internal timing trap: escalation of a Change Request dispute allows 5 Business Days per level over three levels (15 Business Days) and expressly does not suspend timetables, while a Change Request is deemed approved if Customer does not respond within 10 Business Days — a change can be deemed approved while it is still under dispute. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 8.1–8.3

Change-related charge exemption conflicts with the fixed-price commitment: the Procedure states change charges are not subject to notice requirements for charge increases, while the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no increase permitted. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.3

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW forbids substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution on resignation, dismissal or medical absence. 02_sow.md cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.1, 2.4

Day-rate conflict: standard rate £1,450 per person per day (Pricing) and role rates up to £1,450 (Exhibit B) versus transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day (Exit Plan), with knowledge-transfer sessions charged at the Exit rate; no clause reconciles which rate governs exit work. 10_pricing.md cl.2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2, 6.3

Expenses conflict: the SOW states the Fee covers all travel unless expressly stated otherwise, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel, subsistence and mileage recoverable at cost subject only to a £500 monthly approval threshold, and the SOW requires prior written approval for any out-of-Fee expense. 02_sow.md cl.5.2, 5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.3.1–3.3

Monitoring conflict: the Acceptable Use Policy states Provider does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility for it, while the InfoSec Policy requires continuous monitoring for anomalous access and full access logging, and the DPA requires logging of access to Customer Personal Data. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.5.1, 5.3; 03_dpa.md cl.7.2

Disclosure conflict: the Acceptable Use Policy permits Provider to disclose Customer content to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer before or after, which is incompatible with the DPA's processor duties to process only on documented instructions, to notify infringing instructions and to assist Customer with supervisory-authority matters. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.6.1–6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.2.2–2.3, 10.2

Payment card data inconsistency: the InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data held on Provider systems and a payment tokenisation subprocessor is approved, while the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform. 06_infosec.md cl.1.2; 12_subprocessors.md §2 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl.3.2

The DPA states data subjects include Customer's retail customers and loyalty scheme identifiers, while the Acceptable Use Policy bars any personal data relating to persons under 16 — no mechanism or allocation of responsibility for age screening of retail/loyalty data. 03_dpa.md cl.3.2–3.3 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl.3.1

Unilateral amendment rights conflict with the bilateral change regime: Provider may amend the Acceptable Use Policy on 30 days' notice, maintains and may add to the Glossary (whose definitions override all other documents), and the Glossary treats every document as amended from time to time — allowing Provider to change contract meaning without Customer agreement. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.8.1–8.2; 15_glossary.md cl.1.2, 3.3, 4.1–4.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4; 08_change_control.md §4

Response-time target is circular/unenforceable: Priority 1 'response within 15 minutes' is measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, i.e. from the response itself, so the clock is entirely within Provider's control. 04_sla.md cl.5.1, 5.4

Two overlapping and inconsistent service level regimes govern the same platform (SOW section 7 and the Service Level and Support Schedule) with different targets, credit caps and commencement triggers, and no clause states which regime applies. 02_sow.md §7 vs 04_sla.md §§3–4

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for up to six months after the effective date of termination 'on the terms then in force', which is irreconcilable with the MSA term/termination provisions (including immediate termination for material breach) and with the Order Form's fixed term. 09_exit.md cl.2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.1–3.4; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Exit timing is unworkable: milestone 1 (exit plan confirmed with incoming supplier) falls at T+15 Business Days, yet Provider has 15 Business Days merely to produce an effort estimate and Customer must approve that estimate before any assistance begins. 09_exit.md cl.3.3–3.4 and Annex 1 milestone 1

Exit Plan requires delivery of Customer data 'in the format used by Provider's systems', which conflicts with the DPA obligation to return data in a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit knowledge transfer requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect during the transition period (post-termination), conflicting with Exhibit B's requirement that Key Personnel be dedicated to the programme and with the SOW team composition obligations that end with the SOW. 09_exit.md cl.6.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1.2; 02_sow.md cl.3.1

Order Form permits invoices lacking a valid purchase order number to be 'returned unpaid', which conflicts with the MSA/SOW obligation to pay each undisputed invoice within the stated period. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3

The DPA clause headed 'Precedence' contains no precedence rule at all — it merely states the Addendum forms part of the Agreement — leaving the DPA's rank against the MSA, SOW, Order Form and Glossary unresolved. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

DPA states Annex 1 'sets out the processing details in full', but Annex 1 omits required details (e.g. frequency of processing, retention/erasure specifics, technical and organisational measures) and merely repeats clauses 3.1–3.3. 03_dpa.md cl.3.4 and Annex 1

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is inconsistent with the DPA's own no-limitation clause and with the MSA's liability carve-outs, and may be unenforceable as an indemnity against administrative penalties; no cap, conduct or mitigation provisions are given. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1–11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1–13.2

Order Form service commencement (1 April 2027) with service levels from that date is impossible against the SOW build schedule: no platform exists until Phase 2/3 (months 4–18), so availability credits would accrue before there is a platform. 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 3.3 vs 02_sow.md §4, cl.7.1

Volume-band overage charges (£0.004 per transaction above 250,000 per month) contradict the statement that the recurring charge is fixed and not subject to any increase during the initial term, and the SOW statement that the Fee covers all charges unless expressly stated. 10_pricing.md cl.1.3, 5.1–5.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.5.2
Pricing Schedule requires transaction volumes to be reported in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents do not include volumes. 10_pricing.md cl.5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.6.2

Invoice-dispute mechanics conflict: MSA/SOW require payment of 'undisputed' invoices without a dispute deadline, while the Pricing Schedule bars queries raised more than 10 Business Days after receipt. 10_pricing.md cl.6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3

Confidentiality survives only three years after termination, which is inconsistent with the 7-year records retention obligation and with the DPA treating all Customer Personal Data as Confidential Information for as long as it is held. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Out-of-hours service desk subprocessor (Larkfield) is engaged for out-of-hours support, which is inconsistent with the SLA's business-hours-only Priority 2/3 coverage and highlights the unresolved 24x7 promise in the Order Form. 12_subprocessors.md §2 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.2; 05_order_form.md cl.3.1

Subprocessor list review is scheduled at the 'quarterly steering committee', a body created only by Statement of Work 1; if the SOW is terminated (which the SOW says does not terminate the MSA) the review mechanism disappears. 12_subprocessors.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.4, 8.2

Glossary makes its own definitions override all others while also stating a term not defined in it takes its meaning from where used, yet key operative terms (e.g. 'Statement of Work', 'Schedule', 'Order Form', 'Continuity Event', 'Incident', 'Priority 1') are omitted, leaving the supremacy rule partial and unpredictable. 15_glossary.md cl.1.2–1.3, §2

Incident reporting duplication/conflict: root cause analysis for every Priority 1 Incident due within 5 Business Days of Resolution (SLA) versus a written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident (InfoSec), with no reconciliation of the two deliverables or their deadlines. 04_sla.md cl.8.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.6.2
Remediation timelines are inconsistent for the same critical exposure: critical penetration-test findings within 30 days but critical security patches within 14 days. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

Incident register review is set at a 'quarterly security review' that no document establishes; the only governance forums defined are the monthly service review and quarterly steering committee in the SOW. 06_infosec.md cl.6.3 vs 02_sow.md §8

Maintenance notice conflict: SLA requires 5 Business Days' notice of a maintenance window, while the BCDR Plan contemplates up to 12 hours' planned unavailability on failback with no notice obligation and BCDR tests require 20 Business Days' notice. 04_sla.md cl.3.4 vs 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2, 6.2

SOW phase durations (3+15+12+6 = 36 months) fill the entire programme with no float, yet phases may overlap only by written agreement and the assumption of no more than three legacy interfaces has no stated consequence or relief mechanism if breached. 02_sow.md cl.4.1–4.5, 10.3

The SOW's monthly service review, the SLA's report and the Change Control/change log reviews all reference 'the monthly service review' created only in the SOW; if the SOW terminates while the MSA continues, the SLA and Change Control governance obligations become inoperable. 04_sla.md cl.8.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.8.1, 2.4

Mutual liability cap based on Fees paid in the preceding 12 months would, on its face, cap Customer's own obligation to pay the Fees and would also cap Provider's liability below the SOW's £250,000 figure and below the £5m insurance requirement, leaving the insurance level unexplained/unmatched. 01_msa.md cl.13.1 vs cl.16.1; 02_sow.md cl.9.2

Provider's Delivery Lead is both the party approving changes up to £35,000 and the first level of escalation for change disputes, so the same person decides and hears challenges to the decision. 08_change_control.md cl.4.3, 8.1

Exhibit B fixes only four Key Personnel roles while the SOW commits an 11-person team including six engineers and a business analyst; Exhibit B then allows free reassignment of non-key personnel while requiring maintenance of team size, leaving the composition commitment unenforceable. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1, cl.4.1–4.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.1–3.2

Service credit cap stated three incompatible ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SOW), maximum 10% of monthly Fee (SLA), aggregate maximum 5% of recurring monthly charge (Pricing). 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2; 10_pricing.md cl.4.2

Start of service levels conflict: SOW applies service levels only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme), while the Order Form applies them from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, but the SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.2

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England & Wales public holidays (MSA); Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA); Monday–Friday including public holidays (Glossary, which claims to prevail). 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1; 15_glossary.md s.2

'Confidential Information' defined inconsistently: limited to information marked confidential in writing at disclosure (MSA) vs any information whether or not marked and whether oral or written (Glossary); the DPA adds a third rule for personal data. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

'Security Incident' defined three different ways: broad DPA definition (any unauthorised access, alteration, loss etc.); narrow SLA definition (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption); very broad Glossary definition (any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability). 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1; 15_glossary.md s.2
Security incident notification deadlines irreconcilable: 24 hours (DPA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy), 72 hours (SLA). 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3

Audit rights contradictory: MSA says delivery of the SOC 2 report extinguishes all audit/inspection rights, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1-9.2

MSA 12.2 requires records to be made available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights — the record-access obligation is self-cancelling. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps each party at 12 months' Fees (~£153,600) and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 Provider cap and the SOW claims precedence. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.2 and cl.1.2

DPA disapplies every limitation and exclusion of liability for any breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, which is incompatible with MSA 13.3 (cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum) and SOW 9.2-9.3. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.3 and 02_sow.md cl.9.2-9.3
Professional indemnity insurance limit conflict: £5,000,000 (MSA) vs £2,000,000 (SOW). 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Governing law internally contradictory within the DPA: clause 13.1 adopts the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in 13.2', and 13.2 then imposes the laws of the Republic of Ireland, also conflicting with MSA 15.1-15.2 (exclusive English jurisdiction). 03_dpa.md cl.13.1-13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.15

Data location conflict: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and its Annex 2 approves only London and Dublin, but the SOW places the delivery team (with system access) in Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1, Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4

InfoSec Policy lets Provider's CISO unilaterally choose any 'equivalent' region and notify Customer up to 30 days after go-live, contradicting the DPA's UK/EEA restriction and requirement of prior written Customer authorisation plus a transfer mechanism. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1-2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1-4.2

Approved subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, contradicting the DPA's UK/EEA-only processing restriction and the Annex 2 approved location list (London and Dublin only); Manchester is likewise not an approved Annex 2 location. 12_subprocessors.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1 and Annex 2

Two different documents are designated 'Annex 2' to the DPA: the DPA's own Annex 2 (approved processing locations) and Schedule 9 (subprocessor list), which states it is Annex 2 to the DPA. 12_subprocessors.md header vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2 / cl.4.3

Subprocessor appointment conflict: DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while Schedule 9 permits addition or replacement on 30 days' notice (objection only) and immediate replacement with notice afterwards. 03_dpa.md cl.5.1 vs 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.1, 3.4
MSA permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent, contradicting the DPA's specific-consent requirement for subprocessors. 01_msa.md cl.9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Data deletion and retention obligations cannot all be satisfied: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days. 01_msa.md cl.12.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.2.3

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, yet Customer data must be deleted 30 days (DPA) or 90 days (Exit 2.3) after termination — service cannot be delivered without the data. 09_exit.md cl.2.1-2.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 and 09_exit.md cl.2.3
Reference to a non-existent provision: Exit Plan points to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3
Reference to a non-existent provision: SLA refers to escalation contacts 'listed in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4

Reference to a non-existent provision/body: Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and describes no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1

Change approval conflict: MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure deems a change approved on Customer silence, lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 without Customer, and permits unilateral emergency changes. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Charge-change conflict: Change Control says change-related charges are exempt from the notice requirements for ordinary charge increases, but the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no increase, and MSA 4.4 governs increases. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.3 and 01_msa.md cl.4.4

Cross-reference to the wrong rate: Change Control charges impact assessments for rejected changes 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan' (£1,250/day, a transition-assistance rate), which also conflicts with the £1,450 standard rate card. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2 and 10_pricing.md cl.2.1

Day-rate conflict: transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day (Exit Plan) vs standard time-and-materials rate of £1,450 per person per day (Pricing) and role rates in Exhibit B. 09_exit.md cl.3.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl.2.1 and 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.3

Escalation paths conflict: SOW route is delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor; Change Control route is Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer (roles otherwise undefined in the contract set). 02_sow.md cl.8.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl.8.1

Deemed approval can occur before escalation completes: a Change Request is deemed approved after 10 Business Days of Customer silence, while escalation gives each of three levels 5 Business Days and expressly does not suspend the timetable. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2 with cl.8.2-8.3

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW forbids substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in stated cases. 02_sow.md cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.1, 2.4

Team location conflict: SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, whereas Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md cl.3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1

Recovery objectives incompatible with the SLA: RTO of 8 hours from Invocation (and up to 12 hours' further unavailability on failback) cannot coexist with a 4-hour Priority 1 Resolution target or 99.9% monthly availability (~43 minutes' downtime). 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 5.1

Availability exclusions conflict: BCDR excludes all Continuity Event and failback downtime from the availability calculation and suspends SLA obligations entirely, whereas the SLA/SOW exclude only agreed maintenance windows and the listed clause 9 exclusions. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1, 5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.3, s.9 and 02_sow.md cl.7.3

Disaster recovery site conflict: BCDR uses a secondary environment in Frankfurt, Germany, but the DPA's approved locations list only London (primary) and Dublin (disaster recovery). 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Circular/self-defeating measurement: SLA response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute 'response' target can never be breached. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1-5.3

Encryption obligations inconsistent: DPA requires encryption of Customer Personal Data in transit and at rest, while the InfoSec Policy mandates encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', leaving 'Internal Data' personal data unencrypted. 06_infosec.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.7.2

Log/record retention conflict: security logs must be retained 18 months and then deleted, service reports and the change log only for the duration of the Agreement, but the MSA requires 7 years' retention of all records. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

InfoSec Policy relies on a 'quarterly security review' that is not established anywhere in the governance provisions (SOW provides only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee). 06_infosec.md cl.6.3 vs 02_sow.md s.8

Unilateral amendment rights conflict with the change-control and mutual-agreement provisions: Provider may amend the Acceptable Use Policy on 30 days' notice and change the InfoSec Policy with mere notification, although both are Schedules forming part of the Agreement. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.8.1-8.2 and 06_infosec.md cl.10.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4 and 08_change_control.md s.1

Provider disclaims all monitoring of and responsibility for content, which conflicts with its access-logging, continuous monitoring and processor security obligations. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.5.1, 5.3 and 03_dpa.md cl.7.1-7.2

Immediate suspension without notice for a suspected policy breach is inconsistent with the MSA's requirement of a 15-day remedy period for material breach, given that a material AUP breach is deemed a material breach of the Agreement. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.5.1, 9.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.4

'Services' defined inconsistently: services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) vs SOW services plus SLA support services (Glossary), altering scope, fee coverage and liability calculations. 01_msa.md cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

'Deliverable' defined inconsistently: an item identified as a deliverable in a SOW (MSA) vs any output whether or not so identified (Glossary), which also conflicts with Exhibit A's closed D1–D7 list. 01_msa.md cl.1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md s.2

'Fee' defined inconsistently: amounts payable under MSA clause 4 (MSA) vs all amounts including time-and-materials and expenses (Glossary), which changes the liability cap and the percentage-based service credit caps. 01_msa.md cl.1.4 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

'Agreement' defined inconsistently: MSA plus Schedules and Addenda (MSA) vs MSA plus Order Form plus every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum (Glossary), leaving the Order Form's and Exhibits' contractual status unclear. 01_msa.md cl.1.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2
'Subprocessor' scope differs: a third party processing 'Customer Personal Data' (DPA) vs any third party processing 'Personal Data' (Glossary). 03_dpa.md cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

Expenses approval conflict: SOW requires prior written approval for all expenses outside the Fee, while the Pricing Schedule requires approval only where monthly expenses exceed £500. 02_sow.md cl.5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.3.2

findings: Circular order of precedence: MSA cl.14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 cl.1.2 says the SOW (which is Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA. Each document claims to defeat the other. 01_msa.md cl.14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.1.2

Order Form cl.2.1/2.2 places itself at the top of the precedence order, contradicting MSA cl.14.2 (MSA prevails) and SOW cl.1.2 (SOW prevails); three documents each claim primacy. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1-2.2

Glossary cl.1.2 states its definitions prevail over any definition in any other document, yet the Glossary is Schedule 10 and therefore ranks below the Order Form and the MSA under Order Form cl.2.1 and MSA cl.14.2 — a fourth, circular precedence claim. 15_glossary.md cl.1.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl.2.1, 01_msa.md cl.14.2

The Order Form is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined in MSA cl.1.1 (MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only) and is not a 'Schedule' within MSA cl.1.6, so its precedence claim has no contractual hook; the Glossary definition of 'Agreement' does include the Order Form, conflicting with MSA cl.1.1. 01_msa.md cl.1.1/1.6 vs 05_order_form.md cl.2 and 15_glossary.md 'Agreement'

Exhibits A and B (Documents 13 and 14) are not included in the MSA definition of 'Agreement' nor in the Order Form's precedence list, leaving them with no defined rank or status. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md / 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md
