Cross-reference to a non-existent clause and body: Change Control cl.4.1 submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and never establishes a Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1
Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan cl.5.3 refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: Change Control cl.7.2 charges for impact assessments 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', which contains only a transition-assistance rate (£1,250/day), not an impact assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Duplicate/conflicting 'Annex 2' to the DPA: the DPA's own Annex 2 lists approved processing locations (London, Dublin), while Document 12 declares itself to be Annex 2 to the DPA (a subprocessor list). Two different documents claim the same annex slot. 03_dpa.md Annex 2 vs 12_subprocessors.md preamble

Document 12 has two incompatible identities/ranks: it is both Schedule 9 to the MSA and Annex 2 to the DPA; under Order Form cl.2.1 Schedules outrank Addenda, so its own precedence position is contradictory. 12_subprocessors.md preamble vs 05_order_form.md cl.2.1

Data location conflict: DPA cl.4.1 permits processing only in the UK/EEA and Annex 2 approves only London and Dublin, but the SOW delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, Exhibit B bases two key roles in Bengaluru, the approved subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics in Singapore, and the BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt (not in Annex 2). 03_dpa.md cl.4.1/4.3 & Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4, 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1, 12_subprocessors.md cl.2, 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1

Information Security Policy cl.2.1 lets Provider's CISO unilaterally choose any region for storing and processing Customer data, and cl.2.3 requires only 30 days' after-the-fact notice, directly contradicting DPA cl.4.1/4.2 (UK/EEA only, prior written authorisation and transfer mechanism). 06_infosec.md cl.2.1-2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1-4.2

Subprocessor consent conflict: DPA cl.5.1 requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, but Document 12 cl.3.1 allows addition on 30 days' notice and cl.3.4 allows immediate replacement with notice afterwards; MSA cl.9.3 further permits subcontracting without any consent. 03_dpa.md cl.5.1 vs 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.1/3.4 and 01_msa.md cl.9.3

Audit rights conflict: MSA cl.10.2 provides a SOC 2 report and expressly removes any further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while DPA cl.9.1-9.2 grants an annual audit including inspection of premises and systems. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1-9.2

Internally self-defeating provision: MSA cl.12.2 promises records will be made available to Customer 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 is precisely the clause that denies inspection rights. 01_msa.md cl.12.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA cl.6.1 states no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer confirms expressly in writing, while SOW cl.6.3 deems a Deliverable accepted after five Business Days' silence; Exhibit A cl.5.3 again says silence does not constitute acceptance. 01_msa.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.3
Conflicting acceptance assessment periods: 5 Business Days (SOW deemed acceptance) versus 15 Business Days (Exhibit A cl.5.2/5.4). 02_sow.md cl.6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.2/5.4

Conflicting sources of the Deliverables list and acceptance criteria: SOW cl.6.1 says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead; Exhibit A cl.1.2 says it is the sole source of acceptance criteria; MSA cl.6.2 points to a non-existent Schedule 1, Section 12. 02_sow.md cl.6.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.1.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.6.2

Warranty period conflict: MSA cl.8.2 warrants Deliverables for 90 days after acceptance; Exhibit A cl.7.1 warrants each accepted Deliverable for 180 days. 01_msa.md cl.8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.7.1

Liability cap conflict: MSA cl.13.1 caps liability at 12 months' Fees (approx. £148,800-£157,200) and cl.13.3 says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while SOW cl.9.2 sets a £250,000 cap on Provider's liability. 01_msa.md cl.13.1/13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.2

DPA cl.11.1 disapplies every limitation and exclusion of liability for breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, contradicting MSA cl.13.1/13.3 (which state the cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum) and SOW cl.9.3 (exclusion of indirect loss). 03_dpa.md cl.11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1/13.3, 02_sow.md cl.9.3
Insurance conflict: MSA cl.16.1 requires £5,000,000 professional indemnity cover; SOW cl.9.4 requires not less than £2,000,000 for the same engagement. 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Governing law conflict: MSA cl.15.1/15.2 apply the laws and exclusive jurisdiction of England and Wales, while DPA cl.13.2 applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland to the Addendum and disputes under it. 01_msa.md cl.15.1-15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.13.2

Internal contradiction within the DPA governing law clause: cl.13.1 adopts the law applicable to the Agreement 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and cl.13.2 then displaces it entirely with Irish law, making cl.13.1 self-cancelling. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1-13.2

Term conflict: MSA cl.3.1 sets a 24-month initial term, Order Form cl.1.2 sets a 12-month initial term, and SOW cl.2.1 commits to a 36-month programme — the programme cannot be completed within either stated term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.1.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.1

Renewal/non-renewal notice conflict: MSA cl.3.2/3.3 require 90 days' notice to prevent automatic 12-month renewal; Order Form cl.6.2 requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal. 01_msa.md cl.3.2-3.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl.6.2

Termination for convenience conflict: MSA cl.3.3 requires not less than 90 days' notice; SOW cl.2.3 allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice, which would defeat the MSA notice period for the only Services being provided. 01_msa.md cl.3.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.3

Date conflict: the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and the Order Form Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027), and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 02_sow.md cl.2.2 vs 01_msa.md preamble, 05_order_form.md cl.1.3/7.3

Records retention conflict: MSA cl.12.4 requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination, DPA cl.8.2 requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination, and Exit cl.2.3/5.2 require retention for 90 days then deletion. These cannot all be met. 01_msa.md cl.12.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.2.3/5.2

Log retention conflict: Information Security Policy cl.5.2 requires security logs to be retained for 18 months and then deleted, contradicting the 7-year retention obligation in MSA cl.12.4. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Report/change log retention conflict: SLA cl.6.3 and Change Control cl.9.3 require retention only 'for the duration of the Agreement', contradicting MSA cl.12.4 (7 years post-termination) and Exit cl.4.1(e) (delivery of change log at exit). 04_sla.md cl.6.3 and 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Confidentiality definition conflict: MSA cl.11.1 protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; the Glossary protects any information whether or not marked and whether oral or written; DPA cl.1.4 deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 15_glossary.md 'Confidential Information' vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality survival of 3 years (MSA cl.11.3) is shorter than the 7-year records/data retention obligation (MSA cl.12.4) and than the indefinite protection required for personal data under the DPA — data would remain held after confidentiality obligations lapse. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4 and 03_dpa.md cl.1.4/7

Change control conflict: MSA cl.2.4 requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but Change Control cl.4.2 deems approval from Customer silence, cl.4.3 lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 unilaterally, and cl.6.1 permits emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Acceptable Use Policy cl.8.1 lets Provider unilaterally amend the Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice, contradicting MSA cl.2.4 (bilateral written agreement) and the Change Control Procedure's scope over changes to the Services. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.8.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4, 08_change_control.md cl.1.1

Glossary cl.4.1/4.2 make the Provider's Commercial Director the maintainer of a document whose definitions override every other contract document, while also requiring change control for additions — an internal contradiction and a unilateral amendment power over agreed terms. 15_glossary.md cl.4.1-4.2 with cl.1.2

Definition conflict for 'Deliverable': MSA cl.1.3 limits it to items identified as deliverables in a Statement of Work; the Glossary extends it to any output of the Services whether or not so identified, which also expands the IP assignment in MSA cl.7.2 and the exit obligations. 01_msa.md cl.1.3 vs 15_glossary.md 'Deliverable'

Definition conflict for 'Fee': MSA cl.1.4 limits Fee to amounts payable under clause 4; the Glossary includes all recurring, time-and-materials charges and expenses. This changes the value of the liability cap and of the percentage-based service credit caps. 01_msa.md cl.1.4 vs 15_glossary.md 'Fee'

Definition conflict for 'Services': MSA cl.1.5 covers only services described in a Statement of Work; the Glossary adds the support services in the SLA, leaving unclear whether support is within the SOW Fee. 01_msa.md cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary.md 'Services'

Definition conflict for 'Subprocessor': DPA cl.1.5 refers to processing of Customer Personal Data; the Glossary refers to Personal Data generally (UK GDPR), a different scope. 03_dpa.md cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary.md 'Subprocessor'/'Personal Data'

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW cl.3.5 prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B cl.2.1 permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and cl.2.4 permits immediate substitution. 02_sow.md cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.1/2.4

Team location conflict: SOW cl.3.4 states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md cl.3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1

Rate conflicts for time-and-materials/assistance work: Pricing cl.2.1 standard rate £1,450/day, Exhibit B role rates £950-£1,450, and Exit cl.3.2/6.3 transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day — no reconciliation, and the Exit rate applies to roles priced differently elsewhere. 10_pricing.md cl.2.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.3 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Expenses approval conflict: SOW cl.5.4 requires prior written approval for all expenses outside the Fee, while Pricing cl.3.2 requires approval only where expenses exceed £500 in a month. 02_sow.md cl.5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.3.2

Recovery objectives are incompatible with the availability and resolution commitments: an 8-hour RTO and 12 hours of failback unavailability cannot coexist with 99.9% monthly availability (~43 minutes) or the 4-hour Priority 1 Resolution target; the reconciliation is asserted only by BCDR cl.5.1/5.3, which conflicts with the SLA's own exclusion list. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1/5.1-5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 5.1, 9

BCDR cl.5.2 contemplates up to 12 hours of planned unavailability without observing the SLA requirement of 5 Business Days' notice for maintenance windows, and it is not an 'agreed maintenance window' under SLA cl.9.3. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.4/9.3

SLA response and resolution targets are circular/unmeasurable: cl.5.4 measures the response time from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident, so the 15-minute Priority 1 response target measures nothing and Provider controls the clock start. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1-5.3

SLA cl.4.3 makes service credits Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, conflicting with SOW cl.7.4 (entitlement expressed differently), with the DPA's disapplication of limitations, and with Customer's general damages/termination rights for material breach. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4, 03_dpa.md cl.11.1, 01_msa.md cl.3.4

Exit obligations conflict with termination: Exit cl.2.1/2.2 require Provider to keep providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which is inconsistent with immediate termination for material breach (MSA cl.3.4) and with the 12/24-month terms, and no charging basis for that continuation is stated. 09_exit.md cl.2.1-2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.1/3.4

Exit data format conflict: Exit cl.4.1(a) requires return of data 'in the format used by Provider's systems', while DPA cl.8.1 requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit milestone timetable is internally unachievable: Annex 1 milestone 1 falls due at T+15 Business Days, yet cl.3.3/3.4 allow Provider 15 Business Days merely to produce an effort estimate which Customer must then approve before assistance begins; milestone 2 (data extract at T+30 Business Days) also post-dates the DPA's 30-day deletion deadline. 09_exit.md Annex 1 with cl.3.3-3.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2

Exit cl.6.1 requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect to support knowledge transfer during the transition period, conflicting with Exhibit B cl.1.2 (Key Personnel dedicated exclusively to this programme) once the programme has ended, and with the fixed team commitment in SOW cl.3.1. 09_exit.md cl.6.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1.2

Payment card data contradiction: the Information Security Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data and the subprocessor list includes a payment tokenisation provider, while the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits Customer from storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform; the DPA's data categories (Annex 1) omit payment data altogether. 06_infosec.md cl.1.2 & 12_subprocessors.md cl.2 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl.3.2 and 03_dpa.md cl.3.3/Annex 1

Acceptable Use Policy cl.4.2 (Provider inspection of content) and cl.6.1-6.2 (disclosure to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer) conflict with DPA cl.2.2 (processing only on Customer's documented instructions) and with the processor's duty to inform the controller. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.4.2, 6.1-6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.2.2, 10

Suspension right conflict: AUP cl.5.1 allows immediate suspension of the Services without notice and cl.5.4 keeps charges running, with no cure period, contradicting MSA cl.3.4's 15-day remedy regime and the MSA's absence of any suspension right. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.5.1/5.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.4

Internal inconsistency in the Information Security Policy: critical patches must be applied within 14 days (cl.9.1) but critical penetration-test findings may take 30 days to remediate (cl.7.4). 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

Acceptance criteria for the migration deliverables are inconsistent: D4 requires zero record loss on a representative sample while D5 tolerates a 0.01% reconciliation variance. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.3.4-3.5

Pricing cl.7.1 requires a rate card review at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date, which conflicts with cl.1.3 and Exhibit B cl.3.2 fixing charges/rates for the initial term (24 months under the MSA). 10_pricing.md cl.7.1 vs cl.1.3, 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.3.2

Invoice query window of 10 Business Days (Pricing cl.6.3) conflicts with the open-ended right to dispute invoices implied by MSA cl.4.3 ('each undisputed invoice') and the 30/45/60-day payment terms. 10_pricing.md cl.6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3

Pricing cl.1.1 states the recurring charge comprises a base platform charge and a managed-service surcharge but gives no split, making the volume-band and credit calculations and any partial-service adjustments indeterminate. 10_pricing.md cl.1.1

DPA cl.11.2 provides for mutual indemnification against regulatory fines, which is unenforceable in many cases and cuts across the DPA's own disapplication of liability limits and the MSA liability regime. 03_dpa.md cl.11.2
Single point of failure with no deputy: only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, and the same individual owns the Plan, with no alternate named. 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1 with cl.9.1

SOW cl.3.3 requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours while cl.3.4 locates the team in Bengaluru and the SLA requires 24x7 Priority 1 cover, with no defined 'Customer working hours' anywhere in the documents. 02_sow.md cl.3.3-3.4 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.1

The DPA gives Customer an audit right (cl.9) but the Order Form precedence order ranks the Addendum lowest, so the MSA's no-audit clause and liability cap would override the DPA notwithstanding DPA cl.11.1/12.1 — an unresolved precedence contradiction. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1(d) vs 03_dpa.md cl.11.1, 12.1

Exit cl.3.1 obliges Provider to give reasonable transition assistance, but cl.3.4 makes assistance conditional on Customer approving an estimate, creating a deadlock in which no assistance need be provided. 09_exit.md cl.3.1 vs cl.3.4

The Glossary's Business Day definition ('Monday to Friday, including public holidays') is internally incoherent for a UK contract and, if it prevails under cl.1.2, silently overrides the deadline calculations agreed in every other document. 15_glossary.md 'Business Day' with cl.1.2

findings: Circular / irreconcilable order of precedence: the MSA says it prevails over every Schedule and Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 (a Schedule) says it prevails over the MSA. Neither conflict rule can be applied. 01_msa.md cl.14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.1.2

Third and fourth competing precedence rules: the Order Form claims to prevail over every other document (and ranks Schedules third), while the Glossary (Schedule 10) claims its definitions prevail over any definition in any other document. Combined with MSA 14.2 and SOW 1.2 the precedence chain is fully circular. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2; 15_glossary.md cl.1.2

MSA 13.3 states the liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, which directly contradicts SOW 1.2 (SOW prevails) and DPA 11.1 (no limitation applies) — an unresolvable precedence loop on the most important commercial term. 01_msa.md cl.13.3; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

Monthly charge stated four inconsistent ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing Schedule), and £12,800 implied by the Order Form's £153,600 annual contract value. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 10_pricing.md cl.1.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Billing timing conflict: MSA, SOW and Order Form all require invoicing monthly in arrears, but the Pricing Schedule invoices the recurring charge monthly in advance on the first Business Day of the month. 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.5 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.2, 6.1

Price-increase conflict: MSA permits an annual CPI-linked increase on 60 days' notice, but the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or increase; the Change Control Procedure adds a third route (change-related charges exempt from notice requirements). 01_msa.md cl.4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl.5.3

Initial term stated inconsistently: 24 months (MSA), 12 months (Order Form), and a 36-month programme (SOW) that cannot be completed within either contractual term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2; 02_sow.md cl.2.1

Commencement dates conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — i.e. work begins a month before the agreement it is issued under exists, and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027). 01_msa.md preamble; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.2

Termination/non-renewal notice conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience and makes renewal terminable only under cl.3.3, while the Order Form allows non-renewal on 30 days' notice and the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md cl.3.2–3.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2; 02_sow.md cl.2.3

"Business Day" defined three incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA); Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA); Monday–Friday including public holidays (Glossary). "Confidential Information" defined inconsistently: MSA requires written marking at disclosure; the Glossary covers all information whether marked or not, oral or written; the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential regardless of marking. 01_msa.md cl.11.1; 15_glossary.md s.2; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

"Deliverable" defined inconsistently: only items identified as deliverables in a SOW (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary) — this changes the scope of the IP assignment, acceptance and warranty regimes. 01_msa.md cl.1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

"Fee" defined inconsistently: amounts payable under MSA cl.4 (i.e. the monthly charge) versus all amounts payable including T&M and expenses (Glossary). The MSA cap is also mutual whereas the SOW cap applies only to Provider. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limit conflicts: not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) versus not less than £2,000,000 (SOW). 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Audit rights irreconcilable: MSA states that provision of the SOC 2 report extinguishes any further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises and systems, and the Information Security Policy requires sharing penetration test reports. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2; 06_infosec.md cl.7.2
MSA cl.12.2 makes record access subject to cl.10.2, which denies any access/audit right — the records obligation is self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent conflicts three ways: MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent; DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; the Approved Subprocessor List allows additions on 30 days' notice (and immediate replacement in some cases) with only an objection right. 01_msa.md cl.9.3; 03_dpa.md cl.5.1; 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.1, 3.4

Data location conflicts: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with approved locations London and Dublin only, but the delivery team (and therefore access to data) sits in Bengaluru, India, a Subprocessor (Kestrel Analytics) is in Singapore, the disaster recovery site is in Frankfurt (not listed in Annex 2), and the Information Security Policy lets Provider's CISO unilaterally choose any Provider region. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1, 4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md cl.3.4; 12_subprocessors.md s.2; 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1; 06_infosec.md cl.2.1

Duplicate/conflicting Annex 2: the DPA contains its own Annex 2 listing approved processing locations, while Schedule 9 states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA and lists subprocessors instead. Two different documents claim the same annex number and content. 03_dpa.md cl.4.3 and Annex 2 vs 12_subprocessors.md preamble
Reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum" for security escalation contacts; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4
Reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan cites "Data Processing Addendum, clause 14"; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3

Reference to a non-existent clause and body: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17"; the MSA has only 16 clauses and establishes no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1

Governing law conflict and internal self-contradiction: MSA is governed by English law with exclusive English jurisdiction; the DPA says it follows the Agreement's law "save as provided in clause 13.2" and then subjects itself to the law of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2
DPA clause headed "Precedence" contains no precedence rule at all, so the Addendum's relationship to conflicting MSA terms (notably liability and audit) is unresolved. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Data retention obligations mutually impossible: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days then deletion; the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months; the SLA requires reports to be kept only for the term. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 5.2; 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.6.3

Exit timetable is incompatible with the data retention/deletion rules: the transition period runs to 6 months after termination and parallel running completes at T+90 Business Days (about 4.5 months), but all Customer data must be deleted 30 days (DPA) or 90 calendar days (Exit cl.2.3) after termination. 09_exit.md cl.2.1, 2.3, Annex 1 milestones 4–5 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for the whole transition period following any termination, including termination for material breach which the MSA makes effective immediately on notice — the two cannot both operate. 09_exit.md cl.1.2, 2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.4
Data return format conflict: Exit Plan requires return "in the format used by Provider's systems" whereas the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit assistance is made conditional on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider's pricing to block the mandatory exit obligations and the Annex 1 milestone at T+15 Business Days. 09_exit.md cl.3.3–3.4 with Annex 1

Transition day rate (£1,250) conflicts with the rate card standard rate (£1,450) and with the Exhibit B role rates, which are stated to apply to all time-and-materials work in place of the standard rate. 09_exit.md cl.3.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl.2.1, 2.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.3.1

Change Control cross-reference is wrong in substance: it charges impact-assessment preparation "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", but that document sets only a transition-assistance rate, not a rate for change work. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2

Deemed approval and unilateral approval of changes contradict the MSA requirement that any change to the Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Internal timing defect: a Change Request is deemed approved after 10 Business Days' silence, but the escalation ladder allows 5 Business Days at each of three levels (up to 15 Business Days) and expressly does not suspend the timetable — a disputed change can be deemed approved while the dispute is still running. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2 vs cl.8.1–8.3

Provider's Delivery Lead may approve changes up to £35,000 without reference to Customer, which conflicts both with MSA cl.2.4 and with the requirement for Customer approval of expenses/charges elsewhere (SOW cl.5.4, Pricing cl.3.2 £500 threshold). 08_change_control.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.4; 10_pricing.md cl.3.2
No-set-off clause conflicts with the automatic deduction of service credits from invoices. 01_msa.md cl.4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 10_pricing.md cl.4.1

Recovery objectives are mathematically incompatible with the availability commitments: an 8-hour RTO plus up to 12 hours' planned unavailability on failback far exceeds the downtime allowance of 99.9% (approx. 43 minutes/month) or even 99.5% (approx. 3.6 hours/month). 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.7.2

BCDR purports to suspend all SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and to exclude that downtime from availability, but the SLA's exclusions list does not include continuity events and the SLA contains no such suspension — the two documents give different availability calculations. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1, 5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.2, s.9

A 24-hour RPO (i.e. up to a day of data loss) is inconsistent with the migration acceptance criteria requiring zero record loss / 0.01% variance and with the promise of transaction-record integrity. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.3.4–3.5

Invocation may be declared only by Provider's Head of Operations, with no deputy or alternate, creating a single point of failure in the continuity plan; Customer has no right to require invocation. 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1

Encryption obligations inconsistent: the DPA requires encryption of all Customer Personal Data at rest, but the Information Security Policy mandates encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, leaving Internal Data (which can include personal data) unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.1.3, 3.1

Information Security Policy allows Provider's CISO to determine data locations and to notify new regions up to 30 days after they enter service, contradicting the DPA requirement of prior written Customer authorisation for any change of processing territory. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.2

Acceptable Use Policy states Provider does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility for it, contradicting the security obligations to log all access, monitor continuously for anomalous access, and act as processor under documented instructions. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.5.1, 5.3; 03_dpa.md cl.7.2

AUP permits Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement with no obligation to notify Customer before or after, which conflicts with the processor's duty to process only on Customer's documented instructions and to notify Customer of incidents/requests. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.6.1–6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.2.2, 6.1, 10.1

AUP prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, yet the Information Security Policy expressly contemplates payment card data as Restricted Data and a Subprocessor is engaged for payment tokenisation — inconsistent assumptions about what data the platform holds. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.3.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.1.2; 12_subprocessors.md s.2

Suspension of the Services without notice, with charges continuing to accrue, conflicts with the availability commitment and service-credit regime, since suspension-related downtime is not among the SLA exclusions. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.5.1, 5.4 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1, s.9

Unilateral amendment rights (Provider may amend the AUP on 30 days' notice; Provider reviews and changes the Information Security Policy; the Glossary is maintained by Provider's Commercial Director) contradict the MSA's requirement that changes be agreed in writing, the definition of a Schedule as a document executed by both parties, and the Change Control Procedure. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.8.1; 06_infosec.md cl.10.1–10.2; 15_glossary.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.6, 2.4; 08_change_control.md s.4

Self-defeating measurement rule: SLA response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, making the 15-minute "response" target circular and allowing Provider to control the clock start. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1

Internal inconsistency in the SLA: a Security Incident is treated as a Priority 1 Incident requiring resolution within 4 hours, yet notification to Customer is allowed up to 72 hours after confirmation. 04_sla.md cl.7.2 vs cl.7.3

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the DPA's disapplication of all limitations and with the SOW's separate credit entitlement of a different amount. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.11.1; 02_sow.md cl.7.4

Key personnel locations conflict: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London; the SOW also requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours. 02_sow.md cl.3.3–3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1

Substitution of key personnel conflicts: SOW requires Customer's prior written agreement, whereas Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in stated circumstances. 02_sow.md cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.1, 2.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination while records and data must be retained for 7 years and personal data is deemed Confidential Information indefinitely — the protection lapses while the data is still held. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 with cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Phase schedule cannot fit the contract term: the four SOW phases total 36 months from 1 March 2027 (ending February 2030) and may not overlap without written agreement, whereas the MSA initial term ends 31 March 2029 and the Order Form term ends 31 March 2028, so completion depends on renewals neither document guarantees. 02_sow.md cl.2.1–2.2, s.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Reporting inconsistency: the Pricing Schedule requires actual transaction volumes to be reported in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents do not include volumes. 10_pricing.md cl.5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.6.2

"Initial term" for price-hold purposes is ambiguous because the term is defined differently in the MSA (24 months) and Order Form (12 months); the Pricing Schedule and Exhibit B both hold rates "for the initial term" without specifying which. 10_pricing.md cl.1.3; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.3.2

Rate card internally inconsistent with role rates: the standard rate is £1,450/day for every role "unless a role-specific rate is set out in Exhibit B", but Exhibit B sets the Delivery Lead and Solution Architect rates at exactly £1,450 while the Change Control and Exit documents use other rates, leaving the applicable rate for change/exit work unclear. 10_pricing.md cl.2.1, 2.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.3

Transfer clause in the Subprocessor Schedule requires a transfer mechanism for any subprocessor outside the United Kingdom, which contradicts the DPA's permission to process freely within the UK and EEA (e.g. the Dublin backup provider). 12_subprocessors.md cl.5.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1

Subprocessor Schedule gives Customer a right to terminate affected Services on 30 days' notice, conflicting with the MSA's 90-day convenience termination regime and with the absence of any partial-termination mechanism in the MSA. 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.3

Incident reporting duplicated with different deadlines: root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution (SLA) versus a written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident (Information Security Policy), with no statement of which governs. 04_sla.md cl.8.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.6.2

Governance body referenced that is not established anywhere: the Information Security Policy relies on a "quarterly security review", but the governance provisions create only a monthly service review and a quarterly steering committee. 06_infosec.md cl.6.3 vs 02_sow.md s.8

Remediation timescales inconsistent: critical penetration-test findings must be fixed within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding requiring a patch. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

The Glossary is stated to be the overriding source of definitions yet is maintained unilaterally by Provider's Commercial Director and, contradictorily, any addition to it is subject to the Change Control Procedure. 15_glossary.md cl.1.2, 4.1–4.2

Glossary "Business Day" definition is internally incoherent for a services contract (working days that include public holidays) and defeats every notice and response period drafted on the assumption that holidays are excluded. 15_glossary.md s.2

Glossary "Subprocessor" refers to processing of "Personal Data" generally, whereas the DPA limits it to Customer Personal Data, widening the consent/flow-down regime unintentionally. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.5

Order Form's precedence list omits the Exhibits (A and B) and does not reconcile Statements of Work, which are simultaneously described as Schedules; the status and ranking of the Exhibits is left undefined. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1; 01_msa.md cl.2.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md s.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md preamble

Acceptance criteria for D5 are internally inconsistent with D4: D4 requires zero record loss on a sample while D5 tolerates a 0.01% reconciliation variance in production. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.3.4–3.5

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is drafted so that each party indemnifies the other for fines "imposed on it as a result of the other's breach", which conflicts with the MSA liability cap and with cl.11.1 and may be unenforceable for public-law fines. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1–11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3

Exit rehearsal obligation is indefinite ("at least once in the term") and inconsistent with the annual review obligation and with the BCDR annual test cycle, leaving no enforceable date. 09_exit.md cl.9.1–9.2 vs 07_bcdr.md cl.6.1

Invoice query window of 10 Business Days sits uneasily with the payment obligation for "undisputed" invoices and with 30/45/60-day payment terms, potentially barring disputes before payment falls due. 10_pricing.md cl.6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3
unmatched: "Services" defined inconsistently: services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus SOW services plus the support services in the SLA (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl.1.5 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

findings: Circular precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 (a Schedule) says it prevails over the MSA. Neither can be applied. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Four-way circular precedence: Order Form ranks itself first and says it prevails over any other document; the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda; the SOW says it prevails over the MSA; and the Glossary (Schedule 10, ranked below both) says its definitions prevail over any other document. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1–2.2; 01_msa.md cl. 14.2; 02_sow.md cl. 1.2; 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2
Order Form precedence list omits Exhibits (Exhibit A and Exhibit B), so documents forming part of the agreement are unranked. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1
Three incompatible monthly charges for the same Services: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing Schedule). 01_msa.md cl. 4.1; 02_sow.md cl. 5.1; 10_pricing.md cl. 1.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 and is inconsistent with both the MSA fee (£148,800/yr) and the Pricing Schedule (£157,200/yr). 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4
Three incompatible payment terms: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl. 4.3; 02_sow.md cl. 5.3; 05_order_form.md cl. 1.6

Billing basis conflict: MSA, SOW and Order Form require invoicing monthly in arrears; the Pricing Schedule requires the recurring charge to be invoiced monthly in advance on the first Business Day of the month. 01_msa.md cl. 4.3; 02_sow.md cl. 5.3; 05_order_form.md cl. 1.5 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.2, 6.1

Initial term conflict: MSA states 24 months; Order Form states 12 months; SOW commits to a 36-month programme that cannot be completed within either term. 01_msa.md cl. 3.1; 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2; 02_sow.md cl. 2.1

Start-date conflict: the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — before the Agreement exists and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027). 01_msa.md preamble; 05_order_form.md cl. 1.3, 7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.2

Termination/non-renewal notice conflict: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form. 01_msa.md cl. 3.3; 02_sow.md cl. 2.3; 05_order_form.md cl. 6.2

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: MSA requires express written acceptance and prohibits deemed acceptance, while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl. 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 6.3

Day-rate conflict for the same work: standard rate £1,450 per person per day (Pricing) vs transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day (Exit Plan), with the Change Control Procedure pricing impact assessments at 'the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan'. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.1; 09_exit.md cl. 3.2; 08_change_control.md cl. 7.2

Cross-reference to 'Exhibit B' for role rates without identifying the document; Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule, and is ranked differently in precedence. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.4

Exhibit B's Key Personnel table names a 'Lead Solution Architect' and 'Second Solution Architect' but the rate table lists only a single undifferentiated 'Solution Architect' role, and no rate is given for the Lead role. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 1 and 3

Glossary redefines core terms inconsistently with the operative documents while claiming to override them: 'Agreement' (includes the Order Form, unlike MSA 1.1), 'Deliverable' (any output, unlike MSA 1.3), 'Services' (includes support services, unlike MSA 1.5), 'Fee' (all amounts including expenses, unlike MSA 1.4), 'Subprocessor' (any Personal Data, unlike DPA 1.5). 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2, 2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5; 03_dpa.md cl. 1.5

Because the Glossary redefines 'Fee' to include all charges and expenses, the service credit caps and the liability cap expressed as percentages of, or multiples of, the 'monthly Fee'/'Fees' become indeterminate. 15_glossary.md cl. 2 ('Fee') vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4; 04_sla.md cl. 4.2; 01_msa.md cl. 13.1
Glossary defining 'Business Day' as including public holidays is self-defeating and inconsistent with ordinary usage and with every deadline drafted elsewhere. 15_glossary.md cl. 2 ('Business Day')

Glossary definitions are stated to prevail over all other documents yet the Glossary is unilaterally maintained by Provider's Commercial Director, allowing Provider to rewrite operative obligations. 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2, 4.1
No-set-off/no-deduction clause conflicts with the automatic application of service credits as deductions from invoices. 01_msa.md cl. 4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl. 4.1; 10_pricing.md cl. 4.1

'Sole financial remedy' for availability failure in the SLA conflicts with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of limitations, and sits oddly with the unlimited-liability carve-outs. 04_sla.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4; 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1

Response and Resolution clocks run from the moment Provider itself acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the response target is self-referential and Provider controls the start of its own deadlines. 04_sla.md cl. 5.4
Priority 2 Resolution target of one Business Day cannot be reconciled with Priority 2 support being available only 08:00–18:00 on Business Days for a 24x7 platform. 04_sla.md cl. 5.2 vs 2.2

Incident report timing conflict: RCA for a Priority 1 (which includes a Security Incident) due within 5 Business Days of Resolution under the SLA, but written incident report due within 10 Business Days of closure under the InfoSec Policy. 04_sla.md cl. 8.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 6.2

Internal inconsistency on critical remediation: critical patches within 14 days of release but critical penetration-test findings within 30 days, with no reconciliation of overlapping critical vulnerabilities. 06_infosec.md cl. 9.1 vs 7.4

Provider may unilaterally amend the Acceptable Use Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice, contradicting the MSA requirement that changes be agreed in writing by both parties and the Change Control Procedure. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 8.1–8.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 2.4; 08_change_control.md cl. 1.1

Provider may disclose Customer content to authorities and is not obliged to notify Customer at any time, conflicting with the processor's duty to act only on documented instructions and to flag infringing instructions, and with the controller's own compliance obligations. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 6.1–6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 2.2–2.3

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 states the MSA prevails over any Schedule, while SOW 1 (Schedule 1) clause 1.2 states the SOW prevails over the MSA. Each document claims priority over the other. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Three-way circular/conflicting precedence: the Order Form claims to prevail over every other document, the MSA claims to prevail over Schedules and Addenda, the SOW claims to prevail over the MSA, and the Glossary claims its definitions prevail over all other documents. No coherent hierarchy can be derived. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1-2.2; 01_msa.md cl. 14.2; 02_sow.md cl. 1.2; 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2

Reference to a non-existent section: MSA clause 6.2 requires acceptance criteria in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but Statement of Work 1 (Schedule 1) has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl. 6.2

Reference to a non-existent clause: Change Control Procedure cl. 4.1 refers to a 'Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and describes no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.1
Reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan cl. 5.3 refers to the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl. 5.3
Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA cl. 7.4 points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl. 7.4

Reference to a non-existent exhibit: Pricing Schedule cl. 2.4 refers to role-specific rates 'in Exhibit B', but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule; no Exhibit B exists to Schedule 7. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.4

Reference to a non-existent rate: Change Control cl. 7.2 says impact-assessment preparation is charged 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan'; the Exit Plan sets only a transition-assistance rate (£1,250/day) and contains no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl. 7.2

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA); Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA); Monday-Friday including public holidays (Glossary). All time limits measured in Business Days are indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl. 1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 1.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

'Confidential Information' defined two ways: MSA limits it to information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; the Glossary covers all information whether or not marked and whether oral or written. 01_msa.md cl. 11.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

'Deliverable' defined two ways: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; the Glossary extends it to any output of the Services whether or not so identified. 01_msa.md cl. 1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

'Fee' defined two ways: MSA limits it to amounts payable under clause 4 (the monthly Fee); the Glossary includes all amounts including T&M and expenses. This changes the size of the liability cap in MSA cl. 13.1 and of service credit percentages calculated on 'the monthly Fee'. 01_msa.md cl. 1.4 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

Exhibit B role rates conflict with the Pricing Schedule: Pricing cl. 1.3 fixes charges for the initial term and cl. 2.4 defers to role-specific rates in 'Exhibit B', but Exhibit B cl. 3.2 says rates are held only for the initial term and reviewed annually, and Pricing cl. 7.1 requires annual rate card review — no single governing mechanism. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 3.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3/2.4/7.1

SOW cl. 3.1 requires not fewer than eleven FTE, but cl. 3.2's enumerated composition also totals eleven, leaving no margin; Exhibit B cl. 4.2 obliges Provider to 'maintain the team size committed in the Statement of Work' without reconciling the minimum with substitution and handover overlaps. 02_sow.md cl. 3.1-3.2 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 4.2

SOW cl. 3.3 requires the delivery lead to be available during 'Customer's working hours', a term never defined anywhere in the contract set, and inconsistent with the Bengaluru base location in cl. 3.4. 02_sow.md cl. 3.3-3.4

SOW cl. 10.3's assumption of no more than three legacy interfaces requiring bespoke adapters has no stated consequence if exceeded and no link to the Change Control Procedure, leaving the assumption unenforceable. 02_sow.md cl. 10.3

DPA cl. 11.2's mutual indemnity for fines 'imposed on it as a result of the other's breach' is legally unworkable as regulators impose fines on the controller for its own compliance failures, and it conflicts with cl. 11.1's blanket disapplication of limitations. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.2

MSA cl. 10.2's SOC 2 report obligation conflicts with InfoSec cl. 7.1-7.2 (annual penetration test report sharing) and cl. 6.3 (incident register availability) which grant Customer assurance rights the MSA purports to exclude. 01_msa.md cl. 10.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 6.3/7.2

Exit Plan cl. 9.2 requires a desk-based exit rehearsal 'at least once in the term' but with a 12-month Order Form term and 24-month MSA term it is unclear which term applies; cl. 9.3's one-month report deadline also conflicts with the Business Day-based deadlines used elsewhere. 09_exit.md cl. 9.2-9.3

Pricing cl. 5.2 sets an overage rate per transaction but no document allocates responsibility for measuring or disputing transaction volumes beyond Provider's own report, and volume overages are outside the 'fixed for the initial term' assurance in cl. 1.3. 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3 vs 5.1-5.3

Subprocessor Schedule cl. 3.3 lets Provider proceed over Customer's reasonable data protection objection with only a right to terminate 'the affected Services', which contradicts DPA cl. 5.1's absolute consent requirement and cl. 4.2's prior authorisation requirement for transfers. 12_subprocessors.md cl. 3.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 5.1

Larkfield Support Partners provides the out-of-hours service desk, which is inconsistent with SLA cl. 2.2 limiting Priority 2/3 support to business hours and with Order Form cl. 3.2 naming Provider's own service desk as the support contact. 12_subprocessors.md s.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 2.2 / 05_order_form.md cl. 3.2

SLA availability of 99.9% monthly permits roughly 43 minutes of downtime, which is inconsistent with the SLA's own 4-hour Priority 1 Resolution target — a single Priority 1 incident resolved within target breaches the availability commitment. 04_sla.md cl. 3.1 vs 5.1

InfoSec cl. 8.3 requires access revocation within one Business Day of a leaver's last working day, which for offshore Bengaluru personnel and the disputed Business Day definitions can exceed the DPA's security expectations and the InfoSec least-privilege principle. 06_infosec.md cl. 8.3

No document identifies a Statement of Work 2 or further SOWs despite MSA cl. 2.1 contemplating 'one or more Statements of Work' and Glossary defining Services by reference to 'a Statement of Work', leaving the Order Form's 'ongoing platform operation' scope unsupported by any SOW. 05_order_form.md cl. 1.1 vs 02_sow.md (replatforming only)
unmatched: Reference to a non-existent exhibit: Pricing Schedule cl. 2.4 refers to role-specific rates 'in Exhibit B', but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule; no Exhibit B exists to Schedule 7. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.4
Conflicting assessment periods: SOW cl. 6.3 gives Customer 5 Business Days to respond; Exhibit A cl. 5.2/5.4 gives 15 Business Days. 02_sow.md cl. 6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.2

Conflicting expense approval thresholds: SOW cl. 5.4 requires prior written approval for any expense outside the Fee, while Pricing cl. 3.2 requires approval only where expenses exceed £500 in a month; SOW cl. 5.2 also states the Fee covers all travel, contradicting the travel expense provisions. 02_sow.md cl. 5.2/5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 3.1-3.2

Conflicting record retention for change log and service reports: Change Control cl. 9.3 and SLA cl. 6.3 require retention only for the duration of the Agreement, contradicting MSA cl. 12.4's 7-year post-termination retention. 08_change_control.md cl. 9.3 / 04_sla.md cl. 6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

Confidentiality survival mismatch: MSA cl. 11.3 limits confidentiality obligations to 3 years post-termination, but DPA cl. 1.4 makes all Customer Personal Data Confidential Information and Data Protection Law obligations are indefinite; the 3-year cut-off would end protection for personal data still held under the 7-year retention obligation. 01_msa.md cl. 11.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4 / 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

SLA cl. 5.4 measures response and resolution from Provider's own acknowledgement in its tool rather than from Incident report, allowing Provider to control the clock and rendering the cl. 5.1 15-minute response target circular/meaningless. 04_sla.md cl. 5.4

InfoSec cl. 2.1 lets Provider's CISO unilaterally determine data locations and cl. 2.3 permits notifying Customer of a new region up to 30 days after it enters service, directly contradicting DPA cl. 4.2 requiring Customer's prior written authorisation for any transfer. 06_infosec.md cl. 2.1/2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.2

InfoSec cl. 3.1 requires encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, whereas DPA cl. 7.2 requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data (much of which would be classified Internal Data). 06_infosec.md cl. 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 7.2

Acceptable Use Policy cl. 6.2 permits disclosure to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer, conflicting with MSA cl. 11.2 confidentiality obligations and DPA cl. 2.2/6.3 requirements to act only on Customer instructions and to keep Customer informed. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 2.2 / 01_msa.md cl. 11.2

Exit Plan cl. 3.4 requires Customer approval of the effort estimate before assistance begins, which can block the mandatory transition assistance and the fixed Annex 1 milestones; no fallback if Customer withholds approval. 09_exit.md cl. 3.4 vs Annex 1

Pricing cl. 6.1 requires invoices on the first Business Day of each month, which is incompatible with invoicing 'in arrears' as required by the MSA, SOW and Order Form for a month not yet complete, and with the volume-based charges in s.5 that can only be computed after month end. 10_pricing.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3 / 10_pricing.md s.5

Glossary cl. 4.1 makes the Glossary maintained by Provider's Commercial Director and cl. 4.2 subjects additions to change control, yet cl. 1.2 gives Glossary definitions overriding force — allowing one party's document owner to override negotiated definitions. 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2 vs 4.1

MSA cl. 6.2 requires Customer to assess Deliverables against Schedule 1 criteria but cl. 6.1 and 6.3 provide no time limit for Customer's assessment or rejection, leaving acceptance open-ended and conflicting with the deemed-acceptance and fixed-period provisions elsewhere. 01_msa.md cl. 6.1-6.3

MSA cl. 2.3 obliges Provider to comply with Customer's reasonable instructions on the manner of performance, which conflicts with the Change Control Procedure requiring formal Change Requests for any change to scope, timetable or acceptance criteria and with Provider's unilateral discretion elsewhere. 01_msa.md cl. 2.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 1.1

DPA cl. 6.1 requires notification of any Security Incident within 24 hours of awareness while cl. 6.2 requires the notification to include categories and approximate numbers of affected data subjects — information typically unavailable within 24 hours, and no provision for phased notification. 03_dpa.md cl. 6.1-6.2

Named contacts are inconsistent: Order Form cl. 4.1 names the Head of Procurement as commercial contact but cl. 7.1 has the Chief Procurement Officer sign; MSA cl. 5.2 requires a single point of contact while the Order Form names four contacts and the BCDR/SLA refer to separate 'nominated technical contact' and 'nominated security contact' not identified anywhere. 05_order_form.md ss. 4, 7 vs 01_msa.md cl. 5.2 / 04_sla.md cl. 7.3 / 07_bcdr.md cl. 4.2

Governance cadence conflict: InfoSec cl. 6.3 refers to a 'quarterly security review' and Subprocessor Schedule cl. 6.1 to review at the quarterly steering committee, but no security review is established in the SOW governance section, which provides only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee. 06_infosec.md cl. 6.3 vs 02_sow.md s.8

InfoSec cl. 7.4 requires remediation of critical findings within 30 days while cl. 9.1 requires critical patches within 14 days — overlapping and inconsistent deadlines for the same class of critical vulnerability. 06_infosec.md cl. 7.4 vs 9.1

Exhibit A criterion 3.2 refers to 'the requirements register' and 3.3 to 'the agreed functional test pack', neither of which is defined or produced by any document in the set. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 3.2-3.3

SOW cl. 6.1 makes the Deliverables list a document unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead, contradicting Exhibit A's fixed Deliverable table D1-D7 and the requirement that changes to deliverables go through change control. 02_sow.md cl. 6.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md s.2

SOW cl. 6.4 requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, whereas Exhibit A cl. 5.4 imposes no resubmission deadline but a fresh 15 Business Day assessment — inconsistent remediation cycles. 02_sow.md cl. 6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.4

Exhibit B role rates conflict with the Pricing Schedule: Pricing cl. 1.3 fixes charges for the initial term and cl. 2.4 defers to role-specific rates in 'Exhibit B', but Exhibit B cl. 3.2 says rates are held only for the initial term and reviewed annually, and Pricing cl. 7.1 requires annual rate card review — no single governing mechanism. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 3.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3/2.4/7.1

SOW cl. 3.1 requires not fewer than eleven FTE, but cl. 3.2's enumerated composition also totals eleven, leaving no margin; Exhibit B cl. 4.2 obliges Provider to 'maintain the team size committed in the Statement of Work' without reconciling the minimum with substitution and handover overlaps. 02_sow.md cl. 3.1-3.2 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 4.2

SOW cl. 10.3's assumption of no more than three legacy interfaces requiring bespoke adapters has no stated consequence if exceeded and no link to the Change Control Procedure, leaving the assumption unenforceable. 02_sow.md cl. 10.3

Larkfield Support Partners provides the out-of-hours service desk, which is inconsistent with SLA cl. 2.2 limiting Priority 2/3 support to business hours and with Order Form cl. 3.2 naming Provider's own service desk as the support contact. 12_subprocessors.md s.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 2.2 / 05_order_form.md cl. 3.2

No document identifies a Statement of Work 2 or further SOWs despite MSA cl. 2.1 contemplating 'one or more Statements of Work' and Glossary defining Services by reference to 'a Statement of Work', leaving the Order Form's 'ongoing platform operation' scope unsupported by any SOW. 05_order_form.md cl. 1.1 vs 02_sow.md (replatforming only)
