findings: Circular order of precedence: the MSA says it prevails over Schedules/Addenda, the SoW (Schedule 1) says it prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says it prevails over everything, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over every other document. No consistent hierarchy can be derived. MSA cl. 14.2; SoW cl. 1.2; Order Form cl. 2.1–2.2; Glossary cl. 1.2

"Business Day" is defined three incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays; and Monday–Friday including public holidays. Every deadline expressed in Business Days is therefore indeterminate. MSA cl. 1.2; SLA cl. 1.1; Glossary s.2 ("Business Day")

"Confidential Information" defined two ways: only information marked confidential at disclosure (MSA) versus any information whether or not marked and whether oral or written (Glossary); the DPA adds a third rule for personal data. MSA cl. 11.1; Glossary s.2; DPA cl. 1.4

"Security Incident" defined three incompatible ways: any unauthorised access/loss etc. of Customer Personal Data (DPA); only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data (SLA); and any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform (Glossary). The SLA definition is narrower than, and the Glossary definition far broader than, the DPA definition. DPA cl. 1.6; SLA cl. 7.1; Glossary s.2

Three conflicting security-incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy), 72 hours (SLA). All three cannot be satisfied as drafted and the documents do not reconcile them. DPA cl. 6.1; InfoSec cl. 6.1; SLA cl. 7.3

Four different recurring charges for the same Services: £12,400/month (MSA), £12,800/month (SoW), £13,100/month (Pricing Schedule), and an Annual Contract Value of £153,600 (= £12,800/month) in the Order Form. MSA cl. 4.1; SoW cl. 5.1; Pricing cl. 1.1; Order Form cl. 1.4
Three conflicting payment terms: 30 days from receipt of invoice (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SoW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). MSA cl. 4.3; SoW cl. 5.3; Order Form cl. 1.6

Billing direction conflict: MSA, SoW and Order Form require invoicing monthly in arrears; the Pricing Schedule states the recurring charge is invoiced monthly in advance on the first Business Day of the month. MSA cl. 4.3; SoW cl. 5.3; Order Form cl. 1.5 vs Pricing cl. 1.2, 6.1

Indexation conflict: the MSA permits an annual CPI-linked fee increase on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing Schedule states the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or any other increase. MSA cl. 4.4 vs Pricing cl. 1.3

Term conflict: MSA initial term 24 months; Order Form initial term 12 months; SoW commits to a 36-month programme. The programme cannot be completed within either contractual term. MSA cl. 3.1; Order Form cl. 1.2; SoW cl. 2.1

Start-date conflict: the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SoW programme is stated to commence on 1 March 2027 — a month before the Agreement under which it is issued exists. MSA (Effective Date); Order Form cl. 1.3 vs SoW cl. 2.2

The Order Form is dated 12 March 2027 and is stated to be made "under" the MSA, whose Effective Date is 1 April 2027; the Order Form therefore purports to be executed under an agreement not yet in effect. Order Form cl. 7.3 vs MSA (Effective Date)

Termination notice conflict: 90 days' notice for convenience (MSA), 30 days for the SoW, and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form, with the Order Form claiming precedence. Terminating the 12-month Order Form on 30 days' notice would also strand the 36-month SoW. MSA cl. 3.3; SoW cl. 2.3; Order Form cl. 6.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA requires express written acceptance and expressly excludes deemed acceptance; the SoW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence; Exhibit A requires a signed acceptance certificate within a 15 Business Day window and states silence is not acceptance. MSA cl. 6.1; SoW cl. 6.3 vs Exhibit A cl. 5.2–5.3

Broken cross-reference: the MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria "set out in Schedule 1, Section 12", but the SoW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria. MSA cl. 6.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflict: the SoW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the Provider's delivery lead, while Exhibit A states it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria (and the MSA points to a non-existent SoW Section 12). SoW cl. 6.1 vs Exhibit A cl. 1.2, s.2–3; MSA cl. 6.2

Resubmission timetable conflict: SoW requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days with a 5 Business Day review cycle; Exhibit A applies a fresh 15 Business Day assessment period per submission. SoW cl. 6.4 vs Exhibit A cl. 5.4
Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) versus 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). MSA cl. 8.2 vs Exhibit A cl. 7.1
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly (SoW) versus 99.9% monthly (SLA) for the same platform. SoW cl. 7.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1

Service credit cap stated three ways: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SoW), not more than 10% of the monthly Fee (SLA), and not more than 5% of the recurring monthly charge (Pricing). SoW cl. 7.4; SLA cl. 4.2; Pricing cl. 4.2

Service credits are calculated on different bases ("monthly Fee" vs "recurring monthly charge"), and the Glossary redefines "Fee" to include time-and-materials charges and expenses, changing the credit calculation and the liability cap from what the MSA intended. SoW cl. 7.4; SLA cl. 4.2; Pricing cl. 4.2; Glossary s.2 ("Fee") vs MSA cl. 1.4, 13.1

Service level commencement conflict: the Order Form applies service levels from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027), while the SoW applies them only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme). Order Form cl. 3.3 vs SoW cl. 7.1
Support coverage conflict: the Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; the SLA restricts Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl. 3.1 vs SLA cl. 2.2

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and states that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum; the SoW caps Provider liability at £250,000; and the DPA disapplies all limitations of liability for breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law. MSA cl. 13.1, 13.3 vs SoW cl. 9.2 vs DPA cl. 11.1
Insurance conflict: professional indemnity cover of not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) versus not less than £2,000,000 (SoW). MSA cl. 16.1 vs SoW cl. 9.4

Audit rights conflict: the MSA states that on delivery of a SOC 2 report Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records, and the InfoSec Policy/Subprocessor Schedule contemplate reviews and evidence sharing. MSA cl. 10.2 vs DPA cl. 9.1–9.3

Internal defect: the MSA requires Provider to make records available to Customer "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 removes any right of inspection — the obligation is self-cancelling. MSA cl. 12.2 (read with cl. 10.2)

Subcontracting/subprocessing conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent; the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor; the Subprocessor Schedule allows additions on 30 days' notice (and immediate replacement with notice afterwards). MSA cl. 9.3 vs DPA cl. 5.1 vs Subprocessor List cl. 3.1, 3.4

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK and EEA, but the SoW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India (with system access under MSA cl. 5.1), the Subprocessor List includes a Singapore analytics subprocessor, and the InfoSec Policy allows storage in any Provider region as determined by Provider's CISO with notice only 30 days after the region enters service. DPA cl. 4.1–4.2 vs SoW cl. 3.4; Subprocessor List s.2 (Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd); InfoSec cl. 2.1, 2.3

Approved-locations conflict: DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations, but the BCDR Plan operates the recovery environment in Frankfurt, Germany, and the Subprocessor List includes Manchester and Singapore locations. DPA Annex 2 vs BCDR cl. 3.1; Subprocessor List s.2

Annex numbering conflict: the Subprocessor Schedule declares itself to be "Annex 2 to the Data Processing Addendum", but the DPA already contains an Annex 2 (approved processing locations) and cl. 4.3 relies on that content. Subprocessor List (preamble) vs DPA cl. 4.3 and Annex 2
Reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum" for security escalation contacts; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. SLA cl. 7.4

Reference to a non-existent clause and body: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17"; the MSA ends at clause 16 and establishes no Change Control Board. Change Control cl. 4.1
Reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan refers to "the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14"; the DPA's final clause is 13. Exit Plan cl. 5.3

Reference to a rate that does not exist: the Change Control Procedure charges for impact assessments "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", which contains only a transition-assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate. Change Control cl. 7.2 vs Exit Plan cl. 3.2

Rate inconsistency: the transition-assistance rate is £1,250 per person per day while the Pricing Schedule standard rate is £1,450 per person per day and Exhibit B role rates range from £950 to £1,450, with no stated relationship or discount basis. Exit Plan cl. 3.2 vs Pricing cl. 2.1; Exhibit B s.3

Change approval conflict: the MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while the Change Control Procedure provides for deemed approval after 10 Business Days' silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes implemented without prior approval. MSA cl. 2.4 vs Change Control cl. 4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Internal timing conflict: escalation of a Change Request disagreement allows 5 Business Days at each of three levels (15 Business Days) while expressly not suspending the timetable, yet the change is deemed approved if Customer does not respond within 10 Business Days — a change can be deemed approved while it is still being disputed. Change Control cl. 4.2 vs cl. 8.1–8.3

Change-charge conflict: the Change Control Procedure states change-related charges are exempt from notice requirements for ordinary increases and apply from the next invoice, while the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no increase of any kind. Change Control cl. 5.1, 5.3 vs Pricing cl. 1.3

Data retention/deletion conflicts that cannot all be satisfied: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days and continued Service provision for 6 months post-termination; the InfoSec Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. MSA cl. 12.4 vs DPA cl. 8.2 vs Exit Plan cl. 2.1–2.3, 5.2 vs InfoSec cl. 5.2

Record retention conflict: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only "for the duration of the Agreement" and the Change Control Procedure the same for the change log, both shorter than the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation. SLA cl. 6.3; Change Control cl. 9.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Exit deliverables cannot be met if personal data has already been deleted: the exit milestone for the data extract is T+30 Business Days (≈6 weeks) and handover completes at the end of the 6-month transition period, both after the DPA's 30-day deletion deadline. Exit Plan Annex 1 (milestones 2 and 5); cl. 4.1(a) vs DPA cl. 8.2

Governing law conflict, internally and with the MSA: the DPA says it is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement "save as provided in clause 13.2", and cl. 13.2 then applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland, contradicting the MSA's England and Wales governing law and exclusive jurisdiction. DPA cl. 13.1–13.2 vs MSA cl. 15.1–15.2

Internal defect: response and resolution times are measured from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the response-time targets self-fulfilling and gives Provider unilateral control over the clock start. SLA cl. 5.4 (read with cl. 5.1–5.3)

Internal inconsistency: a Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident (15-minute response, 4-hour resolution) yet notification to Customer's security contact is allowed up to 72 hours after confirmation. SLA cl. 7.2 vs cl. 7.3

Internal inconsistency: Priority 2 resolution is required within one Business Day although Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, so a target measured in elapsed Business Days cannot be met with the stated coverage for incidents raised late in the day. SLA cl. 2.2 vs cl. 5.2

Recovery objective conflicts with the SLA: the BCDR Plan sets an 8-hour RTO from Invocation, while the SLA requires resolution of a Priority 1 Incident (wholly unavailable platform) within 4 hours. BCDR cl. 2.1 vs SLA cl. 5.1

The BCDR Plan unilaterally suspends all SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes Continuity Event and failback downtime from the availability calculation, whereas the SLA contains a closed list of exclusions (Customer equipment, third-party outages, agreed maintenance windows) that does not include these. BCDR cl. 5.1, 5.3 vs SLA cl. 3.3, 9.1–9.3

The BCDR Plan permits up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on return to the primary environment without complying with the SLA's requirement of 5 Business Days' notice for maintenance windows, and 12 hours of downtime is irreconcilable with a 99.9% monthly availability commitment (≈43 minutes). BCDR cl. 5.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1, 3.4

A 24-hour RPO (i.e. up to 24 hours of tolerated data loss) is inconsistent with the DPA/InfoSec integrity commitments and with the SLA's treatment of data loss as a Priority 1 Security Incident; no reconciliation is provided. BCDR cl. 2.2 vs SLA cl. 7.1–7.2; InfoSec cl. 7.1

Team location conflict: the SoW states the entire delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. SoW cl. 3.4 vs Exhibit B s.1 table

Key personnel substitution conflict: the SoW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement; Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediately in stated circumstances. SoW cl. 3.5 vs Exhibit B cl. 2.1, 2.4

Unilateral amendment of Schedules conflicts with the MSA: the Acceptable Use Policy may be amended by Provider on 30 days' notice, the InfoSec Policy is reviewed and changed by Provider with notice only, and the Glossary is maintained by Provider's Commercial Director — yet a Schedule is defined as a document executed by both parties and all changes must be agreed in writing. AUP cl. 8.1; InfoSec cl. 10.1–10.2; Glossary cl. 4.1 vs MSA cl. 1.6, 2.4

The AUP permits Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement or regulators with no obligation to notify Customer before or after, conflicting with the DPA requirements to process only on Customer's documented instructions and to notify/obtain approval in relation to disclosures of Customer Personal Data. AUP cl. 6.1–6.2 vs DPA cl. 2.2, 6.3

Suspension under the AUP causes unavailability and continued charges, but suspension is not among the SLA's exclusions from the availability calculation, so Provider would incur service credits for its own contractual suspension. AUP cl. 5.1, 5.4 vs SLA cl. 9.1–9.3

Data classification conflict: the InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data to be held on Provider systems, while the AUP prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform (and a payment tokenisation subprocessor is engaged). InfoSec cl. 1.2 vs AUP cl. 3.2; Subprocessor List s.2 (Ashcombe Payments Ltd)

Remediation timing inconsistency within the InfoSec Policy: critical penetration-test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for overlapping critical items. InfoSec cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

Duplicative and inconsistent incident reporting: the SLA requires root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution while the InfoSec Policy requires a written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident, for what may be the same incident, with no reconciliation. SLA cl. 8.1 vs InfoSec cl. 6.2

"Agreement" defined two ways: the MSA defines it as the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda (omitting the Order Form and Exhibits), while the Glossary includes the Order Form and every Exhibit. MSA cl. 1.1 vs Glossary s.2 ("Agreement")

"Deliverable" defined two ways: an item identified as a deliverable in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary), which expands IP assignment, acceptance and warranty obligations. MSA cl. 1.3 vs Glossary s.2 ("Deliverable")

"Services" defined two ways: the services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus those services plus the support services in the SLA (Glossary), affecting the scope of fees, service levels and termination. MSA cl. 1.5 vs Glossary s.2 ("Services")

"Subprocessor" defined inconsistently: a third party engaged to process Customer Personal Data (DPA) versus one engaged to process Personal Data generally (Glossary), and "Personal Data" is defined only in the Glossary while the DPA uses "Customer Personal Data" and "Data Protection Law". DPA cl. 1.1, 1.5 vs Glossary s.2 ("Subprocessor", "Personal Data")

Confidentiality survival conflict: MSA confidentiality obligations end 3 years after termination, yet Provider must retain records and data (all of which include Confidential Information and personal data deemed confidential) for 7 years. MSA cl. 11.3 vs cl. 12.4; DPA cl. 1.4

Internal gap: the Exit Plan applies however the Agreement ends, but the transition period is defined as beginning on the date notice of termination is given — leaving no start date where the Agreement ends by expiry or non-renewal. Exit Plan cl. 1.2 vs cl. 2.1

Exit assistance can be blocked by the party it protects: Provider need not begin assistance until Customer approves the effort estimate, which conflicts with the unqualified obligation to provide transition assistance and with the fixed exit milestones. Exit Plan cl. 3.1, 3.4 vs Annex 1 milestones

Continued Service provision for 6 months after termination conflicts with the MSA right to terminate immediately for unremedied material breach and with the AUP right to suspend the Services, and no charging basis for post-termination Services is agreed (Pricing fixes charges only for the initial term). Exit Plan cl. 2.1–2.2 vs MSA cl. 3.4; AUP cl. 5.1; Pricing cl. 1.3

Exit deliverable format is inadequate and inconsistent with the DPA: data is to be returned "in the format used by Provider's systems", whereas the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. Exit Plan cl. 4.1(a) vs DPA cl. 8.1

Cross-document reporting inconsistency: the Pricing Schedule requires actual transaction volumes to be reported in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents do not include volumes. Pricing cl. 5.3 vs SLA cl. 6.2

Service credit mechanics conflict: the SLA requires credits to be applied automatically to the next invoice and treats them as the sole financial remedy, while the SoW frames credits as an entitlement of up to 25% and the Pricing Schedule imposes a different cap and a no-carry-forward rule; the DPA also disapplies exclusive remedies for data protection breaches. SLA cl. 4.1–4.3; SoW cl. 7.4; Pricing cl. 4.1–4.3; DPA cl. 11.1

Imprecise cross-reference: the Pricing Schedule (Schedule 7) refers to role-specific rates "in Exhibit B" without identifying that Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, and the two documents' rate structures overlap (£1,450 standard rate vs £1,450–£950 role rates) without a stated priority. Pricing cl. 2.4 vs Exhibit B s.3

Rate review conflict: the Pricing Schedule requires review of the rate card at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date, while Exhibit B holds rates for the initial term and reviews annually only thereafter; "Service Commencement Date" is defined only in the Order Form and not in the Glossary. Pricing cl. 7.1 vs Exhibit B cl. 3.2; Glossary s.2

The Glossary's broad "Security Incident" definition would make every availability event a Security Incident, triggering the DPA's 24-hour notification and the SLA's Priority 1 treatment for ordinary service faults — an unworkable interaction with the SLA priority scheme. Glossary s.2 ("Security Incident") vs SLA cl. 1.3–1.5, 7.2; DPA cl. 6.1

Governance body inconsistency: escalation paths differ across documents (delivery lead / account director / executive sponsor in the SoW; Delivery Lead / Programme Director / Chief Information Officer in Change Control), and roles such as Programme Director and Chief Information Officer are not defined or named anywhere. SoW cl. 8.3 vs Change Control cl. 8.1; Order Form s.4

The Glossary requires any addition to it to go through Change Control, but Change Control allows Provider's Delivery Lead to approve unilaterally any change whose cost impact is under £35,000 — permitting Provider to change prevailing definitions without Customer agreement. Glossary cl. 4.2 vs Change Control cl. 4.3

Programme end date exceeds the contract term: a 36-month programme commencing 1 March 2027 ends in February 2030, beyond the MSA's 24-month initial term (ending 31 March 2029) and far beyond the Order Form's 12-month initial term, with no obligation to renew. SoW cl. 2.1–2.2, s.4 vs MSA cl. 3.1; Order Form cl. 1.2

The DPA mutual indemnity for regulatory fines conflicts with the MSA liability cap and with the DPA's own disapplication of all limitations, leaving uncapped, overlapping and potentially unenforceable indemnity exposure. DPA cl. 11.1–11.2 vs MSA cl. 13.1, 13.3

Subprocessor transfer clause is narrower than the DPA: it requires a transfer mechanism only where a Subprocessor is located outside the United Kingdom, ignoring the DPA's UK-and-EEA permission and its requirement for prior written authorisation for any transfer beyond those territories. Subprocessor List cl. 5.1 vs DPA cl. 4.1–4.2

Subprocessor list is maintained and published unilaterally by Provider and reviewed at a quarterly steering committee, which is inconsistent with the DPA's requirement for specific prior written consent to each Subprocessor and with the MSA's requirement that Schedules be executed by both parties. Subprocessor List cl. 1.2, 6.1 vs DPA cl. 5.1; MSA cl. 1.6

Vetting cross-reference mismatch: Exhibit B states all personnel are vetted under the Information Security Policy, but the Policy requires criminal-record checks that may be unavailable for the Bengaluru-based team, and no jurisdictional carve-out or standard is specified. Exhibit B cl. 5.1; InfoSec cl. 8.1 vs SoW cl. 3.4

Internal inconsistency in acceptance criteria: D4 must migrate a sample with zero record loss while D5 permits a reconciliation variance of up to 0.01%, and no criteria are given for the availability, security or performance requirements imposed elsewhere. Exhibit A cl. 3.4–3.5

Exhibit A allows acceptance with Minor Defects outstanding on a mere Provider commitment to a remediation date, with no remediation deadline or remedy, and no linkage to the MSA's obligation to correct rejected Deliverables at no charge. Exhibit A cl. 4.3 vs MSA cl. 6.3

Provider's delivery lead is required to be available during Customer's working hours (England) while the team, and in the SoW the delivery lead, operate from Bengaluru — a time-zone obligation that conflicts with Exhibit B's London basing and full-time dedication commitment. SoW cl. 3.3–3.4 vs Exhibit B s.1, cl. 1.2

No-set-off clause conflicts with the automatic application of service credits as deductions from invoices, since credits are applied by Provider as deductions/withholdings without Customer claim. MSA cl. 4.5 vs SLA cl. 4.1; Pricing cl. 4.1

Provider is required to notify Customer of a new processing region only within 30 days after it enters service, which is inconsistent with the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation before any transfer or change of location. InfoSec cl. 2.3 vs DPA cl. 4.2

The InfoSec Policy makes the Provider's own CISO the sole arbiter of whether a region has "equivalent security controls" and of access approval to Restricted Data, giving Provider unilateral control over obligations the DPA reserves to Customer. InfoSec cl. 2.1, 4.2 vs DPA cl. 2.2, 4.2
unmatched: Resubmission timetable conflict: SoW requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days with a 5 Business Day review cycle; Exhibit A applies a fresh 15 Business Day assessment period per submission. SoW cl. 6.4 vs Exhibit A cl. 5.4

Internal defect: the MSA requires Provider to make records available to Customer "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 removes any right of inspection — the obligation is self-cancelling. MSA cl. 12.2 (read with cl. 10.2)

Record retention conflict: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only "for the duration of the Agreement" and the Change Control Procedure the same for the change log, both shorter than the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation. SLA cl. 6.3; Change Control cl. 9.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Exit deliverables cannot be met if personal data has already been deleted: the exit milestone for the data extract is T+30 Business Days (≈6 weeks) and handover completes at the end of the 6-month transition period, both after the DPA's 30-day deletion deadline. Exit Plan Annex 1 (milestones 2 and 5); cl. 4.1(a) vs DPA cl. 8.2

Internal defect: response and resolution times are measured from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the response-time targets self-fulfilling and gives Provider unilateral control over the clock start. SLA cl. 5.4 (read with cl. 5.1–5.3)

Internal inconsistency: Priority 2 resolution is required within one Business Day although Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, so a target measured in elapsed Business Days cannot be met with the stated coverage for incidents raised late in the day. SLA cl. 2.2 vs cl. 5.2

Suspension under the AUP causes unavailability and continued charges, but suspension is not among the SLA's exclusions from the availability calculation, so Provider would incur service credits for its own contractual suspension. AUP cl. 5.1, 5.4 vs SLA cl. 9.1–9.3

Remediation timing inconsistency within the InfoSec Policy: critical penetration-test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for overlapping critical items. InfoSec cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

Duplicative and inconsistent incident reporting: the SLA requires root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution while the InfoSec Policy requires a written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident, for what may be the same incident, with no reconciliation. SLA cl. 8.1 vs InfoSec cl. 6.2

"Services" defined two ways: the services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) versus those services plus the support services in the SLA (Glossary), affecting the scope of fees, service levels and termination. MSA cl. 1.5 vs Glossary s.2 ("Services")

"Subprocessor" defined inconsistently: a third party engaged to process Customer Personal Data (DPA) versus one engaged to process Personal Data generally (Glossary), and "Personal Data" is defined only in the Glossary while the DPA uses "Customer Personal Data" and "Data Protection Law". DPA cl. 1.1, 1.5 vs Glossary s.2 ("Subprocessor", "Personal Data")

Internal gap: the Exit Plan applies however the Agreement ends, but the transition period is defined as beginning on the date notice of termination is given — leaving no start date where the Agreement ends by expiry or non-renewal. Exit Plan cl. 1.2 vs cl. 2.1

Exit assistance can be blocked by the party it protects: Provider need not begin assistance until Customer approves the effort estimate, which conflicts with the unqualified obligation to provide transition assistance and with the fixed exit milestones. Exit Plan cl. 3.1, 3.4 vs Annex 1 milestones

Continued Service provision for 6 months after termination conflicts with the MSA right to terminate immediately for unremedied material breach and with the AUP right to suspend the Services, and no charging basis for post-termination Services is agreed (Pricing fixes charges only for the initial term). Exit Plan cl. 2.1–2.2 vs MSA cl. 3.4; AUP cl. 5.1; Pricing cl. 1.3

Cross-document reporting inconsistency: the Pricing Schedule requires actual transaction volumes to be reported in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents do not include volumes. Pricing cl. 5.3 vs SLA cl. 6.2

Rate review conflict: the Pricing Schedule requires review of the rate card at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date, while Exhibit B holds rates for the initial term and reviews annually only thereafter; "Service Commencement Date" is defined only in the Order Form and not in the Glossary. Pricing cl. 7.1 vs Exhibit B cl. 3.2; Glossary s.2

Exhibit A allows acceptance with Minor Defects outstanding on a mere Provider commitment to a remediation date, with no remediation deadline or remedy, and no linkage to the MSA's obligation to correct rejected Deliverables at no charge. Exhibit A cl. 4.3 vs MSA cl. 6.3

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 clause 1.2 says the Statement of Work (which is Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA. The two cannot both operate. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Three-way circular precedence: the Order Form claims to prevail over everything, the MSA claims to prevail over all Schedules/Addenda, the SOW claims to prevail over the MSA, and the Glossary (itself a Schedule) claims its definitions prevail over every other document. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1–2.2; 01_msa.md cl. 14.2; 02_sow.md cl. 1.2; 15_glossary.md cl. 1.2

Order Form precedence table is internally inconsistent with its own ranking: 2.1 ranks the Order Form above the MSA but the MSA at 14.2 and 13.3 asserts overriding effect; also 2.2 restates absolute priority making the ranked list in 2.1 redundant/conflicting. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1 and 2.2

"Business Day" is defined three incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England & Wales public holidays (MSA), Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), and Monday–Friday including public holidays (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl. 1.2; 04_sla.md cl. 1.1; 15_glossary.md s.2

"Confidential Information" defined two ways: MSA limits it to information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; the Glossary covers all information whether or not marked and whether oral or written. The DPA also deems all Customer Personal Data confidential regardless of marking, contradicting the MSA definition. 01_msa.md cl. 11.1; 15_glossary.md s.2; 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4

"Deliverable" defined two ways: MSA restricts it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; the Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. This changes the scope of the IP assignment and warranty. 01_msa.md cl. 1.3; 15_glossary.md s.2

"Fee" defined two ways: MSA limits it to amounts payable under clause 4 (the monthly fee); the Glossary makes it all amounts including T&M and expenses. This distorts the liability cap in MSA 13.1 and the service credit percentages calculated on "monthly Fee". 01_msa.md cl. 1.4; 15_glossary.md s.2

"Security Incident" defined three incompatible ways: DPA (any unauthorised access/loss etc. of personal data), SLA clause 7.1 (only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption), and the Glossary (any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform). 03_dpa.md cl. 1.6; 04_sla.md cl. 7.1; 15_glossary.md s.2
"Services" defined two ways: MSA limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work; the Glossary adds the support services in the SLA. 01_msa.md cl. 1.5; 15_glossary.md s.2

"Agreement" defined two ways: MSA covers the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda (omitting the Order Form and Exhibits); the Glossary includes the Order Form, Exhibits and Addenda. 01_msa.md cl. 1.1; 15_glossary.md s.2
Conflicting monthly fee: MSA states £12,400, SOW 1 states £12,800, and the Pricing Schedule states £13,100. 01_msa.md cl. 4.1; 02_sow.md cl. 5.1; 10_pricing.md cl. 1.1

Order Form Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals £12,800 x 12 (the SOW figure), and is inconsistent with the MSA fee (£148,800) and the Pricing Schedule fee (£157,200). 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.1 and 10_pricing.md cl. 1.1
Conflicting payment terms: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl. 4.3; 02_sow.md cl. 5.3; 05_order_form.md cl. 1.6

Conflicting billing timing: MSA 4.3 and SOW 5.3 and Order Form 1.5 require invoicing monthly in arrears, but the Pricing Schedule requires the recurring charge to be invoiced monthly in advance. 10_pricing.md cl. 1.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3, 02_sow.md cl. 5.3, 05_order_form.md cl. 1.5

Fee indexation conflict: MSA 4.4 allows an annual CPI-linked increase, but Pricing 1.3 fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md cl. 4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 1.3

Conflicting service credit caps for the same failure: SOW allows up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps credits at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps all credits at 5% of the recurring monthly charge. 02_sow.md cl. 7.4; 04_sla.md cl. 4.2; 10_pricing.md cl. 4.2
Conflicting availability commitments for the same platform: 99.5% monthly in the SOW versus 99.9% monthly in the SLA. 02_sow.md cl. 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1

Conflicting start of service levels: SOW says service levels begin at the start of Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl. 7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 3.3

SOW 9.3 excludes liability for indirect and consequential loss, while MSA 13 contains no such exclusion and MSA 13.3 states the MSA cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule — leaving it unclear whether the exclusion has effect. 02_sow.md cl. 9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.3

SOW 9.1 prohibits Provider soliciting Customer personnel "during the programme" only, with no post-termination tail, and there is no reciprocal restriction; the Exit Plan's staff clause (8.1) assumes no transfers but does not address solicitation during a six-month post-termination transition. 02_sow.md cl. 9.1 vs 09_exit.md s.8

MSA 12.4's obligation to retain "all records, data and materials" for 7 years is inconsistent with MSA 7.1 (Customer retains title to its data) and with InfoSec/DPA deletion duties, and would require Provider to hold Customer data long after the confidentiality obligation expires at 3 years. 01_msa.md cl. 12.4 with cl. 7.1 and 11.3

Exit 9.2 requires a desk-based exit rehearsal "at least once in the term" with no deadline, while 9.1 requires annual review and 9.3 a report within one month — no trigger date makes 9.2 unenforceable. 09_exit.md cl. 9.1–9.3

BCDR 6.2 requires 20 Business Days' notice of a test and 7.2 requires Customer participation "where Provider reasonably requests", but 6.1 requires a test once in every 12-month period with no fixed date — combined with the annual review in 9.2 the testing schedule is indeterminate. 07_bcdr.md cl. 6.1–6.2 and 7.2

BCDR 8.2 excludes simultaneous loss of primary and recovery environments from the Plan, but the SLA availability commitment and service credit regime contain no corresponding exclusion in clause 9, leaving Provider strictly liable for an event the Plan disclaims. 07_bcdr.md cl. 8.2 vs 04_sla.md s.9

The contract set contains no defined "Service Commencement Date" other than in the Order Form, yet the term is relied on in Pricing 7.1 and Exhibit B 1.1 — documents that the MSA's precedence clause subordinates to a document (the Order Form) whose definitions are not incorporated by the MSA's definition of Agreement. 10_pricing.md cl. 7.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 1.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.1

The Order Form is not recognised in the MSA's structure: MSA 1.1 and 1.6 contemplate only Schedules and Addenda, and MSA 14.1–14.2 make no mention of an Order Form, so the Order Form's precedence claim has no anchor in the MSA it purports to sit under. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.1, 1.6 and 14.1–14.2

Exhibits A and B are stated to be exhibits to Statement of Work 1 rather than Schedules to the MSA, so under MSA 1.1/1.6 and the Order Form precedence list (which covers only Schedules and Addenda) their contractual rank is undetermined. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md header; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md header vs 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1

Exhibit B 4.2 requires Provider to maintain "the team size committed in the Statement of Work", but Exhibit B's Key Personnel table lists only four roles and SOW 3.2's composition (including six engineers and a business analyst) is not reproduced, so the commitment is unverifiable from Exhibit B alone. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 4.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 3.2

Exhibit B 6.2 gives Provider 20 Business Days to replace an unsatisfactory individual, which conflicts with 2.3's requirement to fund a two-week handover overlap and with 1.2's dedication requirement, and no equivalent right exists for Key Personnel removal under SOW 3.5. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 6.2 with cl. 2.3

Exhibit A 3.7 requires training of at least 20 named staff for D7 acceptance, but the Exit Plan caps free knowledge transfer at 10 sessions and the SOW Fee is said to cover all personnel — no linkage between the training obligation and the charging regime. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 3.7 vs 09_exit.md cl. 6.2

MSA 2.3 requires Provider to comply with Customer's reasonable instructions on manner of performance, which conflicts with MSA 2.4 and the Change Control Procedure requiring formal change control for any alteration to the Services, and with InfoSec 2.1 giving Provider's CISO unilateral determination of data location. 01_msa.md cl. 2.3 vs cl. 2.4 and 06_infosec.md cl. 2.1

AUP 5.4 provides that charges continue to accrue during a Provider-initiated suspension, which conflicts with the availability commitments and service credit entitlements in the SLA and SOW that would otherwise be triggered by the same unavailability. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 5.4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1 and 4.1

AUP 4.1 states Provider does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility for it, contradicting InfoSec 5.1/5.3 (logging all access, continuous monitoring for anomalous access) and DPA 7.2's logging obligations. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 5.1 and 5.3

Change Control 1.1 covers changes to acceptance criteria, but Exhibit A 1.2 declares itself the sole source of acceptance criteria with no amendment mechanism, and the Glossary 4.2 treats definitional additions as changes — three overlapping and unreconciled amendment routes. 08_change_control.md cl. 1.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 1.2 and 15_glossary.md cl. 4.2

Change Control 6.1 lets Provider implement emergency changes without approval, which conflicts with MSA 2.4's absolute requirement for prior bilateral written agreement to any change to the Services. 08_change_control.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 2.4

MSA 3.4 gives 15 days to remedy a material breach, but AUP 9.1 deems a material AUP breach a material breach of the Agreement while AUP 5.1 permits immediate suspension without any cure period — the two remedy regimes are inconsistent. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 5.1 and 9.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.4
unmatched: "Deliverable" defined two ways: MSA restricts it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; the Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. This changes the scope of the IP assignment and warranty. 01_msa.md cl. 1.3; 15_glossary.md s.2
"Services" defined two ways: MSA limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work; the Glossary adds the support services in the SLA. 01_msa.md cl. 1.5; 15_glossary.md s.2

Conflicting assessment periods for Deliverables: 5 Business Days (SOW 6.3) versus 15 Business Days (Exhibit A 5.2/5.4); resubmission period of 10 Business Days in the SOW is not reconciled with Exhibit A's remedy-and-resubmit process. 02_sow.md cl. 6.3–6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 5.2 and 5.4

Sole-remedy conflict: SLA 4.3 makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failures, while SOW 7.4 grants credits as an entitlement without exclusivity and the MSA liability regime contemplates damages claims. 04_sla.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4

Internal inconsistency: MSA 12.2 requires Provider to make records available to Customer "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 removes any inspection right, so the obligation is self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2 with cl. 10.2

Broken cross-reference: Pricing 2.4 refers to role-specific rates "set out in Exhibit B", but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule; no Exhibit B exists within Schedule 7. 10_pricing.md cl. 2.4

Internal inconsistency: Change Control 8.3 states escalation does not suspend "the timetable in clause 3", but clause 3 is the impact assessment timetable binding Provider, whereas the escalation in clause 8 concerns disagreements after assessment — the cross-reference is to the wrong clause and produces no coherent effect. 08_change_control.md cl. 8.3

Expenses conflict: SOW 5.4 requires prior written approval for all expenses outside the Fee, while Pricing 3.2 requires approval only where expenses exceed £500 in a month; SOW 5.2 also says the Fee covers all travel, contradicting Pricing 3.1/3.3 which make travel and mileage recoverable. 02_sow.md cl. 5.2 and 5.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl. 3.1–3.3

Confidentiality survival of 3 years (MSA 11.3) is shorter than the 7-year record retention in MSA 12.4 and shorter than the periods over which retained Confidential Information will still be held, leaving retained data unprotected. 01_msa.md cl. 11.3 vs cl. 12.4

Prohibition on storing personal data of under-16s (AUP 3.1) conflicts with DPA 3.2/Annex 1, which contemplate processing personal data of Customer's retail customers and loyalty scheme identifiers without any age restriction or screening mechanism. 11_acceptable_use.md cl. 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 3.2 and Annex 1

Glossary defines "Transition Period" by reference to the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan never uses or defines the capitalised term "Transition Period" — it refers only to "the transition period" in clause 2.1. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 2.1

Glossary 4.1 makes the Glossary maintainable by Provider's Commercial Director, allowing Provider unilaterally to change overriding definitions, which conflicts with MSA 2.4 bilateral change requirement despite 4.2's reference to change control. 15_glossary.md cl. 4.1 and 4.2

Exit Annex 1 milestone 4 requires "parallel running complete" at T+90 Business Days (roughly 4.5 calendar months), but parallel running is a Phase 3 programme activity of 12 months' duration under the SOW; also T+90 Business Days may fall after the end of the six-month transition period, conflicting with milestone 5. 09_exit.md Annex 1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 4.3 and 09_exit.md cl. 2.1

Exit 3.4 requires Customer approval of the effort estimate before assistance begins, which can indefinitely block the mandatory milestones in Annex 1 and the certification obligation in 4.2 — an internal deadlock. 09_exit.md cl. 3.4 vs Annex 1 and cl. 4.2

Exit 6.1 commits the Delivery Lead and one solution architect to knowledge transfer during the transition period, but Exhibit B 1.2 requires Key Personnel to be dedicated solely to the programme and SOW 3.5 restricts substitution, so post-termination availability is unsupported. 09_exit.md cl. 6.1 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 1.2

Exhibit A 3.3 requires D3 to pass "the agreed functional test pack" and 3.2 refers to "the requirements register", neither of which is defined or attached anywhere in the contract set. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl. 3.2–3.3

SLA 5.4 measures response and resolution from Provider's own acknowledgement in its service management tool, which makes the 15-minute P1 response target circular (response time measured from the response) and gives Provider unilateral control over the clock. 04_sla.md cl. 5.4 with cl. 5.1

SLA 6.3 requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, conflicting with MSA 12.4's 7-year post-termination retention of all records; the same defect applies to Change Control 9.3 and Exit clause 4.1(e). 04_sla.md cl. 6.3 and 08_change_control.md cl. 9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

InfoSec 2.3 permits Provider to notify Customer of a new processing region up to 30 days after it enters service, i.e. after data may already be processed there, contradicting DPA 4.2's requirement of prior written authorisation. 06_infosec.md cl. 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.2

InfoSec 6.3 requires an incident register available at a "quarterly security review", a forum not established anywhere in the contract set (SOW 8 provides only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee). 06_infosec.md cl. 6.3 vs 02_sow.md s.8

Order Form 4.1–4.4 names contacts by job title only, and "Provider delivery contact: Delivery Lead" conflicts with SOW 5.2/6.2's reference to "Customer's nominated contact" and MSA 5.2's single point of contact, leaving the nomination regime ambiguous. 05_order_form.md s.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 5.2 and 02_sow.md cl. 6.2

Order Form 5.3 permits invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, which conflicts with MSA 4.3/SOW 5.3 payment obligations running from receipt of invoice and creates an indefinite payment deferral not contemplated elsewhere. 05_order_form.md cl. 5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3

Pricing 7.1 requires an annual rate card review at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date, but 1.3 fixes charges for the initial term and Exhibit B 3.2 holds rates for the initial term — under the 24-month MSA term the first anniversary review could produce no permissible change. 10_pricing.md cl. 7.1 and 1.3 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl. 3.2 and 01_msa.md cl. 3.1

Pricing 5.3 requires volume reporting in the monthly service report, but the SLA's prescribed report contents (clause 6.2) do not include volumes, so the two reporting specifications conflict. 10_pricing.md cl. 5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl. 6.2

Subprocessor Schedule 6.1 requires review at the quarterly steering committee, which is established only in SOW 1; if the SOW is terminated under SOW 2.4 while the MSA continues, the review forum ceases to exist. 12_subprocessors.md cl. 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.4 and 8.2

SOW 2.4 allows termination of the SOW without terminating the MSA, but the MSA's Fee, acceptance and liability provisions all depend on a Statement of Work existing; the MSA would continue with no Services and no basis for the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md cl. 2.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.5 and 4.1

Exit 9.2 requires a desk-based exit rehearsal "at least once in the term" with no deadline, while 9.1 requires annual review and 9.3 a report within one month — no trigger date makes 9.2 unenforceable. 09_exit.md cl. 9.1–9.3

BCDR 6.2 requires 20 Business Days' notice of a test and 7.2 requires Customer participation "where Provider reasonably requests", but 6.1 requires a test once in every 12-month period with no fixed date — combined with the annual review in 9.2 the testing schedule is indeterminate. 07_bcdr.md cl. 6.1–6.2 and 7.2

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule, but SOW 1 (which is Schedule 1) clause 1.2 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. The two cannot both operate. 01_msa.md cl.14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.1.2

Further circular/conflicting precedence: Order Form cl.2.1-2.2 puts the Order Form above the MSA and all Schedules, while the MSA cl.14.2 gives itself priority and the Glossary cl.1.2 gives its own definitions priority over every other document. Three documents each claim supremacy. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1-2.2; 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 15_glossary.md cl.1.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England & Wales public holidays (MSA), Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), and Monday-Friday including public holidays (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1; 15_glossary.md s.2

Monthly fee stated four different ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), £13,100 (Pricing Schedule), and an Annual Contract Value of £153,600 implying £12,800/month (Order Form). No single payable amount can be determined. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 10_pricing.md cl.1.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Invoicing timing conflict: MSA cl.4.3 and SOW cl.5.3 and Order Form cl.1.5 require monthly invoicing in arrears, while the Pricing Schedule cl.1.2 requires the recurring charge to be invoiced monthly in advance. 10_pricing.md cl.1.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.5

Fee indexation conflict: MSA cl.4.4 permits an annual CPI-linked increase, but Pricing Schedule cl.1.3 fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or increase. 01_msa.md cl.4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl.1.3

Term conflict: MSA initial term is 24 months, the SOW programme is 36 months, and the Order Form initial term is 12 months, all for the same services. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start date conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — the SOW would start a month before the MSA takes effect. 02_sow.md cl.2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3
Order Form is dated 12 March 2027, i.e. after the SOW programme commencement date of 1 March 2027. 05_order_form.md cl.7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.2

Phase durations (3 + 15 + 12 + 6 = 36 months) only equal the 36-month programme if no phases overlap, yet the programme cannot fit within the MSA's 24-month initial term or the Order Form's 12-month initial term. 02_sow.md cl.4.1-4.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Termination notice conflict: MSA cl.3.3 requires 90 days' notice for convenience; SOW cl.2.3 allows 30 days for the SOW; Order Form cl.6.2 requires only 30 days' non-renewal notice. Notice periods cannot be reconciled across the same services. 01_msa.md cl.3.3; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2
Availability target conflict: SOW cl.7.2 requires not less than 99.5% monthly availability; SLA cl.3.1 requires not less than 99.9%. 02_sow.md cl.7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1

Service credit cap conflict three ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SOW), not exceeding 10% (SLA), aggregate not exceeding 5% (Pricing Schedule). 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2; 10_pricing.md cl.4.2

Service level commencement conflict: SOW cl.7.1 applies service levels from the start of Phase 3 (18 months in), whereas Order Form cl.3.3 applies them from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support hours conflict: SLA cl.2.2 limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00-18:00 on Business Days, while Order Form cl.3.1 promises 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md cl.2.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.1

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: MSA cl.6.1 and Exhibit A cl.5.3 require express written acceptance and state silence is not acceptance, while SOW cl.6.3 deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl.6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3
Acceptance assessment period conflict: SOW cl.6.3 gives Customer 5 Business Days to respond; Exhibit A cl.5.2 gives 15 Business Days. 02_sow.md cl.6.3 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.2

Broken cross-reference: MSA cl.6.2 refers to acceptance criteria in 'Schedule 1, Section 12'. The SOW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections, and the acceptance criteria in fact sit in Exhibit A. 01_msa.md cl.6.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflict: SOW cl.6.1 says Deliverables are listed in the phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A cl.1.2 says the Exhibit is the sole source of acceptance criteria and lists the Deliverables itself. 02_sow.md cl.6.1 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.1.2, s.2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: MSA cl.8.2 gives 90 days from acceptance; Exhibit A cl.7.1 gives 180 days. 01_msa.md cl.8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.7.1

'Deliverable' defined inconsistently: MSA cl.1.3 limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW; the Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. 01_msa.md cl.1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s.2

Resubmission timing conflict: SOW cl.6.4 requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days; Exhibit A cl.5.4 imposes no such deadline and instead restarts a 15 Business Day assessment period, and MSA cl.6.3 sets no deadline. 02_sow.md cl.6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.5.4

Liability cap conflict: MSA cl.13.1 caps liability at 12 months' Fees (approx. £149,000-£157,000) and cl.13.3 says that cap overrides any Schedule, while SOW cl.9.2 sets a £250,000 cap. The two caps are incompatible and cl.13.3 conflicts with SOW cl.1.2 precedence. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.2

DPA cl.11.1 disapplies all limitations of liability for any breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, contradicting MSA cl.13.1/13.3 which state the cap applies notwithstanding any provision of any Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3
Professional indemnity insurance conflict: MSA cl.16.1 requires not less than £5,000,000; SOW cl.9.4 requires not less than £2,000,000. 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Audit rights directly contradictory: MSA cl.10.2 states Customer has no right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while DPA cl.9.1-9.2 grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1-9.2

MSA cl.12.2 requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 provides only a SOC 2 report and expressly negates further access — the cross-reference makes the obligation self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl.12.2

'Confidential Information' defined inconsistently: MSA cl.11.1 limits it to information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; the Glossary covers all information whether marked or not, oral or written; DPA cl.1.4 deems all Customer Personal Data confidential regardless of marking. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 15_glossary.md s.2; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

'Security Incident' defined three incompatible ways: broad unauthorised access/loss/alteration (DPA cl.1.6), narrow 'confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption' (SLA cl.7.1), and any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of data or platform (Glossary). 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1; 15_glossary.md s.2
Security incident notification deadline conflict three ways: 24 hours (DPA cl.6.1), 72 hours (SLA cl.7.3), 48 hours (InfoSec cl.6.1). 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Data location conflict: DPA cl.4.1 restricts processing to the UK/EEA and Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, but SOW cl.3.4 places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India, Exhibit B bases two Key Personnel in Bengaluru, the Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics in Singapore, and the InfoSec Policy cl.2.1 lets Provider choose any region at its CISO's discretion. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1, Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1; 12_subprocessors.md s.2; 06_infosec.md cl.2.1

BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt, Germany is not among the approved processing locations in DPA Annex 2 (London and Dublin only), so invoking the Plan would breach DPA cl.4.1/4.2. 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Subprocessor approval conflict: DPA cl.5.1 requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, but Subprocessor List cl.3.1 allows Provider to add or replace on 30 days' notice, cl.3.3 lets Provider proceed over Customer's objection, and cl.3.4 permits immediate replacement without prior notice. 03_dpa.md cl.5.1 vs 12_subprocessors.md cl.3.1, 3.3, 3.4

Broken cross-reference / annex mismatch: DPA cl.4.3 says Annex 2 lists approved processing locations and the DPA itself contains such an Annex 2, but Document 12 states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA (a subprocessor list). Two different documents claim to be DPA Annex 2 with different content. 03_dpa.md cl.4.3 and Annex 2 vs 12_subprocessors.md header
Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA cl.7.4 points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4
Reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan cl.5.3 refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3

Reference to a non-existent clause and body: Change Control cl.4.1 submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'. The MSA ends at clause 16 and no Change Control Board is described anywhere. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1

Reference to a non-existent exhibit: Pricing Schedule cl.2.4 refers to role-specific rates 'set out in Exhibit B', but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule, and is not incorporated into it. 10_pricing.md cl.2.4

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: Change Control cl.7.2 says impact assessments are chargeable 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan'; the Exit Plan sets only a transition assistance rate (£1,250/day) for transition work, not for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2

Internal contradiction in DPA governing law: cl.13.1 applies the law of the Agreement (England and Wales per MSA cl.15.1) while cl.13.2 applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland to the same Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1-13.2
DPA has no operative precedence rule: cl.12 is headed 'PRECEDENCE' but cl.12.1 only states the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, leaving conflicts with the MSA unresolved. 03_dpa.md cl.12

Data deletion and retention obligations are mutually impossible: DPA cl.8.2 requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination, Exit Plan cl.2.3 requires retention for 90 days after termination, Exit Plan cl.2.1/Annex 1 require handover deliverables up to 6 months after termination, and MSA cl.12.4 requires 7 years' retention of all records, data and materials. 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.1, 2.3; 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Exit Plan Annex 1 milestone 4 requires parallel running to be complete at T+90 Business Days (~4.5 months) while the transition period runs 6 months and milestone 5 (handover certification) is at end of transition period — but Provider must also delete data at 90 calendar days under cl.2.3/5.2, before handover completes. 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 5.2, Annex 1

Log retention conflict: InfoSec cl.5.2 requires security logs to be retained for 18 months 'and then deleted', which conflicts with MSA cl.12.4's 7-year retention of all records relating to the Agreement. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Service report retention conflict: SLA cl.6.3 requires retention only for the duration of the Agreement, and Change Control cl.9.3 the same for the change log, versus MSA cl.12.4's 7 years post-termination. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Subcontracting conflict: MSA cl.9.3 lets Provider subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, contradicting DPA cl.5.1's requirement of prior written consent to each Subprocessor. 01_msa.md cl.9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Change approval conflict: MSA cl.2.4 requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but Change Control cl.4.2 deems changes approved by Customer silence, cl.4.3 lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 unilaterally, and cl.6.1 permits emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Change Control cl.8.3 says escalation does not suspend 'the timetable in clause 3' (impact assessment), yet cl.4.2 deems a change approved on Customer silence within 10 Business Days while cl.8.2 allows each of three escalation levels 5 Business Days — a genuine disagreement can be deemed approved mid-escalation. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 8.2-8.3

Set-off prohibition conflicts with automatic service credit deduction: MSA cl.4.5 bars any deduction or set-off, while SLA cl.4.1 and Pricing cl.4.1 require credits to be applied automatically as a deduction from the next invoice. 01_msa.md cl.4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 10_pricing.md cl.4.1

Standard day rate conflict for solution architects/delivery lead is consistent (£1,450) but the Exit Plan charges transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day for the Delivery Lead and a solution architect, contradicting the rate card rates that Exhibit B cl.3.1 says apply to time-and-materials work. 09_exit.md cl.3.2 vs 10_pricing.md cl.2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.3

Payment card data handling contradiction: Acceptable Use cl.3.2 prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform, yet InfoSec cl.1.2 classifies payment card data as Restricted Data held by Provider and the Subprocessor List includes Ashcombe Payments Ltd for payment tokenisation. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.3.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.1.2; 12_subprocessors.md s.2

Team composition mismatch: SOW cl.3.1 requires not fewer than 11 FTE but cl.3.2 lists 1 + 2 + 6 + 1 + 1 = 11 roles, leaving no margin, and Exhibit B designates only 4 Key Personnel roles; Exhibit B lists a 'Lead Solution Architect' and 'Second Solution Architect' while the rate card has a single 'Solution Architect' role. 02_sow.md cl.3.1-3.2 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1, s.3

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW cl.3.5 bars substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B cl.2.1 permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and cl.2.4 permits immediate substitution. 02_sow.md cl.3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.1, 2.4

Exhibit B cl.1.1 says the individuals in Key Personnel roles are named in the programme initiation document, a document not identified, executed or incorporated anywhere in the contract set. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1.1

Delivery lead availability conflict: SOW cl.3.3 requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours while cl.3.4 places the team in Bengaluru; Exhibit B bases the Delivery Lead in London — inconsistent location for the same role. 02_sow.md cl.3.3-3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s.1

Exhibit B cl.1.2 requires Key Personnel to be dedicated solely to this programme, which is incompatible with cl.4.1's discretion over non-key personnel only and with SOW cl.3.5's named-personnel regime; it also conflicts with substitution on 10 days' notice. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.1.2, 2.1

Personnel replacement timing conflict: Exhibit B cl.6.2 gives Provider 20 Business Days to replace an individual, but cl.2.3 requires a two-week handover overlap funded by Provider — the two cannot both be met on immediate substitutions under cl.2.4. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.2.3, 2.4, 6.2

Vetting conflict: InfoSec cl.8.1 requires criminal-record checks on all personnel with access to Customer data, which may be unlawful/impossible for the Bengaluru-based team, and Exhibit B cl.5.1 defers wholly to that Policy without addressing offshore vetting. 06_infosec.md cl.8.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl.5.1

Encryption obligations inconsistent: DPA cl.7.2 requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while InfoSec cl.3.1 requires encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, leaving Internal Data (which can include personal data) unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.3.1

Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours is incompatible with the BCDR Recovery Time Objective of 8 hours from Invocation for the same total-outage scenario, and with cl.5.2's permitted 12 hours of planned unavailability on failback. 04_sla.md cl.5.1 vs 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2

BCDR cl.5.1 suspends all Service Level and Support Schedule obligations during a Continuity Event, which conflicts with SLA cl.9 exclusions (which do not list Continuity Events) and effectively removes the availability commitment without limit. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1 vs 04_sla.md s.9

RPO of 24 hours permits up to a day of data loss, which is irreconcilable with Exhibit A acceptance criteria requiring zero record loss (D4) and 0.01% reconciliation variance (D5), and with DPA integrity obligations. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl.3.4-3.5

Maintenance window notice conflict: SLA cl.3.4 requires 5 Business Days' notice of maintenance, but BCDR cl.5.2 allows up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on failback with no notice requirement. 04_sla.md cl.3.4 vs 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2

Service credits stated as Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures (SLA cl.4.3), which conflicts with DPA cl.11.1 removing all limitations and with the general liability regime in MSA cl.13. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.11.1; 01_msa.md cl.13

Governance body mismatch: SOW cl.8.3 sets escalation as delivery lead, account director, executive sponsor, while Change Control cl.8.1 sets Delivery Lead, Programme Director, Chief Information Officer — roles that appear nowhere else and are inconsistent with each other and with the Order Form's named contacts. 02_sow.md cl.8.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl.8.1; 05_order_form.md s.4

Security review cadence conflict: InfoSec cl.6.3 refers to a 'quarterly security review' that is not established in any governance clause; SOW cl.8 provides only a monthly service review and quarterly steering committee. 06_infosec.md cl.6.3 vs 02_sow.md s.8

InfoSec cl.2.1 permits Provider unilaterally to store data in any region at its CISO's discretion with notice up to 30 days after the region enters service, contradicting DPA cl.4.2's requirement for prior written Customer authorisation. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.2

Vulnerability remediation conflict: InfoSec cl.7.4 requires critical findings remediated within 30 days while cl.9.1 requires critical security patches within 14 days — inconsistent treatment of the same critical risk category. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4, 9.1

Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the Policy unilaterally on 30 days' notice (cl.8.1) and deems continued use acceptance (cl.8.2), contradicting MSA cl.2.4's requirement that changes be agreed in writing by both parties and Pricing cl.7.2/Glossary cl.4.2 routing changes through Change Control. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.8.1-8.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4; 08_change_control.md s.1

Acceptable Use cl.5.1 permits immediate suspension without notice for a suspected breach, with charges continuing (cl.5.4), while the availability service levels and credits in SLA s.3-4 make no exclusion for such suspensions — Provider would breach its availability commitment by exercising the right. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.5.1, 5.4 vs 04_sla.md s.3, s.9

Acceptable Use cl.6.2 permits disclosure of Customer content to authorities with no obligation to notify Customer, conflicting with DPA cl.2.2 (process only on documented instructions), cl.2.3 and MSA cl.11.2 confidentiality obligations. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.6.1-6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.2.2; 01_msa.md cl.11.2

Acceptable Use cl.4.1 states Provider does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility, conflicting with InfoSec cl.5.3 continuous monitoring and DPA cl.7.2 logging/monitoring obligations. 11_acceptable_use.md cl.4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.5.3; 03_dpa.md cl.7.2

Confidentiality survival of 3 years (MSA cl.11.3) is shorter than the 7-year record retention (MSA cl.12.4) and inconsistent with the perpetual confidentiality expected for personal data under DPA cl.1.4. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Glossary 'Agreement' definition (MSA, Order Form and every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum) conflicts with MSA cl.1.1 (MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only, omitting the Order Form and Exhibits). 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.1

Glossary 'Fee' definition (all amounts including T&M and expenses) conflicts with MSA cl.1.4 (amounts payable under clause 4) and with SOW cl.5.2/Pricing s.3 which treat expenses as outside the Fee; this also changes the value of the MSA cl.13.1 liability cap and the service credit percentages. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.4; 02_sow.md cl.5.2; 10_pricing.md s.3

Glossary 'Services' definition includes support services under the SLA, whereas MSA cl.1.5 limits Services to those described in a Statement of Work — affecting scope, service credits and the change control trigger. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.5

Glossary 'Subprocessor' refers to processing of 'Personal Data' generally while DPA cl.1.5 limits it to Customer Personal Data — inconsistent scope for the consent and flow-down obligations. 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.5

Glossary 'Personal Data' is defined by reference to UK GDPR only, while DPA cl.1.2 defines Data Protection Law as the law of every territory in which the Services are provided (including India and Singapore). 15_glossary.md s.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.2

Governance defect: the Glossary is maintained unilaterally by Provider's Commercial Director (cl.4.1) yet its definitions override every other document (cl.1.2), allowing Provider to rewrite the contract's operative terms. 15_glossary.md cl.1.2, 4.1

Glossary cl.1.3 ('a term not defined here has the meaning given where it is used') combined with cl.1.2 creates ambiguity where the Glossary defines a term more narrowly or differently from a document-specific definition intended to apply locally, e.g. 'Business Day' in the SLA. 15_glossary.md cl.1.2-1.3
Reference to an undefined term: MSA cl.1.1 and elsewhere refer to 'Statement of Work' as a document type but the MSA never defines 'Statement of Work' or 'Addendum'. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 2.1

MSA cl.1.6 defines 'Schedule' as requiring execution by both parties and express statement that it is a Schedule, but the Glossary, Pricing, InfoSec, BCDR and other Schedules are numbered Schedules 2-10 with no evidence of separate execution, and the Exhibits are not Schedules yet are relied on by the MSA acceptance regime. 01_msa.md cl.1.6 vs Documents 4, 6-12, 15

Order Form's Annual Contract Value of £153,600 for a 12-month initial term contradicts each of the three monthly fee figures except £12,800, and cannot fund the 36-month SOW programme or the ongoing platform operation it says it covers. 05_order_form.md cl.1.1, 1.4
