findings: Circular/conflicting order of precedence: MSA cl 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, SOW 1 cl 1.2 says the SOW (a Schedule) prevails over the MSA, and Order Form cl 2.1-2.2 says the Order Form prevails over everything, while Glossary cl 1.2 says its definitions prevail over all other documents. No single hierarchy can be applied. 01_msa.md cl 14.2; 02_sow.md cl 1.2; 05_order_form.md cl 2.1-2.2; 15_glossary.md cl 1.2

Order Form precedence clause omits Exhibits (Exhibit A and Exhibit B) and the Glossary/Order Form's own relationship to the Exhibits, so documents 13 and 14 have no rank in the hierarchy. 05_order_form.md cl 2.1
Monthly Fee stated three different ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), and £13,100 recurring monthly charge (Pricing Schedule). 01_msa.md cl 4.1; 02_sow.md cl 5.1; 10_pricing.md cl 1.1

Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 (the SOW figure), contradicting both the MSA fee (£148,800/yr) and the Pricing Schedule (£157,200/yr). 05_order_form.md cl 1.4 vs 01_msa.md cl 4.1 and 10_pricing.md cl 1.1

Payment terms conflict four ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form); the invoice-date vs receipt-date trigger also differs. 01_msa.md cl 4.3; 02_sow.md cl 5.3; 05_order_form.md cl 1.6

Billing timing conflict: MSA cl 4.3, SOW cl 5.3 and Order Form cl 1.5 all require invoicing monthly in arrears, while Pricing Schedule cl 1.2 requires invoicing monthly in advance. 10_pricing.md cl 1.2 vs 01_msa.md cl 4.3, 02_sow.md cl 5.3, 05_order_form.md cl 1.5

Fee escalation conflict: MSA cl 4.4 permits an annual CPI-linked increase, but Pricing Schedule cl 1.3 fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or increase. 01_msa.md cl 4.4 vs 10_pricing.md cl 1.3

Invoice issue date is impossible to reconcile with arrears billing/PO requirements: invoices issued on the first Business Day of each month (Pricing 6.1) cannot cover a month billed in arrears and, per Pricing 1.2, in advance. 10_pricing.md cl 6.1 with cl 1.2

Term conflict: MSA initial term is 24 months, Order Form initial term is 12 months, and the SOW programme runs 36 months — the programme cannot be completed within either contractual term. 01_msa.md cl 3.1; 05_order_form.md cl 1.2; 02_sow.md cl 2.1

Termination-for-convenience notice conflict: 90 days under the MSA vs 30 days under the SOW vs 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form. 01_msa.md cl 3.3; 02_sow.md cl 2.3; 05_order_form.md cl 6.2

Renewal conflict: MSA renews in successive 12-month periods after a 24-month initial term, while the Order Form renews in 12-month periods after a 12-month initial term, producing misaligned renewal dates. 01_msa.md cl 3.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl 6.1-6.2

Commencement date conflict: MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — i.e. before the MSA exists. 02_sow.md cl 2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date and 05_order_form.md cl 1.3
Order Form signed 12 March 2027, after the SOW programme was due to commence (1 March 2027). 05_order_form.md cl 7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl 2.2

Phase durations (3 + 15 + 12 + 6 = 36 months) equal the stated 36-month programme only if no overlap occurs, yet cl 4.5 contemplates overlap; more importantly the 36 months exceed the 24-month MSA term and 12-month Order Form term. 02_sow.md cl 4.1-4.5 with cl 2.1

'Business Day' defined three incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England & Wales public holidays (MSA), Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), and Monday-Friday including public holidays (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl 1.2; 04_sla.md cl 1.1; 15_glossary.md s2

'Confidential Information' defined two ways: only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure (MSA) vs any information whether or not marked and whether oral or written (Glossary); DPA cl 1.4 adds a third overlay. 01_msa.md cl 11.1; 15_glossary.md s2; 03_dpa.md cl 1.4

'Deliverable' defined two ways: an item identified as a deliverable in a SOW (MSA) vs any output of the Services whether or not so identified (Glossary), which changes the scope of the IP assignment and acceptance regime. 01_msa.md cl 1.3 vs 15_glossary.md s2

'Fee' defined two ways: amounts payable under MSA clause 4 (MSA) vs all amounts including T&M charges and expenses (Glossary); this also changes the base for the liability cap and service credit percentages. 01_msa.md cl 1.4 vs 15_glossary.md s2
'Services' defined two ways: services described in a Statement of Work (MSA) vs SOW services plus SLA support services (Glossary). 01_msa.md cl 1.5 vs 15_glossary.md s2

'Security Incident' defined three incompatible ways: any unauthorised access/loss etc. of Customer Personal Data (DPA), only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption (SLA), and any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform (Glossary). 03_dpa.md cl 1.6; 04_sla.md cl 7.1; 15_glossary.md s2

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (Information Security Policy) — cannot all be satisfied and the triggers differ (awareness vs confirmation). 03_dpa.md cl 6.1; 04_sla.md cl 7.3; 06_infosec.md cl 6.1
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly under the SOW vs 99.9% monthly under the SLA. 02_sow.md cl 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl 3.1

Service credit caps conflict three ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SOW), maximum 10% of monthly Fee (SLA), and aggregate maximum 5% of recurring monthly charge (Pricing). 02_sow.md cl 7.4; 04_sla.md cl 4.2; 10_pricing.md cl 4.2

Service level start date conflict: SOW says service levels apply from the start of Phase 3 (month 19), while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md cl 7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl 3.3

Support hours conflict: SLA provides Priority 2/3 support only 08:00-18:00 on Business Days, while the Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md cl 2.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl 3.1

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and states in cl 13.3 that this applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW imposes a £250,000 cap; the DPA cl 11.1 disapplies all limitations for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md cl 13.1 & 13.3; 02_sow.md cl 9.2; 03_dpa.md cl 11.1
Insurance conflict: MSA requires professional indemnity of not less than £5,000,000 while the SOW requires not less than £2,000,000 for the same engagement. 01_msa.md cl 16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl 9.4

Audit rights conflict: MSA cl 10.2 removes all rights to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, but DPA cl 9.1-9.2 grants an annual audit including inspection of premises and systems, and Information Security Policy cl 7.3 gives Customer a pen-test nomination right. 01_msa.md cl 10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl 9.1-9.2

MSA cl 12.2 requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes audit/inspection rights and provides only for a SOC 2 report — the cross-reference is self-defeating. 01_msa.md cl 12.2 with cl 10.2

Acceptance regime conflict: MSA cl 6.1 and Exhibit A cl 5.3 require express written acceptance and state silence is not acceptance, while SOW cl 6.3 deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 5.3; 02_sow.md cl 6.3
Assessment periods conflict: SOW allows 5 Business Days to respond, Exhibit A allows 15 Business Days to assess and issue a certificate. 02_sow.md cl 6.3-6.4 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 5.2

Source of acceptance criteria conflict: MSA cl 6.2 points to 'Schedule 1, Section 12' (SOW 1 has only 10 sections — non-existent reference), SOW cl 6.1 points to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, and Exhibit A cl 1.2 claims to be the sole source. 01_msa.md cl 6.2; 02_sow.md cl 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 1.2
Deliverable warranty period conflict: 90 days from acceptance (MSA) vs 180 days from acceptance (Exhibit A). 01_msa.md cl 8.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 7.1

Subcontracting conflict: MSA cl 9.3 allows subcontracting without Customer consent, but DPA cl 5.1 requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor and Subprocessor List cl 3.1 allows addition on mere 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md cl 9.3; 03_dpa.md cl 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md cl 3.1

Subprocessor List cl 3.4 permits immediate replacement of a Subprocessor with notice afterwards, directly contradicting the DPA's prior-specific-consent requirement. 12_subprocessors.md cl 3.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl 5.1

Data location conflict: DPA cl 4.1 restricts processing to the UK/EEA, but the SOW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India; the approved Subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics in Singapore; and the Information Security Policy allows storage in any Provider region at the CISO's discretion. 03_dpa.md cl 4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl 3.4, 12_subprocessors.md s2, 06_infosec.md cl 2.1
DR site in Frankfurt, Germany is not among the approved processing locations listed in DPA Annex 2 (London and Dublin only). 07_bcdr.md cl 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Annex 2 conflict: DPA cl 4.3 says Annex 2 lists approved processing locations and the DPA's own Annex 2 does so, but Document 12 states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA (a subprocessor list) — two different Annex 2s. 03_dpa.md cl 4.3 & Annex 2 vs 12_subprocessors.md preamble
Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA cl 7.4 refers to escalation contacts in 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum'; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl 7.4
Reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan cl 5.3 refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl 5.3

Reference to a non-existent clause: Change Control cl 4.1 refers to a Change Control Board 'described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and describes no such board. 08_change_control.md cl 4.1

Reference to a non-existent provision: Change Control cl 7.2 says impact-assessment charges are at 'the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', which contains only a transition assistance rate (£1,250/day) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl 7.2 vs 09_exit.md

Pricing cl 2.4 refers role-specific rates to 'Exhibit B', but Exhibit B is an exhibit to Statement of Work 1, not to the Pricing Schedule, and is not ranked in the Order Form precedence list. 10_pricing.md cl 2.4

Governing law conflict internal to the DPA: cl 13.1 adopts the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in clause 13.2', while cl 13.2 imposes the laws of the Republic of Ireland; this also conflicts with MSA cl 15.1-15.2 (England and Wales exclusive jurisdiction). 03_dpa.md cl 13.1-13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl 15

Data deletion vs retention conflict: DPA cl 8.2 requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination, Exit Plan cl 2.3 requires retention for 90 days after termination, and MSA cl 12.4 requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years — mutually impossible. 03_dpa.md cl 8.2; 09_exit.md cl 2.3; 01_msa.md cl 12.4

MSA cl 12.4's 7-year retention also conflicts with SLA cl 6.3 (reports retained only for the duration of the Agreement), Change Control cl 9.3 (change log retained only for the duration of the Agreement) and Infosec cl 5.2 (security logs deleted after 18 months). 01_msa.md cl 12.4 vs 04_sla.md cl 6.3, 08_change_control.md cl 9.3, 06_infosec.md cl 5.2

Confidentiality survival period of 3 years is shorter than the 7-year record retention obligation and shorter than the data retention/deletion regime, leaving retained confidential data unprotected. 01_msa.md cl 11.3 with cl 12.4

Change approval conflict: MSA cl 2.4 requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but Change Control cl 4.2 deems approval from Customer silence, cl 4.3 lets Provider's Delivery Lead unilaterally approve changes up to £35,000, and cl 6.1 allows emergency changes without approval. 01_msa.md cl 2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl 4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Change Control cl 5.3 exempts change-related charges from notice requirements for charge increases, conflicting with MSA cl 4.4 (60 days' notice, once per 12 months, CPI-capped) and Pricing cl 1.3 (charge fixed for initial term). 08_change_control.md cl 5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl 4.4 and 10_pricing.md cl 1.3

Change Control cl 8.3 states escalation does not suspend the timetable in clause 3 (impact assessment), but the escalation timetable in cl 8.1-8.2 concerns disagreements after the assessment; the cross-reference is to the wrong clause (approval timetable in cl 4). 08_change_control.md cl 8.3

Service credit mechanics conflict: SLA cl 4.1 requires automatic application without any claim, while SOW cl 7.4 says Customer 'is entitled to' credits (claim-based) and caps differ; Pricing cl 4.1 applies credits to the next recurring invoice which is issued in advance. 04_sla.md cl 4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl 7.4 and 10_pricing.md cl 4.1

SLA cl 4.3 makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW/MSA liability regime and with DPA cl 11.1 disapplying limitations, and is inconsistent with Customer's right to terminate/claim for material breach. 04_sla.md cl 4.3

Resolution targets are unachievable against the definitions: Priority 1 Resolution within 4 hours while a Security Incident is treated as Priority 1, yet BCDR RTO is 8 hours from Invocation — a disaster-driven P1 cannot be resolved in 4 hours. 04_sla.md cl 5.1 & 7.2 vs 07_bcdr.md cl 2.1

BCDR cl 5.1 suspends all SLA obligations during a Continuity Event while cl 5.2-5.3 allow up to 12 hours' further planned unavailability excluded from availability — combined with a 99.9% target (roughly 43 minutes' downtime per month) this makes the SLA effectively unenforceable and conflicts with SLA cl 3.3 which excludes only agreed maintenance windows. 07_bcdr.md cl 5.1-5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl 3.1, 3.3, 9.3

BCDR RPO of 24 hours' data loss is incompatible with Exhibit A acceptance criteria requiring zero record loss / 0.01% reconciliation variance and with the warm-standby claim in cl 3.2. 07_bcdr.md cl 2.2 vs 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 3.4-3.5

Maintenance window notice of 5 Business Days (SLA) is inconsistent with the 20 Business Days' notice required for BCDR tests that may cause unavailability, and no notice period is specified for the up to 12 hours' planned unavailability in BCDR cl 5.2. 04_sla.md cl 3.4 vs 07_bcdr.md cl 5.2, 6.2

Team composition conflict: SOW cl 3.1 requires not fewer than 11 FTE but cl 3.2 lists only 1+2+6+1+1 = 11 roles with no allowance for the stated minimum, and Exhibit B lists only 4 Key Personnel roles, omitting the business analyst and engineers referenced in the rate card. 02_sow.md cl 3.1-3.2 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s1

Team location conflict: SOW cl 3.4 states the whole delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md cl 3.4 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s1

Key personnel substitution conflict: SOW cl 3.5 prohibits substitution without Customer's prior written agreement, but Exhibit B cl 2.1 allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and cl 2.4 allows immediate substitution. 02_sow.md cl 3.5 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl 2.1, 2.4

Rate conflict: Pricing cl 2.1 sets a standard rate of £1,450 per person per day and Exhibit B sets role rates, but the Exit Plan charges transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day with no cross-reference reconciling the three. 10_pricing.md cl 2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s3; 09_exit.md cl 3.2

Rate review conflict: Pricing cl 7.1 requires review of the rate card at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date (i.e. during the initial term where the term is 24 months), while Exhibit B cl 3.2 holds rates for the initial term and Pricing cl 1.3 fixes charges for the initial term. 10_pricing.md cl 7.1 & 1.3 vs 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl 3.2

Exit Plan cl 2.1 defines the transition period as beginning when notice is given and ending 6 months after the effective date of termination, so a 90-day MSA termination notice produces a period exceeding the contract term and requires Provider to continue Services after termination without any charging basis for the recurring fee. 09_exit.md cl 2.1-2.2

Exit milestones are internally inconsistent with the transition period: milestone 4 (parallel running complete) at T+90 Business Days is roughly 4.5 calendar months but handover certification is at end of transition period (T+6 months), while data must be deleted after the 90-calendar-day retention period in cl 2.3 — deletion could precede completion of handover. 09_exit.md Annex 1 with cl 2.3 and cl 5.2

Exit Plan cl 4.1(a) requires Customer data to be delivered 'in the format used by Provider's systems', conflicting with DPA cl 8.1 requiring a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl 4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl 8.1

Exit Plan cl 3.4 requires Customer approval of the estimate before assistance begins, which can block Provider's mandatory transition obligations and conflicts with cl 1.2/cl 3.1 (assistance applies however the Agreement ends). 09_exit.md cl 3.4 with cl 3.1

Exit Plan cl 4.1(e) refers to 'the outstanding change log maintained under the Change Control Procedure', but Change Control cl 9.3 retains the change log only for the duration of the Agreement, so it may not exist at end of the transition period (which runs past termination). 09_exit.md cl 4.1(e) vs 08_change_control.md cl 9.3

Payment card data conflict: Information Security Policy cl 1.2 classifies payment card data as Restricted Data (contemplating its presence), while Acceptable Use Policy cl 3.2 prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, and Subprocessor List includes Ashcombe Payments Ltd for payment tokenisation. 06_infosec.md cl 1.2 vs 11_acceptable_use.md cl 3.2 and 12_subprocessors.md s2

Encryption conflict: DPA cl 7.2 requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, but Infosec cl 3.1 requires encryption at rest only for Restricted Data, leaving Internal Data (which includes personal data such as contact details and transaction records) unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl 7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl 3.1 and 1.3

Infosec cl 2.1 lets Provider's own CISO unilaterally determine data locations and cl 2.3 permits notification of a new region up to 30 days after it enters service, contradicting the DPA's prior-written-authorisation requirement for transfers. 06_infosec.md cl 2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl 4.2

Infosec cl 5.2 requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months, which may conflict with the DPA logging obligation and MSA 7-year record retention, and could destroy evidence needed for the 180-day/annual audit and incident processes. 06_infosec.md cl 5.2

Vulnerability/remediation timescales conflict: Infosec cl 7.4 requires remediation of critical findings within 30 days while cl 9.1 requires critical security patches within 14 days, with no reconciliation of which applies to a critical patchable finding. 06_infosec.md cl 7.4 vs 9.1

Infosec cl 10.1-10.2 allows Provider to review and materially change this Policy on mere notification, and Acceptable Use cl 8.1 allows Provider unilateral amendment on 30 days' notice, contradicting MSA cl 2.4 (changes agreed in writing by both parties) and Pricing cl 7.2/Glossary cl 4.2 (changes go through Change Control). 06_infosec.md cl 10.2; 11_acceptable_use.md cl 8.1 vs 01_msa.md cl 2.4

Acceptable Use cl 3.1 prohibits storing personal data of anyone under 16, which is inconsistent with the DPA's data subject categories (Customer retail customers, without age limitation) and unenforceable in a loyalty scheme context. 11_acceptable_use.md cl 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl 3.2

Suspension right conflict: Acceptable Use cl 5.1 permits immediate suspension of all Services without notice on a reasonable belief of breach, overriding the MSA cl 3.4 15-day remedy period and defeating the SLA availability commitment (SLA exclusions in cl 9 do not cover suspension). 11_acceptable_use.md cl 5.1 vs 01_msa.md cl 3.4 and 04_sla.md cl 3.1, 9

Acceptable Use cl 6.2 removes any obligation to notify Customer of a disclosure to authorities, conflicting with DPA cl 2.2-2.3 and cl 6 (processor obligations to inform the controller regarding processing and incidents). 11_acceptable_use.md cl 6.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl 2.2-2.3

Acceptable Use cl 4.1 states Provider does not monitor content, contradicting Infosec cl 5.3 (continuous monitoring for anomalous access) and cl 5.1 (logging all access to Customer data). 11_acceptable_use.md cl 4.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl 5.1, 5.3

Glossary defines 'Subprocessor' as a third party processing 'Personal Data' generally, whereas the DPA defines it as a third party processing Customer Personal Data — a scope mismatch affecting consent obligations. 15_glossary.md s2 vs 03_dpa.md cl 1.5

Glossary definition of 'Agreement' (including the Order Form, Exhibits) conflicts with MSA cl 1.1 (this MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only), affecting which documents are contractually incorporated. 15_glossary.md s2 vs 01_msa.md cl 1.1

Glossary cl 1.2 gives the Glossary overriding force but cl 4.1 makes it maintained unilaterally by Provider's Commercial Director, allowing Provider to change binding definitions; also conflicts with Order Form cl 2.1 which ranks Schedules below the MSA and Order Form. 15_glossary.md cl 1.2 & 4.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl 2.1

Glossary cl 4.2 requires additions to the Glossary to go through Change Control, but the Change Control Procedure applies only to changes to scope, timetable, charges or acceptance criteria (cl 1.1) — definitions fall outside its scope. 15_glossary.md cl 4.2 vs 08_change_control.md cl 1.1

DPA cl 12.1 is headed 'Precedence' but states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, giving no precedence rule; the DPA therefore has no stated rank relative to the MSA despite MSA cl 14.2 and the DPA's cl 11.1 override of liability limits. 03_dpa.md cl 12.1
DPA cl 11.2 mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is legally unenforceable in many jurisdictions and contradicts DPA cl 11.1 and MSA cl 13.1/13.3 caps. 03_dpa.md cl 11.2

MSA cl 2.3 requires Provider to comply with Customer's instructions on the manner of performance, which conflicts with the fixed-price/fixed-scope regime and with Change Control cl 1.1 requiring changes to go through the procedure. 01_msa.md cl 2.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl 1.1

MSA cl 7.2 assigns Deliverable IP only on payment in full, which conflicts with the Exit Plan obligation to deliver all Deliverables including source code on exit and with the Glossary's broader Deliverable definition. 01_msa.md cl 7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl 4.1(b)
Set-off prohibition in MSA cl 4.5 conflicts with automatic service credit deduction mechanisms in SLA cl 4.1 and Pricing cl 4.1. 01_msa.md cl 4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl 4.1 and 10_pricing.md cl 4.1

SLA cl 5.4 measures response and resolution times from Provider's own acknowledgement in its tool rather than from Incident report/occurrence, allowing Provider to control the clock and rendering the 15-minute P1 response target meaningless. 04_sla.md cl 5.4

SLA Priority 2/3 targets are expressed in Business Days while P2/P3 support hours are limited to 08:00-18:00 on Business Days under a Business Day definition that conflicts across documents, making the targets indeterminate. 04_sla.md cl 1.1, 2.2, 5.2-5.3

SLA cl 7.1 defines Security Incident narrowly (loss or corruption) so pure confidentiality breaches escape P1 treatment and the SLA notification clock, conflicting with DPA cl 1.6 and Glossary. 04_sla.md cl 7.1

BCDR cl 4.1 permits only Provider's Head of Operations to declare Invocation, with no fallback or Customer right to require invocation, and no deadline for declaration — RTO runs only from Invocation, so recovery can be indefinitely delayed. 07_bcdr.md cl 2.1, 4.1

BCDR cl 8.2 excludes simultaneous loss of primary and recovery environments from the Plan, yet the recovery environment (Frankfurt) and primary (London) sit with a single third-party infrastructure supplier assumed available under cl 8.1, leaving an unaddressed single point of failure. 07_bcdr.md cl 8.1-8.2

Change Control cl 4.3 allows unilateral Provider approval of changes up to £35,000, which exceeds any expenses/approval threshold elsewhere (e.g. Pricing cl 3.2 requires approval above £500) and conflicts with SOW cl 5.4 requiring prior written Customer approval for expenses outside the Fee. 08_change_control.md cl 4.3 vs 10_pricing.md cl 3.2 and 02_sow.md cl 5.4

SOW cl 4.5 says phases may overlap only where agreed in writing, but the total of the phase durations already consumes the entire 36 months, so any slippage makes the programme duration in cl 2.1 unachievable without a change. 02_sow.md cl 2.1, 4.1-4.5

Exhibit A cl 4.3 permits acceptance with Minor Defects outstanding, but MSA cl 6.3 requires Provider to correct and resubmit any rejected Deliverable and MSA cl 8.2 warrants conformity to acceptance criteria — no mechanism reconciles accepted-with-defects status. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 4.3 vs 01_msa.md cl 6.3, 8.2

Exhibit A defines 'Material Defect' and 'Minor Defect' but the SOW and MSA acceptance clauses use neither term, and the Glossary defines only Material Defect, leaving 'Minor Defect' without cross-document effect. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 4.1-4.2; 15_glossary.md s2

Exhibit A cl 6.1 escalates deliverable disputes 'under the governance provisions of the Statement of Work' (SOW cl 8.3: delivery lead, account director, executive sponsor), which conflicts with the different escalation chain in Change Control cl 8.1 (Delivery Lead, Programme Director, CIO). 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md cl 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl 8.3 and 08_change_control.md cl 8.1

Exhibit B cl 1.2 requires Key Personnel to be dedicated exclusively to this programme, conflicting with Exhibit B cl 2.4 immediate substitution and with SOW cl 3.3 (delivery lead only 'available during Customer's working hours') and the Exit Plan's demand for the same Delivery Lead during transition after termination. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl 1.2 vs 09_exit.md cl 6.1

Exhibit B cl 6.2 requires replacement of an unsatisfactory individual within 20 Business Days, which conflicts with the substitution notice/handover overlap regime (cl 2.1, 2.3) and with SOW cl 3.5's requirement for Customer's prior written agreement to any substitution. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md cl 6.2 vs cl 2.1-2.3 and 02_sow.md cl 3.5

Exhibit B rate table omits roles referenced elsewhere (e.g. Programme Director, account director, security roles) and lists 'Solution Architect' at the same rate as Delivery Lead while Pricing cl 2.4 assumes Exhibit B is exhaustive of role-specific rates. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md s3 with 10_pricing.md cl 2.4

Pricing cl 5.2 sets overage at £0.004 per transaction with no cap, contradicting Pricing cl 1.3 (charge fixed and not subject to any increase during the initial term) and the fixed Annual Contract Value in the Order Form. 10_pricing.md cl 5.2 vs cl 1.3 and 05_order_form.md cl 1.4

Pricing cl 6.3 requires invoice queries within 10 Business Days, but MSA cl 4.3/SOW cl 5.3 contemplate disputing invoices generally with 30/45-day payment terms — the short query window effectively removes the right to withhold payment on disputed invoices. 10_pricing.md cl 6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl 4.3

Order Form cl 5.3 permits invoices without a PO number to be returned unpaid, which can conflict with the payment obligation and interest/late payment position, and no PO requirement appears in the MSA or Pricing invoicing clauses. 05_order_form.md cl 5.1-5.3 vs 10_pricing.md cl 6.2

Order Form cl 3.2 names 'Provider's service desk' as the named support contact, but the Subprocessor list shows out-of-hours service desk is provided by Larkfield Support Partners Ltd, a subprocessor, with no reconciliation of the 24x7 commitment. 05_order_form.md cl 3.2 vs 12_subprocessors.md s2

Governance frequency mismatch: SOW cl 8.1-8.2 provides monthly service reviews and a quarterly steering committee, Infosec cl 6.3 refers to a 'quarterly security review' that is not established anywhere, and Subprocessor List cl 6.1 requires list review at the quarterly steering committee. 06_infosec.md cl 6.3 vs 02_sow.md cl 8.1-8.2

Provider is required to give not less than 20 Business Days' notice of a BCDR test but must also test at least annually within a 12-month period; combined with 15 Business Days for test reports and 1 month for remediation plans, and a 24-month/12-month term, the testing cycle may not complete within the term. 07_bcdr.md cl 6.1-6.4 with 01_msa.md cl 3.1 and 05_order_form.md cl 1.2

Exit Plan cl 9.2 requires a desk-based exit rehearsal 'at least once in the term' with no deadline, and cl 9.1 requires annual review, which cannot occur within a 12-month Order Form term ending at renewal. 09_exit.md cl 9.1-9.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl 1.2

Exit Plan Annex 1 milestone 1 requires the exit plan to be confirmed with an incoming supplier by T+15 Business Days, an obligation on a third party outside Provider's or Customer's control and inconsistent with the transition period beginning at notice (pre-T). 09_exit.md Annex 1 with cl 2.1

findings: Circular order of precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SoW 1 (a Schedule) says it prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says it prevails over everything (including the MSA), and the Glossary (Schedule 10) says its definitions prevail over every other document. No conflict can be resolved. MSA cl.14.2; SoW 1 cl.1.2; Order Form cl.2.1–2.2; Glossary cl.1.2

Precedence ladder has no tie-breaker between documents of the same rank: SLA (Sch 2), InfoSec (Sch 3), BCDR (Sch 4), Change Control (Sch 5), Exit (Sch 6), Pricing (Sch 7), AUP (Sch 8), Subprocessor List (Sch 9) and Glossary (Sch 10) all sit in tier (c), yet they contradict one another (e.g. service-credit caps, availability, incident notification). Order Form cl.2.1(c)

Document 12 is designated both Schedule 9 (precedence tier (c)) and Annex 2 to the DPA (tier (d)), so it simultaneously outranks and forms part of the DPA. Subprocessor List, header/cl.1; Order Form cl.2.1(c)–(d)

Two different Annex 2s to the DPA exist: the DPA's own Annex 2 (London primary, Dublin DR) and the Subprocessor List which states it is Annex 2. Their contents are different and irreconcilable. DPA cl.4.3 and Annex 2; Subprocessor List header

"Business Day" is defined three incompatible ways: Mon–Fri excluding England & Wales public holidays; Mon–Sat excluding US federal holidays; Mon–Fri including public holidays. Every deadline expressed in Business Days is indeterminate. MSA cl.1.2; SLA cl.1.1; Glossary §2

"Confidential Information" defined inconsistently: MSA requires written marking at disclosure; the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether marked or not; the Glossary covers all information whether marked or not and including oral disclosure. MSA cl.11.1; DPA cl.1.4; Glossary §2

"Deliverable" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SoW; the Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. This changes the scope of IP assignment, acceptance and warranty. MSA cl.1.3; Glossary §2

"Fee" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to amounts payable under clause 4; the Glossary makes it all amounts including T&M and expenses. Service-credit caps and the liability cap are calculated on "Fee" and therefore have no fixed value. MSA cl.1.4; Glossary §2; SLA cl.4.2; SoW cl.7.4; MSA cl.13.1

"Services" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to services described in a SoW; the Glossary includes SLA support services. SoW-based termination and charging provisions therefore have uncertain scope. MSA cl.1.5; Glossary §2

"Security Incident" defined three incompatible ways: broad DPA definition (any unauthorised access/alteration/loss of personal data); narrow SLA definition (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption); and open-ended Glossary definition (any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform). DPA cl.1.6; SLA cl.7.1; Glossary §2

Monthly charge stated four different ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SoW), £13,100 (Pricing), and £153,600 annual contract value in the Order Form (= £12,800/month). MSA cl.4.1; SoW cl.5.1; Pricing cl.1.1; Order Form cl.1.4
Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt; 45 days from receipt; 60 days from invoice date. MSA cl.4.3; SoW cl.5.3; Order Form cl.1.6

Billing basis conflicts: MSA, SoW and Order Form require invoicing monthly in arrears; the Pricing Schedule requires invoicing monthly in advance on the first Business Day of the month. MSA cl.4.3; SoW cl.5.3; Order Form cl.1.5; Pricing cl.1.2, cl.6.1

Indexation conflict: the MSA permits a CPI-linked increase once every 12 months on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term with no indexation or increase. MSA cl.4.4; Pricing cl.1.3
No set-off/deduction clause conflicts with the automatic application of service credits as deductions from invoices. MSA cl.4.5; SLA cl.4.1; Pricing cl.4.1
Initial term conflict: MSA initial term is 24 months from 1 April 2027; the Order Form initial term is 12 months from the same date. MSA cl.3.1; Order Form cl.1.2

The 36-month programme cannot be performed within the 12-month Order Form term (or the 24-month MSA initial term) without reliance on automatic renewal, which either party can defeat. SoW cl.2.1; Order Form cl.1.2, cl.6.1–6.2; MSA cl.3.1–3.2

Commencement dates conflict: the SoW programme commences 1 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date and Order Form Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027). SoW cl.2.2; MSA header; Order Form cl.1.3, cl.7.3

Termination notice periods conflict: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for the SoW (which contains all the Services), and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form, which prevails and effectively overrides the MSA's 90 days. MSA cl.3.3; SoW cl.2.3; Order Form cl.6.2

Acceptance regime conflicts three ways: MSA requires express written acceptance and no deemed acceptance; the SoW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days' silence; Exhibit A requires a signed certificate after a 15 Business Day assessment and states silence is not acceptance. MSA cl.6.1; SoW cl.6.3; Exhibit A cl.5.2–5.3

Resubmission periods conflict: SoW requires re-submission within 10 Business Days with no further assessment period stated; Exhibit A applies a further 15 Business Day assessment period. SoW cl.6.4; Exhibit A cl.5.4

Reference to a non-existent provision: the MSA points to acceptance criteria in "Schedule 1, Section 12", but SoW 1 has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. MSA cl.6.2; SoW 1 (sections 1–10)

Three competing sources for Deliverables/acceptance criteria: MSA (Schedule 1 s.12), SoW (phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, a non-contractual document unilaterally maintained by Provider), and Exhibit A (which claims to be the sole source). MSA cl.6.2; SoW cl.6.1; Exhibit A cl.1.2
Deliverable warranty period conflicts: 90 days from acceptance under the MSA, 180 days under Exhibit A. MSA cl.8.2; Exhibit A cl.7.1
Availability target conflicts: 99.5% monthly in the SoW versus 99.9% monthly in the SLA (and the Order Form applies service levels from a different start date). SoW cl.7.2; SLA cl.3.1
Service credit cap stated three ways: up to 25% of monthly Fee (SoW), maximum 10% (SLA), maximum 5% (Pricing). SoW cl.7.4; SLA cl.4.2; Pricing cl.4.2

Service level start date conflicts: SoW applies service levels only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme); the Order Form applies them from the Service Commencement Date. SoW cl.7.1; Order Form cl.3.3
Support coverage conflicts: Order Form promises 24x7 for all priority levels; the SLA limits P2 and P3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl.3.1; SLA cl.2.2

Response times are self-referential and meaningless: response and resolution are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the response target can never be missed and Provider controls the clock. SLA cl.5.4

Liability caps conflict: MSA caps at 12 months' Fees (approx. £150k) and states the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule; the SoW sets a higher £250,000 cap; the DPA disapplies all limitations for any breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law. MSA cl.13.1, cl.13.3; SoW cl.9.2; DPA cl.11.1

Exclusion of indirect/consequential loss appears only in the SoW, but the MSA states its liability provisions prevail notwithstanding any Schedule, leaving it unclear whether the exclusion has effect. SoW cl.9.3; MSA cl.13.3, cl.14.2
Mutual liability cap arguably limits Customer's own obligation to pay the Fees, since it caps "each party's total aggregate liability" with no carve-out for sums due. MSA cl.13.1
Insurance limits conflict: £5,000,000 professional indemnity in the MSA versus £2,000,000 in the SoW. MSA cl.16.1; SoW cl.9.4

Audit rights directly conflict: the MSA gives Customer no right to audit, inspect or attend beyond receiving a SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. MSA cl.10.2; DPA cl.9.1–9.2

Confidentiality survival of only 3 years is inconsistent with the 7-year records retention obligation and with the indefinite protection required for personal data treated as Confidential Information. MSA cl.11.3, cl.12.4; DPA cl.1.4

The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, yet the InfoSec Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data held on Provider systems and an approved subprocessor provides payment tokenisation. AUP cl.3.2; InfoSec cl.1.2; Subprocessor List §2

The AUP prohibits storing personal data of anyone under 16, which is inconsistent with the DPA's stated data subject categories (retail customers and loyalty scheme identifiers) with no age screening obligation anywhere. AUP cl.3.1; DPA cl.3.2–3.3

Provider may unilaterally amend the Acceptable Use Policy (a Schedule) on 30 days' notice, contradicting the requirement for changes to be agreed in writing by both parties and the Change Control Procedure. AUP cl.8.1–8.2; MSA cl.2.4; Change Control cl.1.1

Immediate suspension for suspected AUP breach bypasses the 15-day cure period for material breach and is not an excluded event under the SLA, so a lawful suspension would still breach the availability service level while charges continue to accrue. AUP cl.5.1, cl.5.4; MSA cl.3.4; SLA §9

Provider may disclose Customer content to authorities without any obligation to notify Customer, which conflicts with the processor's duty to act only on documented instructions and to inform the controller about instructions/legal requirements. AUP cl.6.1–6.2; DPA cl.2.2–2.3

Provider states it does not monitor content and accepts no responsibility for it, which sits awkwardly with mandatory continuous monitoring and logging of all access to Customer data. AUP cl.4.1; InfoSec cl.5.1, cl.5.3
Remediation timescales are inconsistent: critical penetration-test findings within 30 days versus critical security patches within 14 days, with no rule for overlap. InfoSec cl.7.4, cl.9.1

The Glossary is unilaterally maintained by Provider's Commercial Director yet its definitions are stated to prevail over every other document, allowing Provider to rewrite the commercial bargain by amending definitions; the change route (Change Control) also permits Delivery-Lead approval and deemed approval by silence. Glossary cl.1.2, cl.4.1–4.2; Change Control cl.4.2–4.3

Glossary "Business Day" (Monday to Friday, including public holidays) is internally illogical for a services contract and, if it prevails, makes public holidays working days for SLA and deadline purposes. Glossary §2

Glossary "Personal Data" is tied to the UK GDPR only, while the DPA's "Data Protection Law" covers every territory where the Services are provided (including India and Singapore), leaving non-UK processing outside the defined protection. Glossary §2; DPA cl.1.2

Glossary "Agreement" is broader than the MSA definition (which covers only Schedules and Addenda executed under the MSA and omits the Order Form and Exhibits), so it is unclear which documents are contractually incorporated. MSA cl.1.1; Glossary §2

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the DPA's disapplication of all limitations and with the general liability regime, and no service-level regime exists for the response/resolution targets at all. SLA cl.4.3, §5; DPA cl.11.1
Service reports need only be retained for the duration of the Agreement, conflicting with the 7-year retention obligation for records relating to the Agreement. SLA cl.6.3; MSA cl.12.4

Termination right on subprocessor objection (30 days' notice to terminate "the affected Services") is undefined and inconsistent with the termination machinery in the MSA, SoW and Order Form. Subprocessor List cl.3.3; MSA cl.3.3; SoW cl.2.3

Approved subprocessors are located outside the UK/EEA (Singapore) with only a generic promise of a transfer mechanism, contradicting the DPA's prohibition on transfers without prior written authorisation and the Annex 2 location list. Subprocessor List §2, cl.5.1; DPA cl.4.1–4.3, Annex 2

Provider both maintains the subprocessor list on its trust portal (unilateral, published) and is subject to specific-consent and review-confirmation obligations; the interaction of unilateral publication with the DPA consent requirement is contradictory. Subprocessor List cl.1.2, cl.3.1; DPA cl.5.1

Programme phase durations (3+15+12+6 = 36 months) leave no float and, with the prohibition on overlap without written agreement, cannot accommodate the acceptance and re-submission cycles (15 + 15 Business Day assessments per Deliverable). SoW §4, cl.4.5; Exhibit A cl.5.2, cl.5.4

Order Form promises "ongoing platform operation" services, but no SoW or Schedule defines operational/hosting services scope; SoW 1 covers only the replatforming programme phases. Order Form cl.1.1; SoW §§2, 4

Invoices may be returned unpaid for want of a purchase order number, which conflicts with the fixed payment-day/arrears invoicing obligations and gives no timescale for correcting or re-submitting invoices. Order Form cl.5.3; MSA cl.4.3; Pricing cl.6.1

Exhibit A requires acceptance sign-off by "Customer's Director of Digital Platforms" while the MSA/SoW route acceptance through Customer's single nominated point of contact; the Order Form names both a commercial and a technical contact, contradicting the single-contact requirement. Exhibit A cl.3.1; MSA cl.5.2; SoW cl.6.2; Order Form §4

Exhibit A allows acceptance with Minor Defects outstanding on a mere commitment to a remediation date, which conflicts with the MSA requirement that rejected Deliverables be corrected and resubmitted and with the conformity warranty. Exhibit A cl.4.3; MSA cl.6.3, cl.8.2

Vetting cross-reference is one-way and incomplete: personnel are vetted "in accordance with the Information Security Policy", but that Policy requires criminal-record checks for all personnel with data access without addressing offshore (India) feasibility or evidencing for non-key personnel. Exhibit B cl.5.1; InfoSec cl.8.1; SoW cl.3.4

Key Personnel must be dedicated and not assigned to other engagements, yet Provider may substitute immediately on resignation/absence and non-key staff may be freely reassigned while a minimum team of 11 FTE must be maintained — no mechanism reconciles dedication with the substitution and team-size commitments. Exhibit B cl.1.2, cl.2.4, cl.4.1–4.2; SoW cl.3.1

Exit Plan requires delivery of "all Deliverables, including source code and build scripts" although the MSA preserves Provider ownership of pre-existing tools, methods and know-how with no licence to Customer for continued platform operation after exit. Exit Plan cl.4.1(b); MSA cl.7.2–7.3
unmatched: "Deliverable" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SoW; the Glossary extends it to any output whether or not so identified. This changes the scope of IP assignment, acceptance and warranty. MSA cl.1.3; Glossary §2

Resubmission periods conflict: SoW requires re-submission within 10 Business Days with no further assessment period stated; Exhibit A applies a further 15 Business Day assessment period. SoW cl.6.4; Exhibit A cl.5.4

Response times are self-referential and meaningless: response and resolution are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the response target can never be missed and Provider controls the clock. SLA cl.5.4
Mutual liability cap arguably limits Customer's own obligation to pay the Fees, since it caps "each party's total aggregate liability" with no carve-out for sums due. MSA cl.13.1
Self-defeating cross-reference: the MSA requires Provider to make records available "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 expressly removes all inspection rights. MSA cl.12.2 and cl.10.2

Exit assistance is subject to Customer approval of Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which can block the mandatory exit obligations and the T+15 Business Day first milestone. Exit Plan cl.3.1, cl.3.4, Annex 1 milestone 1

The obligation to keep providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination is inconsistent with the immediate termination right for material breach and with the termination and renewal mechanics elsewhere. Exit Plan cl.2.1–2.2; MSA cl.3.4

Change log retention (duration of the Agreement) is inconsistent with the obligation to hand over the outstanding change log after termination and with the 7-year record retention obligation. Change Control cl.9.3; Exit Plan cl.4.1(e); MSA cl.12.4
Only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, and Customer has no right to require invocation, so continuity protection is entirely at Provider's discretion. BCDR cl.4.1

No key personnel are actually named in any contract document; the SoW refers to "named key personnel" and Exhibit B defers to a non-contractual programme initiation document. SoW cl.3.5; Exhibit B cl.1.1
Volume reporting is required in the "monthly service report", but the SLA's prescribed report content does not include transaction volumes. Pricing cl.5.3; SLA cl.6.2
